source_text: ἐπεκαλεσάμην σε. τότε δὲ οὐ καταισχύνομαι, ἐὰν τὰ τῆς παρακλήσεως ὑπαρχθῇ. ἐπερ · λ̣όγος οὔκ ἐστιν τοῦ σωτῆρος; –ὀξεῖαι μεταβολαὶ τῶν προσώπων γίνονται. οὕτω καὶ ἐν τοῖς προφητι κοῖς πράττει. καὶ ἄλλο περὶ τ̣οῦ ψιλοῦ ἀνθρώπου· οἷον ἕκαστος ἡμῶν πολλάκις διηγούμενος περὶ ἀνθρώπου ὁτὲ μὲν ἀπὸ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτὸν σημαίνομεν ον , ὁτὲ δὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος. ἐὰν λέγω ὅτι καλὸς ἄνθρωπος, "πυράκης", ἵνα ἀπὸ τῆς γραφῆς εἴπω, "μετὰ κάλλους ὀφθαλμῶν", ὑπερμεγέθης, –εἶτα λέγω ὅτι ἐπιστήμων ἄνθρωπος, θεοῦ δοῦλός ἐστιν, ὑπόκειται τῷ κυρίῳ· μὴ γὰρ ἡ μεταβολὴ τῶν λέξεων ἐξ ὅλων ἔξω. ὅταν περὶ συνθέτου λέγηται, αἱ μεταβολαὶ τῶν προσώπων ἐκ μέρους ἐπὶ αὐτὸ μέρος φέρονται. ἐπεὶ τοίνυν καὶ ὁ ταῦτα λέγων οὐ μόνος ἄνθρωπός ἐστιν οὐδὲ μόνος θεός, ἀλλὰ θεὸς ἐνανθρωπήσας, τὰ μὲν ὡς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου λέγεται, τὰ δὲ ὡς ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγου ἢ περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγου. "καὶ ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ἐθεασάμεθα τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ πατρός". ἐπὶ τοῦ αὐτοῦ λαμβάνεις· μὴ γὰρ τοῦτο λέγει· "ἐπίφανον τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἐπὶ τὸν δοῦλόν σου", τὸν ἄλλον ἐμοῦ· ἐμὲ τὸν δοῦλόν σου. 150 18 αἰσχυνθείησαν οἱ ἀσεβεῖς καὶ καταχθείησαν εἰς ᾅδου. τὸ "καταχθείησαν εἰς ᾅδου" πάλιν δύναμίν τινα ἔχει. οὐκ εἶπεν "καταβήτωσαν εἰς ᾅδην". ἑκουσίως δὲ κατιόντων ἐστὶν τὸ καταβῆναί που. οὗτοι δὲ οὐχ ἑκουσίως ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ καταβιβάζονται. ἀμέλει γοῦν καὶ περὶ τῆς Καφαρναοὺ ἢ πρὸς τὴν Καφαρναοὺ λέγεται· "καὶ σύ, Καφαρναού, ἣ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ, ἕως ᾅδου καταβιβασθήσῃ". ὑπὸ ἄλλων καταβιβάζεται. τότε δὲ αἰσχύνονται ὅταν γνῶσιν ὅτι ἀσεβεῖς εἰσιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν ὁρμὴν προθυμίας καταβῆναι εἰς τὸν ᾅδην. διὰ τοῦτο κατάγονται ἵν' ὥσπερ ἔννοιαν λαβόντες ὅπου μέλλουσιν κατιέναι, αἰσχυνθείησαν. ἔτι πλέον κακίσουσιν ἑαυτοὺς ὅτι ἀσεβεῖς γεγόνασιν. 19 ἄλαλα γενηθήτω τὰ χείλη τὰ δόλια τὰ λαλοῦντα κατὰ τοῦ δικαίου ἀνομίαν. οὐκ ἐπαρᾶται αὐτούς· εὐλογεῖ αὐτούς· μὴ γὰρ εἶπεν· "ἄλαλα γενηθήτω τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν". "τὰ δόλια" ὅταν στερηθῶσιν τῶν διαβολικῶν λόγων, ἄλαλα γέγονεν. τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν οὐ καθάπαξ, ἀλλὰ "τὰ δόλια". ἀποβαλόντα τὸν λόγον λοιπὸν σὺν παρρησίᾳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ λαλοῦσιν. οὕτω γοῦν λέγεται· "ἐξολεθρεύσει κύριος πάντα τὰ χείλη τὰ δόλια καὶ γλῶσσαν μεγαλορήμονα". ὅταν ἡ μεγαλορημονοῦσα γλῶττα, τουτέστιν ὁ λόγος, ὀλεθρευθῇ, ἐκεῖνος ἀφ' οὗ ὀλεθρεύεται, τὸν τοῦ θεοῦ λοιπὸν λαλεῖ λόγον. 19 ἐν ὑπερηφανίᾳ καὶ ἐξουδενώσει. ἐπεὶ ἀπαρεμφάτως κεῖται τὸ "τοῦ δικαίου", δύναται καὶ τοῦ δικαίου ἀνθρώπου καὶ τοῦ δικαίου πράγματος, περὶ οὗ λέγεται· "δικαίως τὸ δίκαιον". ὁ λαλῶν δὲ κατὰ τοῦ δικαίου καὶ κατὰ τοῦ ἔχοντος αὐτὸ καὶ πεποιωμένου κατ' αὐτὸυ λαλεῖ ἐν ὑπερηφανίᾳ καὶ ἐξουδενώσει· τότε γὰρ ἄλαλα γίνεται αὐτῶν τὰ χείλη, ὅταν γνῶσιν οἵας ταπεινότητός εἰσιν, ὅταν γνῶσιν ὅτι ὃν ἐξουδενώσουσιν, οὔκ ἐστιν ἄξιος ἐξουθενώσεως. 20 ὡς πολὺ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς χρηστότητός σου, κύριε, ἧς ἔκρυψας τοῖς φοβουμένοις σε. ἐπεὶ ἔδοξέν τινα ἀρατικῶς λέγειν, σκοποῦντες δὲ εἰς τὴν διάθεσιν τοῦ λέγοντος λέγομεν ὅτι οὔκ εἰσιν ἀραί, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον ἐπευχαί. καλὰ δὲ αὐτοῖς ὑπαρχθῆναι βούλεται. ἐπεὶ συνέβαινεν τοὺς μὴ ἀγνο̣ου῀̣ντας τὴν χρηστότητα καὶ τὸ τέλος τῶν σῳζομένων ἐπιτρίβεσθαι, ἔκρυψεν τοῖς φοβουμένοις. φοβουμένους δὲ ὧδε λέγει τοὺς τὸν κολαστικὸν φόβον ἔχοντας, οὐ τοὺς δικαίους, οὐ τοὺς ἔχοντας ἐκεῖνον τὸν φόβον οὗ οὐδέν ἐστιν ὑστέρημα, οὐ τὸν πάντα ὑπερβαλόντα. λέγει ὅτι· ἐπεὶ ἡ χρηςτότης σου συνφυής ἐστιν ἡ αὐτὴ οὖσα τῇ ἀγαθότητί σου, πάντα δὲ ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας τῶν ὅλων ποιεῖς, καὶ τὰ σκυθρωπὰ καὶ τὸ ὑποπεσεῖν τινα ποιῆσαι σκυθρωποῖς, ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ ἤμελλον οἱ ἐπιτριβόμενοι διὰ ἐπιπολαιότητα βλάπτεσθαι, ἔκρυψας αὐτὸ τοῖς φοβουμένοις σε, οὐ
english: I have called upon you. Then I am not ashamed, if the things of the calling exist. For is there not a word of the Savior? Sharp changes of persons occur. So also it is done in the prophets.

And something else concerning the bare man: just as each of us, frequently narrating about a man, sometimes indicates him from the soul, and sometimes from the body. If I say that he is a beautiful man, 'pyrakis'—so that I may speak from the Scripture, 'with beauty of eyes'—[it is] immense; then I say that he is a learned man, a slave of God, he is subject to the Lord; for the change of persons is not outside of all things. When it is spoken concerning a composite, the changes of persons are carried from part to part.

Since, therefore, also the one saying these things is not a man alone, nor is he God alone, but God having become man, the certain things are said as from the man, and the others as from the God Word or concerning the God Word. 'And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father' (John 1:14). You take it upon the same [subject]; for he does not say: 'Let your face shine upon your slave,' the other to me; me, your slave.

The ungodly were shamed and were brought down into Hades. The 'were brought down into Hades' again has a certain power. He did not say 'they descended into Hades.' But for those descending voluntarily, there is the descending. These, however, are not being brought down into Hades voluntarily. Also, concerning Capernaum, it is said: 'And you, Capernaum, which shall be exalted to heaven, shall be brought down to Hades' (Matt 18:17). It is being brought down by others. Then they are ashamed when they know that they are ungodly and do not have the impulse of readiness to descend into Hades. Because of this, they are brought down so that, having received the understanding of where they are about to descend, they might be shamed. Furthermore, they will do even more evil to themselves because they have become ungodly.
Let the lips be without sound.

The deceitful ones speak lawlessness against the righteous. He does not cast them down; rather, he blesses them; for he did not say, 'Let their lips become silent.' The 'deceitful ones' become silent when they are deprived of devilish words. Their lips are not entirely [silenced], but rather 'the deceitful [ones]'. Having cast away the [deceitful] word, they otherwise speak with boldness and truth. Thus it is said: 'The Lord will destroy all deceitful lips and the loud-sounding tongue' (Psalm 12:3). When the loud-sounding tongue—that is, the word—is destroyed, that from which it is destroyed, the person then speaks the remaining word of God.

19 In pride and contempt. Since 'of the righteous' lies absolutely, it can mean both of a righteous man and of a righteous matter, concerning which it is said: 'Rightly the just' (Psalm 115:3). But he who speaks against the righteous and against him who possesses it and is convinced by it, speaks in pride and contempt; for then their lips become silent when they know what kind of lowliness they are, when they know that the one whom they will despise is not worthy of contempt.

20 How great is the multitude of your goodness, Lord, which you have hidden for those who fear you. Since it seemed to someone to speak in a strange way, but looking into the intention of the speaker, we say that they are not curses, but rather blessings. And you wish for them to be found good. Since it happened that those not ignoring the goodness and the end of the saved were being rubbed, you hid it from those who fear you. But he says 'fearing' here to mean those having the punishing fear, not the righteous, nor those having that fear which has no deficiency, nor those surpassing all. He says: since your goodness is inborn with your goodness, and you do all for the salvation of all, and you make the dark things and the falling of someone dark to be dark, but because those being rubbed through carelessness were going to be harmed, you hid it from those who fear you, not...

source_text: τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν· ὧδε γὰρ τὸν φόβον τὸν διαστελλόμενον πρὸς τὴν ἀγάπην λαμβάνομεν–"ἡ τελεία ἀγάπη ἔξω βάλλει τὸν φόβον". τελεία δέ ἐστιν ἀγάπη ὅταν 95 μὴ ἄλλου χάριν αὐτὸ ἀγαπῶμεν. "ἡ τελεία" οὖν "ἀγάπη ἔξω βάλλει τὸν φόβον ὅτι ὁ φόβος κόλασιν ἔχει"–, οὐκ ἐκεῖνον, περὶ οὗ λέγεται· "οὐκ ἔστιν ὑστέρημα τοῖς φοβουμένοις αὐτόν". 20 ἐξειργάσω τοῖς ἐλπίζουσιν ἐπὶ σὲ ἐναντίον τῶν υἱῶν τῶν ἀνθρώπων. ἐξειργάσω ταύτην τὴν κρύψιν. τινές εἰσιν υἱοὶ ἀνθρώπων οὐ ψεγομένων. ψέγονται δὲ πολλάκις οἱ ἄνθρωποι καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ ὅταν λέγῃ ὅτι· "υἱοὶ ἀνθρώπων, ἕως πότε βαρυκάρδιοι"; ὅταν δὲ λέγῃ· "ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐπέβλεψεν κύριος, εἶδεν πάντας τοὺς υἱοὺς τῶν ἀνθρώπων", ἐπαινετοί εἰσιν οὗτοι οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων. καὶ λέγω παράδοξον· ὅταν πρὸς θεὸν ἀναφέρωνται, οἱ δίκαιοι ἄνθρωποί εἰσιν καὶ ἀνθρώπων υἱοί, ὅταν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς δικαίους, οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ υἱοὶ ἀνθρώπων, φαύλων ὄντων ἐκεί151 νων, περὶ ὧν γράφει Παῦλος· "ὅπου γὰρ ἔρις καὶ ζῆλος ἐν ὑμῖν, οὐχὶ ἄνθρωποί ἐστε"; καὶ περὶ ὧν· "ὑμεῖς δὲ δὴ ὡς ἄνθρωποι ἀποθνῄςκετε", ἐκπεσόντες τοῦ θεοὶ εἶναι καὶ υἱοὶ ὑψίστου. πρὸς τοὺς ἁγίους ἀνθρώπους λεγομένους ἢ θεοὺς ὀνομαζομένους υἱοὶ ἀνθρώπων οἱ φαῦλοι λέγονται, πρὸς δὲ τὸν τῷ θεῷ αἴτιον υἱοὺς σπουδαίους, ἐφ' οὓς ἐπιβλέπει. καὶ πάλιν· "ἀνθρώπους καὶ κτήνη σώσεις, κύριε. ὡς ἐπλήθυνας τὸ ἔλεός σου, ὁ θεός· οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐν σκέπῃ τῶν πτερύγων σου ἐλπιοῦσιν". "μέγα ἄνθρωπος καὶ τίμιον ἀνὴρ ἐλεήμων". ὧδε ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ "κατ' εἰκόνα καὶ ὁμοίωσιν" θεοῦ ἐπὶ μεγέθει ἐπαινεῖται. ὅταν δέ τις ἐκπεσὼν τοῦ εἶναι ὑψίστου υἱὸς ἄνθρωπος γένηται υἱός, φαῦλός ἐστιν οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος. "ἐξειργάσω τοῖς ἐλπίζουσιν ἐπὶ σὲ ἐναντίον τῶν υἱῶν τῶν ἀνθρώπων" τῶν σπουδαίων–ἴσασιν δὲ ἐκεῖνοι τὴν ἐξεργασίαν– κρύψιν τοῦ πλούτου τῆς χρηστότητός σου. 21 κατακρύψεις αὐτοὺς ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ τοῦ προσώπου σου. τοὺς υἱοὺς τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἷς ἐξειργάσω τὸν σὸν ἔλεον. κατακρύπτεταί τις δὲ ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ τοῦ θεοῦ οὕτως· ἔχει θεὸς πρόσωπον ἐπιφαινόμενον διὰ τῶν ἑαυτῶν δημιουργημάτων· λέγεται γάρ· "ἐκ μεγέθους καὶ καλλονῆς τῶν κτισμάτων ἀναλόγως ὁ γενεσιουργὸς αὐτῶν θεωρεῖται". ἐξ ἀναλογίας τῆς κτίσεως θεωρεῖται· ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐὰν ἴδῃ τις σκάφος, φαντασίαν ναυπηγοῦ λαμβάνει κἂν μὴ παρῇ, καὶ ὁ θεωρήσας ἰθυνομένην ναῦν πόρρωθεν εὐθέως εἰς ἔννοιαν ἔρχεται ὅτι ἔστιν ὁ πηδαλιουχῶν αὐτήν, καὶ ἅρμα πόρρωθεν ὁ βλέπων τεταγμένως φερόμενον κἂν μὴ ὁρᾷ τὸν ἡνίοχον, ἐνθύμησιν αὐτοῦ λαμβάνει, οὕτω τεταγμένως τοῦ κόσμου ἄρα φερομένου καὶ περικαλλῆ ἔχοντος τὴν φύσιν φαντασία τοῦ κάλλους καὶ τοῦ μεγέθους τοῦ θεοῦ γνωρίζεται· εἰ γὰρ μεγάλα τὰ γενόμενα, πολὺ μείζω ὁ κατασκευάσας. ὅταν τις οὖν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τῆς τάξεως καὶ τῆς ἐννοίας καὶ τῶν κριμάτων τῆς προνοίας φαντασίαν λάβῃ θεοῦ, οὐκ εἰς τὸ ἀπόκρυφον τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ κατεκρύβη. τοιοῦτοι δέ εἰσιν καὶ οἱ παρ' Ἕλλησιν φιλοσοφήσαντες· ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ μεγέθους τῶν δημιουργημάτων καὶ τῆς καλλονῆς φαντασίαν ἔλαβον θεοῦ. ὁ δὲ ἄνευ τῆς δημιουργίας λαμβάνων θεοῦ φαντασίαν ἑωρακὼς τὸν υἱὸν καὶ διὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τὸν πατέρα–"ὁ" γὰρ "ἑωρακὼς ἐμὲ ἑώρακεν τὸν πατέρα"–, οὗτος ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ τοῦ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ κέκρυπται. ἀπόκρυφον δὲ τὸ κατὰ τὸν λόγον τὸν δημιουργικόν. πάλιν ἵνα καὶ δημωδεστέρως εἴπωμεν· δύο πρόσωπα εἶχεν Ἰησοῦς, ἀνθρώπου καὶ θεοῦ. ὅσοι κατὰ σάρκα αὐτὸν γιγνώσκουσιν, ἐν τῇ φανερώσει τοῦ προσώπου αὐτὸν λαμβάνουσιν. ὅσοι δὲ ἀποστάντες ἀπὸ τοῦ κατὰ σάρκα αὐτὸν εἰδέναι ἦλθον εἰς τὸ γιγνώσκειν αὐτὸν καθὸ θεὸς λόγος ἐστίν, οὗτοι κατεκρύβησαν ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ τοῦ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ ἔτι, ἐπειδὴ ἔλεγον τὴν ἔξωθεν φαντασίαν τοῦ κόσμου πρόσωπον εἶναι, ὁ λόγος ὁ καθ' ὃν γέγονεν τὰ γενόμενα καὶ προνοεῖται καὶ διοικεῖται, τὸ ἀπόκρυφόν ἐστιν τοῦ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀπόκρυφον δὲ τὸ κατὰ τὸν λόγον τὸν δημιουργικόν. κρύπτει τὴν ἑαυτοῦ χρηστότητα ὁ θεὸς πολλάκις τοῖς μικροῖς τοῖς φοβουμένοις αὐτόν. ἐξειλήφαμεν δὲ χθὲς τοὺς φοβουμένους τοὺς φόβῳ 96 κολάσεως ἀπεχομένους κακίας, εἴ γε δεῖ ταύτην ἀποχὴν κακίας εἰπεῖν. "ἡ τελεία", φησίν, "ἀγάπη ἔξω βάλλει τὸν φόβον ὅτι ὁ φόβος κόλασιν ἔχει". ὁ σχὼν ἐπιστήμην ἀγαθοῦ καὶ κακοῦ καὶ ποθήσας τὸ ἀγαθὸν καὶ αὐτῷ προσκλιθεὶς ἀπέχεται τοῦ κακοῦ ἔρωτι τῷ πρὸς τὸ ἀγαθόν, 152 ἀφίσταται τοῦ κακοῦ οὐ φόβῳ κολάσεως, ἐκκλίνει ἀπὸ τοῦ κακοῦ. ἐὰν γοῦν λόγος τις πείσῃ αὐτόν, ὅτι οὐκ ἔνι κόλασις, πράττει ὃ αἱρεῖται κακόν. ὁ θεὸς οὖν πολλάκις οὐκ ἐπάγει τὴν τιμωρίαν παραυτὰ χρηστότητι
english: To those who love: for here we receive the fear that is being set aside for the sake of love—'perfect love casts out fear' (1 John 4:18). And love is perfect when we do not love for the sake of another. Therefore, 'perfect love casts out fear because fear has punishment'—not that which is said concerning it: 'it is no loss to those who fear him.'

I have worked for those who hope in you against the sons of men. I have worked this concealment. Some are sons of men who are not reproached. But men and sons are often reproached when it is said: 'Sons of men, how long will you be heavy-hearted?' (Ps 39:13) But when it is said: 'The Lord looked down from heaven, he saw all the sons of men' (Ps 145:5), these sons of men are praised.

And I say a paradox: when they are lifted up toward God, they are righteous men and sons of men; but when they are toward the righteous, the sinners are sons of men, being vile, concerning whom Paul writes: 'For where there is strife and jealousy among you, are you not human?' (Gal 5:20) and concerning whom: 'But you, indeed, as men, are dying' (1 Cor 3:3), having fallen from being the sons of the Most High. Toward the holy men called or named gods, the vile are called sons of men; but toward the sons who are the cause for God, those whom he looks upon, they are diligent.

And again: 'You will save men and cattle, Lord. As you have multiplied your mercy, O God; and the sons of men hope in the shadow of your wings' (Ps 36:7). 'A great man and a precious man is the merciful one.' Here the man who is 'according to the image and likeness' (Gen 1:26) of God is praised in greatness. But when someone, having fallen from being the son of the Most High, becomes a son of man, this man is vile.

'I have worked for those who hope in you against the sons of men'—the diligent ones—and let those know the work: the concealment of the wealth of your goodness. You will hide them in the secrecy of your face, the sons of men for whom I have worked your mercy. And someone is hidden in the secrecy of God thus: God has a face appearing through his own creatures; for it is said: 'Analogously, the Creator is seen from the greatness and beauty of the creatures.' He is seen from the analogy of creation; for just as if someone sees a ship, the imagination of the shipbuilder...

Where is it received even if not present? And he who sees a ship sailing straight from afar immediately comes to the understanding that there is one steering it. And a chariot being carried in order from afar, even if the one seeing does not see the driver, he remembers him. In this way, as the cosmos is being carried in order and having a beautiful nature, a vision of the beauty and greatness of God is known; for if the things created are great, much greater is the Maker.

Therefore, when someone takes a vision of God from the cosmos, the order, the concept, and the judgments of providence, he has not been hidden into the secrecy of His person. Such also are those who have philosophized among the Greeks; for from the greatness of the created things and the beauty, they took a vision of God. But he who, receiving a vision of God without the creation, has seen the Son and through the Son the Father—for 'he who has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9)—this one is hidden in the secrecy of the person of God. And the creative Word is a secret.

Again, so that I may speak more popularly: Jesus had two persons, of man and of God. Those who know Him according to the flesh, receive Him in the manifestation of the person. But those who, turning away from knowing Him according to the flesh, have come to knowing Him as the Divine Word, these have been hidden in the secrecy of the person of God. And furthermore, since we were saying that the outward vision of the cosmos is a person, the Word through whom the things created came to be, and through whom they are provided for and governed, is the secret of the person of God; and the creative Word is a secret.

God often hides His own goodness from the small ones who fear Him. We examined yesterday those who fear, abstaining from evil through the fear of punishment, if it must be called this abstention from evil. 'Perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment' (1 John 4:18). The disposition of knowledge of good and evil, and desiring the good and, having bowed to it, abstaining from evil lust, stays away from evil not by the fear of punishment, but turns away from evil. If, however, some word persuades him that there is no punishment, he practices what he chooses as evil. God, therefore, often does not bring punishment immediately, but [brings] goodness.

source_text: καὶ ἀγαθότητι. κρύπτει δὲ τὸ πλῆθος τοῦ πλούτου τῆς χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ διὰ τοὺς φοβουμένους, διὰ τοὺς μικρούς, διὰ τοὺς φόβῳ κολάσεως ἀπεχομένους τοῦ κακου῀̣. "ὡς πολὺ" οὖν "τὸ πλῆθος τῆς χρηστότητός σου, κύριε". ἔκρυψεν αὐτήν· ἡ γνῶσις γὰρ αὐτῆς ἐποίει αὐτοὺς ἐπιτριβῆναι εἰς τὰ κακά. ὡς ἐάν τις μέχρι τοῦ θαμβῆσαι υἱὸν ἀγανακτήσεως λόγους προφέρῃ καὶ κρύπτῃ τὴν χρηστότη τα καθ' ἣν ποιεῖ τοῦτο ὡς μέλλων τιμωρήσασθαι· εἰ γὰρ γνοὺς ἦν ὁ υἱός, ὅτι μέχρι σχήματός ἐστιν ἡ ἀπειλή, κατεφρόνει τῆς χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπώλλυτο καὶ ἐγίνετο ὑπεύθυνος ὀργῇ. τῷ ὄντι πολλὴ χρηστότης ἐστὶν αὐτοῦ, πολὺ πλῆθός ἐστιν. λέγει γοῦν καὶ ὁ ἀπόστολ̣ος πρός τινας· "ἢ τοῦ πλούτου τῆς χρηστότητος καὶ τῆς ἀνοχῆς καὶ μακροθυμίας αὐτοῦ καταφρονεῖς, ἀγνοῶν ὅτι τὸ χρηστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς μετάνοιάν σε ἄγει"; ὁ δὲ μὴ τοῦτο ἐπιστάμενος οἴεται ὅτι οὐκ ἀπαρέσκεται τ̣οῖς κακοῖς καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἐπεξέρχεται. καὶ Πέτρος δὲ ὁ τῶν ἀποστόλων κορυφαιώτατος γράφων τὴν ἐπιστολὴν καὶ τοιαύτην λέξιν εἴρηκεν· "οὐ βραδύνει κύριος τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἧς τινες βραδύτητα ἡγοῦνται, ἀλλὰ μακροθυμεῖ οὐ βουλόμενός τινας ἀπολέσαι ἀλλὰ πάντας εἰς μετάνοιαν χωρῆσαι". ἰδοὺ ἡ χρηστότητος̣. οὐκ ἔδει τοῖς πολλοῖς αὐτὴν γνωρίμην εἶναι· κατεφρόνησαν γὰρ ἔτι μᾶλλον αὐτῆς. ἔκρυψας οὖν τοῖς φοβουμένοις σε τὸ πλῆθος τῆς χρηστότητός σου. "ἐξειργάσω τοῖς ἐλπίζουσιν ἐπὶ σὲ ἐναντίον τῶν υἱῶν τῶν ἀνθρώπων". οἱ ἐλπίζοντες οἱ καραδοκοῦντές εἰσιν τὰς θείας ἀμοιβὰς καὶ τὰς ἐπαγγελίας ἃς θεὸς ὑπέσχετο τοι῀̣ς εὖ βιοῦσιν ὀρέξαι. "ἐξειργάσω" οὖν τοῦτο "τοῖς ἐλπίζουσιν ἐπὶ σέ". ἐξειργάσω τοῦτο τὸ κρύψαι τὸ πλῆθος τῆς χρηστότητός σου, ἵνα μηδὲ οἱ ἐλπίζοντες ἐπὶ σὲ τοῦτο ἴδωσιν ὅτι διά τινας οὐκ ἐπιφέρεις τὴν ὀργήν. λέγει οὖν ὅτι "ἐναντίον τῶν ἀνθρώπων". οὐκ εἰς ἀεὶ κρύπτεται τὸ πλῆθος τῆς χρηστότητός σου, ἀλλ' ὅσον ἄνθρωποί εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι περὶ ὧν λέγεται· "ὑμεῖς δὲ δὴ ὡς ἄνθρωποι ἀποθνῄςκετε". καί· "ὅπου γὰρ ἔρις καὶ ζῆλος ἐν ὑμῖν, οὐχὶ ἄνθρωποί ἐστε"; ἐναντίον οὖν τούτων τῶν υἱῶν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐξειργάσω τοῦτο τὸ κρύψαι κατὰ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς χρηστότητός σου· καὶ αὐτοῖς γὰρ ἀνοίγει τοῦτο. ὁ θεὸς τῶν ὅλων λέγεται πολλάκις ἄνθρωπος, οὐχ ὅτι ἄνθρωπος γέγονεν ἢ ἄνθρωπός ἐστιν, ἀλλ' ὅτι συνκαταβαίνων τοῖς ἀνθρώποις οὕτω διοικεῖ τὰ κατ' αὐτοὺς καὶ κριτὴς αὐτῶν οὕτω γίνεται ὡς συνπαθὴς ἄνθρωπος. "ἐτροποφόρησέν σε ὡς εἴ τις τροποφορήσει ἄνθρωπος τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ". τοὺς τρόπους σου ἐφο´̣ρ̣ησεν τρέφων σε καὶ διοικῶν. συνᾴδει τούτῳ τό· "ἐὰν ἀνομίας παρατηρήσῃ, κύριε, κύριε, τίς ὑποστήσεται"; καί· "τὰ βλέφαρα αὐτοῦ ἐξετάζει τοὺς υἱοὺς τῶν ἀνθρώπων". βλεφάροις μόνοις ὁρᾷ τὰ πραττόμενα. ὥσπερ οὖν ὁ ἀποστείλας τὸν υἱόν, ὁ εὐδοκήσας τῇ ἐπιδημίᾳ αὐτοῦ, ἀνθρώπους διοικῶν ὡς ἄνθρωπος προσφέρει τὰς ὠφελίας, οὕτω καὶ οὗτος "υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου" ἐστίν· τοῦ οὕτω ἀγομένου ἀνθρώπου υἱός ἐστιν. καὶ ἄλλο δέ· τρόπον τινὰ τὰ καθέκαστα γεννήματά εἰσιν τοῦ καθόλου. ὁ καθόλου δὲ ἄνθρωπος "κατ' εἰκόνα καὶ ὁμοίωσιν" θεοῦ γέγονεν· οὐδὲ γὰρ πάντως περὶ τοῦ Ἀδὰμ τοῦτο μόνου εἴρηται, ἀλλὰ ἡ φύσις ἡ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἡ καθόλου, τὸ εἶδος "κατ' εἰκόνα καὶ ὁμοίωσιν" θεοῦ γέγονεν. ὁ φυ λάττων οὖν τὸ πρωτότυπον, τὸ ὡσανεὶ καθόλου, ἐκεῖνος υἱός ἐστιν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ἡ Ἰησοῦ ψυχὴ ἐφύλαξεν τὸ κατ' εἰκόνα–ἁμαρτίαν γὰρ οὐκ ἔγνω οὐδὲ ἐποίησεν αὐτήν–, κατὰ τοῦτο υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου 97 ἐκείνου λέγεται τοῦ "κατ' εἰκόνα καὶ ὁμοίωσιν" θεοῦ γεγονότος. ῥηθείη καὶ ἄλλως· εἰ καὶ πατέρα οὐκ ἔσχεν Ἰησοῦς κατὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ μητέρα ἔσχεν. καὶ ἡ γυνὴ δὲ ἄνθρωπος. 153 πρὸς ἀναίρεσιν δὲ τῆς δοκήσεως υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου εἴρηται. εἰ καὶ οὐκ ἔχει ἐκ πατρὸς τὸ εἶναι, ἀλλ' ἐκ μητρός ἐστιν. οὕτω γοῦν "γενόμενος ἐκ γυναικὸς" εἴρηται. πάντες ἐξ ἀνδρῶν γίνονται· τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ ὁ Παῦλος γράφει· "ἐξ ἀνδρὸς" γίνεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος, "διὰ γυναικὸς" δέ· ἐκ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς γὰρ ἡ καταβολὴ γίνεται τοῦ σπέρματος, διὰ τῆς γυναικὸς δὲ ἡ μόρφωσις καὶ ἡ ἀπότεξις. ἐπεὶ τοίνυν οὐκ ἔχει οὗτος τὸ ἐξ ἀνδρὸς καὶ τὸ διὰ γυναικός, ἀλλ' ἐκ γυναικός–τὴν ὅλην γὰρ ὕλην ἐκ τῆς γυναικὸς ἔλαβεν, οὐ κατὰ τοὺς ἄλλους ἀνθρώπους· "Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας, ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη ὁ Χριστός". οὐκ εἶπεν "δι' ἧς"–, καὶ κατὰ τοῦτο οὖν "υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου" χρηματίζει· εἰ γα`̣ρ ἁπλῶς ἄνθρωπος ἐλέγετο, ὑπελάμβανον οἱ δοκηταὶ ὅτι πέφηνεν ἄνθρωπος οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρώπου ἔχων γένεσιν ἢ
english: And goodness. He hides the abundance of the wealth of his kindness because of those who fear, because of the small [ones], because of those who refrain from evil through the fear of punishment. 'How much indeed is the abundance of your kindness, Lord' (Ps 52:10). He hid it; for the knowledge of it was making them stumble into evils. If anyone should bring forth words of indignation even unto the point of causing amazement, and hide the kindness as if he were about to punish, if the son had known that the threat is only in form, he would have despised his kindness and would have been lost and become responsible for wrath. In truth, much kindness is his, a great abundance.

For the apostle also says to some: 'Or do you despise the wealth of his kindness, forbearance, and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?' (Rom 2:4). And the one not knowing this thinks that he is not being unyielding to evils, and therefore does not come forward. And Peter, the foremost of the apostles, writes the epistle and has said such words: 'The Lord is not slow concerning the promise, which some count as slowness, but is patient, not wishing anyone to perish but all to come to repentance' (2 Pet 3:9). Behold the kindness. It was not necessary for it to be made known to the many; for they would have despised it even more. You have therefore hidden from those who fear you the abundance of your kindness. 'I have worked for those who hope in you, against the sons of men' (Ps 146:9). Those who hope are those who are watching for the divine rewards and the promises which God promised to those living well. 'I have worked' therefore this, 'for those who hope in you.' I have worked this, to hide the abundance of your kindness, so that even those who hope in you might not see this, that for a certain reason you do not bring forth wrath. He says therefore, 'against men.' The abundance of your kindness is not hidden forever, but only as long as those men are, concerning whom it is said: 'But you, indeed, as men, are dying.' And: 'For where there is strife and jealousy among you, are you not acting as men?' (1 Cor 3:3). Therefore, against these sons of men, I have worked this hiding according to the abundance of your kindness; for to them also he opens this. The God of all things is called many times [human]...

It is not that he has become a man or is a man, but because he descends with men, he governs their affairs in such a way, and as their judge, he becomes like a man who sympathizes. 'He shall nurture him as a man nurtures his son' (Deut 32:6). He observed your ways by nourishing and governing you. This is confirmed by this: 'If he observes iniquity, Lord, Lord, who will stand?' (Ps 139:24), and: 'His eyes examine the sons of men' (Ps 17:24). With eyes alone he sees what is being done.

Just as the one who sent the Son, having approved of his coming, governs men as a man provides benefits, so also this one is a 'son of man'; he is the son of a man who is thus led. And another thing: the particulars are in a certain way the offspring of the general. And the general human has become 'in image and likeness' (Gen 1:26) of God; for this was not said only concerning Adam, but the human nature, the general species, became 'in image and likeness' of God. He who preserves the prototype, the almost-general, is therefore the son of man.

Since, therefore, the soul of Jesus preserved the image—for he neither knew sin nor did it—because of this, he is called the son of that man who became 'in image and likeness' of God. It is also said otherwise: although Jesus did not have a father according to the man, he had a mother. And the woman is a human. To refute the opinion, he is called son of man. Even if he does not have [the status] from a father, he is from a mother. Thus indeed it is said, 'born of a woman' (Gen 3:15). All are born from men; for Paul also writes: man comes 'from a man,' but 'through a woman'; for from the man the casting of the seed happens, but through the woman the formation and the birth. Since therefore this one does not have [the part] from a man and through a woman, but from a woman—for he took the whole matter from the woman, not according to other men—'And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom Christ was born' (Matt 1:16). He did not say 'through whom'—and because of this, therefore, he is designated 'son of man'; for if he were simply called a man, the doubters would have assumed that he had fallen, a man not having origin from a man or...

source_text: ἀρχήν. ἵνα δείξῃ οὖν ὅτι ἐκ τῆς Μαρίας ἐστίν, εἶπεν ἑαυτὸν "υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου". λέγεται δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ θεὸς λόγος ποτὲ ἀνθρώπου υἱός· ὅταν γὰρ λέγῃ· "οὐδεὶς ἀναβέβηκεν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς, ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου", τὸν θε ὸν λόγον κατ̣' αὐτοῦ λέγει. οὕτω δὲ λέγεται υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου, ὡς ἐὰν λέγωμεν πολλάκις τὴν ψυχὴν ἐκ τῶν γονέων. ὡς ἐὰν λέγωμεν ὅτι· "ὁ Ἰακὼβ ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκ τοῦ Ἰσαάχ ἐστιν", οὐ τοῦτο λέγομεν ὅτι ᾗ ποιός ἐστιν καὶ ἅγιος, ἀλλ' οὗτος ᾧ συνέβη ἁγίῳ εἶναι, ἐκ τοῦ Ἰσαάχ ἐστιν. καὶ κατὰ τοῦτο οὖν λεγέσθω υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ὁ θεὸς λόγος. "ἐὰν οὖν ἴδητε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀναβαίνοντα ὅπου ἦν τὸ πρότερον", οὐδὲ τὸ σῶμα λαμβάνομεν, ἵνα μὴ προσκλιθῶμεν τοῖς λέγουσιν οὐρανόθεν αὐτὸν κεκομικέναι σῶμα. σχεδὸν δὲ πάντες οἱ αἱρεθικοὶ τοῦτο λέγουσιν, ὡς Μαρκίων, Βασιλείδης, Βαλεντῖνος. οὕτω δὲ πολλάκις καὶ λέγομεν ὅτι "σοφὸς ἀνήρ, ἅγιος, θεοῦ φίλος", υἱὸς δέ ἐστιν τῆσδε· μὴ γὰρ καθὸ τοιοῦτός ἐστιν, υἱός ἐστιν ἐκείνης. ἐν τοῖς συνθέτοις πολλάκις τὰ τῶν κατὰ μέρος περὶ τοῦ ὅλου λέγομεν· ὡς ἐὰν λέγωμεν "νοήμων ἄνθρωπος, συνετός, μνήμων, ὑγιὴς τὸ σῶμα, εὔμορφος, εὐμεγέθης", τὰ μὲν ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος, τὰ δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ψυχῆς λέγομεν· ἔνια γὰρ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων τῷ συνθέτῳ οὐ δύναται τῶν ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ τῶν ἐν τῇ συνθέσει εἶναι. τὸ μέντοι γρηγορεῖν ἢ καθεύδειν οὐδὲ περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς λέγεται μόνης οὐδὲ περὶ τοῦ σώματος· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἡ ψυχὴ χωρὶς σώματος τοῦτο ποιεῖ οὐδὲ τὸ σῶμα ἄνευ τῆς ψυχῆς. περὶ τοῦ συνθέτου ἄρα λέγεται. "κατακρύψεις αὐτοὺς ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ τοῦ προσώπου σου". ἡ κτίσις τοῦ θεοῦ λέγεται εἶναί ποτε αὐτοῦ πρόσωπον· "ἐκ μεγέθους καλλονῆς τῶν κτισμάτων ἀναλόγως ὁ γενεσιουργὸς θεωρεῖται". οὐκ ἐν τῷ ἀποκρύφῳ αὐτοῦ προσώπῳ εἰσίν, ἀλλ' ἐν τῳ῀̣ προφανεῖ. ἐὰν ἰατρὸν ἴδῃς ἐργαζόμενον, τεχνικῶς ἐπιτελοῦντα, τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὁρᾷς· δείκνυσιν γὰρ τὰ τῆς ἰατρικῆς ἔργα τὸν ἰατρόν. ὅταν δὲ δυνηθῶμεν τὴν ἀναλογίαν τοῦ λόγου τῶν τεχνητῶν ἰδεῖν καὶ τὴν διάθεσιν τοῦ ποιοῦντος, οὐκέτι τὸ φανερὸν αὐτοῦ πρόσωπον ὁρῶμεν, ἀλλὰ τὸ κεκρυμμένον. οὕτω καὶ ἐπὶ θεοῦ λέγομεν ὅτι, ὅτε θεωροῦμεν τὰ δημιουργήματα, ἐκ τῶν δημιουργημάτων καὶ ἐκ τοῦ μεγέθους τοῦ κάλλους αὐτῶν τὸν ὄντα πέλαγος κάλλους καὶ μεγέθους θεόν, ἐν τῷ φανερῷ αὐτοῦ προσώπῳ ἔχομεν τὸν νοῦν. ὅταν δὲ σκοπήσωμεν, διὰ τί, φέρε, οὐρανὸν πεποίηκεν τ̣οι̣ῶσδε καί πως ἔχοντα καὶ διὰ τί τὸ τηνικαῦτα, εἰς τὸ ἀπόκρυφον τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰσήλθαμεν, εἰς τὸν λόγον καθ' ὃν ἐποίησεν. "ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο". ἴδε τὸ ἔξω πρόσωπον. "καὶ ἐθεασάμεθα τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ πατρός". τὸ νοῆσαι ἀπόκρυφόν ἐστιν. τούτῳ οὖν συνφερόμενος καὶ ὁ ἀ154 πόστολος λέγει· "εἰ καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν κατὰ σάρκα Χριστόν, ἀλλὰ νῦν οὐκέτι γιγνώσκομεν". 21 ἀπὸ ταραχῆς ἀνθρώπων σκεπάσεις αὐτοὺς ἐν σκηνῇ, ἀπὸ ἀντιλογίας γλωσσῶν. οἱ ἄρτι ἀπὸ ταραχῆς ἀνθρώπων 98 ῥυόμενοι καὶ ἀπαλλαττόμενοι σκέπονται ἐν προ̣κοπῇ· ὁ γ̣ὰρ ἐκκλίνας ἀπὸ τοῦ κακοῦ ἵνα τὸ ἀγαθὸν ποιήσῃ, οὐχ ἅμα τῇ ἐκκλίσει τῇ ἀπὸ τοῦ κακοῦ τελείως ἔχε̣ι τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐν ἑαυτῷ. γίνεται μαθητὴς τῆς μονοτρόπου γλώττης, τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ γλώττης. λόγους δὲ σημαίνουσιν αἱ γλῶσσαι, καὶ πολλάκις τοῦτο ἀποδέδεικται· "ἐνέτειναν τὴν γλῶτταν αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ τόξον", τὸν λόγον αὐτῶν. καί· "θάνατος καὶ ζωὴ ἐν χειρὶ γλώσσης". οὐκ ἔχει ὅλως χεῖρα ἡ αἰσθητὴ γλῶσσα. ἐνέργ̣ειαν δὲ ἔχει· ὁ λόγος καλούμενος γλῶσσα. 22 εὐλογητὸς κύριος, ὅτι ἐθαυμάστωσεν τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ ἐν π̣όλει περιοχῆς. ἐπιστήσας τοῖς εἰρημένοις καὶ ἐν γνώσει αὐτῶν γεγενημένος λοιπὸν εὐλογίας̣ τρόπῳ χαριστηρίους ἀναπέμπει αἴνους καὶ λέγει· "ἐθαυμάστωσεν τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ ἐν πόλει περιοχῆς". ἔλεγον ὅτι τὸ πλῆθος τῆς χρηστότητος ἑαυτοῦ ἔκρυψεν ἐλέους ἕνεκα ἵνα ἐλεήσῃ. γνοὺς τὴν αἰτίαν τοῦ κεκρύφθαι τὸ πλῆθος τῆς χρηστότητος εὐλογεῖ τὸν τοῦτο πεποιηκότα καὶ λέγει ὅτι "ἐν τῇ πόλει τῆς περιοχῆς" τοῦτο πεποίηκαμεν. δυνάμεθα "πόλιν περιοχῆς" εἰπεῖν τὴν ἐνταῦθα ζωήν, τὴν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ διατριβήν· τρόπον γάρ τινα ὡς ἐν φρουρᾷ περιεχόμεθα. ἐπειδὴ δὲ καὶ ἐν ταῖς Βασιλείαις λέγεται ἡ Σιὼν "πόλις περιοχῆς"–"τίς ἀπάξει με" γὰρ "εἰς πόλιν περιοχῆς"; –, ἐπαινετή ἐστιν αὕτη ἡ περιοχή, φρουρά ἐστιν ἀκαταμάχητος, ἄβλητον ἕρκος. "ἐθαυμάστωσεν" οὖν "τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ πόλει τῆς περιοχῆς". εἴ τις ἔξω τῆς πόλεώς ἐστιν ταύτης, ἀγνοεῖ διὰ τί κρύπτει ὁ θεὸς τὸ πλῆθος τῆς χρηστότητος
english: Beginning. So that he might show that he is from Mary, he called himself 'a son of man'. And even the God Logos is sometimes called a son of a man; for when he says, 'No one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man' (John 3:13), he speaks this against the God Logos. Thus he is called a son of man, just as we often say that the soul is from the parents. Just as we say, 'The holy Jacob is of Isaac', we do not mean that in his nature or essence he is holy, but that he, by whom it happened to be holy, is of Isaac. Therefore, let the God Logos be called a son of man in this way.

If then you see the Son of Man ascending where he was before (Mark 4:13), we do not even take it to mean the body, so that we may not bow down to those who say that he was brought down from heaven as a body. Almost all the heretics say this, such as Marcion, Basilides, and Valentinus. In this same way, we often say, 'A wise man, holy, a friend of God', and he is a son in this respect: not that he is a son according to such a nature, but he is a son of that lineage. In composite things, we often speak of the parts in regard to the whole; just as if we say, 'A man who is intelligent, sensible, mindful, healthy in body, well-formed, and large-statured', we speak of some things from the body and some from the soul; for some of the things belonging to a composite being cannot belong to each of the individual parts in the composition. But to be awake or to sleep is said neither of the soul alone nor of the body alone; for neither does the soul do this apart from this body, nor the body without the soul. Therefore, it is said concerning the composite.

You will hide them in the secret of your face (Psalm 27:5). The creation of God is sometimes said to be his face; 'in proportion to the greatness of the beauty of the creatures, the Creator is perceived'. They are not in his hidden face, but in his manifest one. If you see a physician working, performing skillfully, you see his face; for the works of medicine demonstrate the physician. But when we are able to see the analogy of the word of the skilled ones and the disposition of the one doing the work, we no longer see his manifest face, but the hidden one. So also we say concerning God that, when we contemplate the created things, from the created things and from the greatness of the...

Regarding others, we fix our mind on God, who is a sea of beauty and greatness in His manifest face. But when we observe, why, I ask, has He made the heavens in such a way, and why in this specific manner, so that we might enter into the hiddenness of His face, into the Word through which He made all things? 'The Word became flesh' (John 1:14). Behold the outward face. 'And we beheld His glory, a glory as of the only-begotten from the Father' (John 1:14). To understand this is hidden.

Therefore, the apostle also agrees, saying: 'Even if we have known Christ according to the flesh, but now we no longer know Him' (2 Cor 5:16). You will cover them from the disturbance of men in a tent, and from the contention of tongues. Those who are now being saved and delivered from the disturbance of men are covered in progress; for he who turns away from evil in order to do good does not at the same time as the turning away from evil have the good perfectly within himself. He becomes a disciple of the unique tongue, the tongue of God. For tongues signify words, and this has often been demonstrated: 'They bent their tongue like a bow' (Ps 126:3), their word; and: 'Death and life are in the power of the tongue' (Prov 18:21). The sensory tongue does not have a hand at all. But it has energy, the Word being called a tongue.

Blessed is the Lord, because His mercy has marveled in a city of protection (Ps 116:2). Having understood those who were speaking and having become in their knowledge, He sends back praises in a manner of thanks for the remainder of blessing and says: 'His mercy has marveled in a city of protection' (Ps 116:2). They were saying that He hid the abundance of His kindness for the sake of mercy, in order that He might show mercy. Having known the reason why the abundance of kindness was hidden, he blesses Him who did this and says that 'in the city of protection' we have done this. We are able to call the life there, the sojourn in this world, a 'city of protection'; for in a certain way we are enclosed as if in a fortress. And since in the Kingdoms Zion is also called a 'city of protection'—'who will take me into a city of protection?'—this protection is to be praised; it is an invincible fortress, an unassailable stronghold. Therefore, 'His mercy has marveled in the city of protection' (Ps 116:2). If anyone is outside this city, he is ignorant of why God hides the abundance of His kindness.

source_text: α̣ὐτοῦ. λέγομεν δὲ τοὺς μικροὺς εἶναι τοὺς φόβῳ κολάσεως μὴ πράττοντας τὸ κακόν. ἐπερ · "τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ ἐμοὶ" οὐ κεῖται; –ἀφαιρεῖται τὸ μέγεθος τοῦ ἐλέους τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐὰν προσθῇς τὸ "ἐμοί". καθόλου ἐστίν. ποιοῦμεν ἐνίοτέ τινα. ἐὰν ποιήσωμεν ὅτι σπουδαῖος ἢ ὅτι ἐπιστήμων, οὐκ ἐκείνῳ πεποιήκαμεν μόνῳ, ἀλλὰ παντὶ σπουδαίῳ, παντὶ ἐπιστήμονι. οὐ δεῖ οὖν ἔχειν τὸ "ἐμοί". φίλαυτός τις προσέθηκεν αὐτό. 23 ἐγὼ δὲ εἶπα ἐν τῇ ἐκστάσει μου Ἀπέριμμαι ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν σου. περὶ τῆς προτέρας ἑαυτοῦ περιστάσε̣ως λέγει, ἐν ᾗ ἐζήτει καὶ ἐταράττετο. ἐκστὰς ἐπὶ τῷ μεγέθει τοῦ θαύματος. καὶ ἐκπλαγεὶς ἐπὶ τῇ οἰκ̣ονομίᾳ τῆς κρύψεως τῆς χρηστότητος τοῦ θεοῦ, ἔδοξα ἀπερῖφθαι ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν τοῦ θεοῦ, ὧν ἀπορίπτεται ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ ἀνάξια τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ πράττων. πλὴν οὗτος οὔκ ἐστιν οὕτω κακὸς ὡς ὁ ἰδίᾳ προαιρέσει ἔξω τοῦ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ γινόμενος. ὁ Κάϊν οὖν τοιοῦτος ἦν· "ἐξῆλθεν" γὰρ "Κάϊν ἀπὸ προσώπου κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ". αὐτομόλησεν πρὸς τὸ κακόν, ἀθεότητα ἠσπάσατο, ἀπρονοησίας γέγονεν εἰσηγη̣τής. περὶ μέντοι τοῦ Ἀδὰμ λέγεται ὅτι "ἐξέβαλεν" κύριος. ἐκβάλλεται δὲ ὁ ἐφιέμενος ἔσω εἶναι. οὐκ ἦν δὲ οὕτω κακὸς ὡς ὁ Κάϊν. καὶ οὗτος οὖν ὁ ταῦτα λέγων εἶπεν ὅτι· ἐπειδὴ τοιαῦτα ἐπέστησαν καὶ τοῦ κα̣τ' εἰκόνα τὴν οἰκονομίαν τοῦ κεκρύφθαι τὸ πλῆθος τῆς χρηστότητός σου ἀπὸ τῶν φοβουμένων σε, ἔδοξα ἀπορερῖφθαι ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν σου. δυνατὸν δὲ καὶ οὕτως· ὥσπερ πάντες οἱ τῇ πίστει προσεληλυθότες "σῶμα Χριστοῦ" εἰσιν "καὶ μέλη ἐκ μέρους", οὕτω καὶ τῶν θείων δυνάμεων, τῶν λογικῶν τὸ συνπλήρωμα σῶ155 μα θεοῦ ἐστιν. καὶ ὥσπερ ἐπὶ τῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ μελῶν λέγομεν ὅτι οἱ διορατικοὶ ὀφθαλμοὶ λέγονται, οἱ δὲ πρακτικοὶ χεῖρες, οἱ "τῇ σπουδῇ μὴ ὀκνηροὶ" πόδες–τόδε "οὐ δύναται ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς εἰπεῖν τῇ χειρί· χρείαν σου οὐκ ἔχω", οὐδὲ ἡ χεὶρ δύναται εἰπεῖν· "οὔκ εἰμι ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, ἐπεὶ ὀφθαλμὸς οὔκ εἰμι". καὶ ὅρα γε· μείζ̣ων ἐστὶν ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς τῆς χειρός, καὶ οὐ δύναται οὗτος ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς ὁ διορατικὸς διὰ τὸ σκοπεῖν τὰς οἰκονομίας εἰπεῖν ὅτι· "χρείαν σου οὐκ ἔχω"· οἶδας γὰρ ὅτι ἔχει πρᾶξιν ἡ χεὶρ ἣν ὀφθαλμὸς προηγουμένως ποιεῖν οὐ δύναται. κα̣······ν̣ γοῦν καὶ οἰήσεώς ἐστιν τοῦτο ὅτι ὁ μείζω τῷ ἐλάττονι οὐ δύναται εἰπεῖν· "χρείαν σου οὐκ ἔχω". οἱ διορατικοὶ ἄνδρες ὀφθαλμοί εἰσιν τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ λέγει· ἐπειδὴ ἐπέστησα πράγμασιν καὶ οὐκ ἐνόησα αὐτά, οὔκ εἰμι ὀφθαλμός. 99 εἶπον οὖν τοῦτο ὅτι· τάχα ἔξω τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν τοῦ θεοῦ γέγονα, τῶν διορατικῶν ἀνδρῶν καθορώντων τῇ διανοίᾳ. 23 διὰ τοῦτο εἰσήκουσας τῆς φωνῆς τῆς δεήσεώς μου. διὰ τοῦτο εἰσήκουσας ὅτι ἔγνων· τὸ ὅσον ἧκεν εἰς τὴν ἐμ̣ὴν ἄγνοιαν, ἀπερίφην ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν τοῦ θεοῦ. 24 ἀγαπήσατε τὸν κύριον, πάντες οἱ ὅσιοι αὐτοῦ. ὅσιοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸ πρὸς θεὸν δίκαιον κατορθοῦντες, οἱ τηροῦντες ἐκεῖνο ὃ εἶπεν ὁ σωτήρ· "ἀπόδοτε τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ". "ἀγαπήσατε τὸν κύριον"· σκόπει πρὸς τί εἴρηται τοῦτο· ἀφ' ὧν ἀπεκρύβη τὸ ἔλεος τοῦ θεοῦ, φοβούμενοι ἦσαν. καὶ ἐλάβομεν τὸ τοῦ Ἰωάννου ῥητὸν καὶ ἐσαφηνίσαμεν οὕτως τό· "ἡ τελεία ἀγάπη ἔξω βάλλει τὸν φόβον, ὅτι ὁ φόβος κόλασιν ἔχει, ὁ δὲ φοβούμενος οὐ τετελείωται". ἡ τελεία οὖν ἀγάπη, ὅταν τις ἀγάπῃ τῇ πρὸς τὸ ἀγαθὸν φεύγῃ τὸ κακόν· οὐ διὰ φόβον κολάσεως ἐκτὸς τοῦ κακοῦ μένει, ἀλλ' ὅτι ἔρωτα ἔχει γνήσιον πρὸς τὸ ἀγαθόν. ἀσυνύπαρκτα δέ ἐστιν τὰ ἐναντία. 24 ὅτι ἀληθείας ἐκζητεῖ κύριος. μονογενής ἐστιν ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλήθεια· "ἐγὼ" γάρ "εἰμι ἡ ἀλήθεια", ὁ σωτὴρ λέγει. γίνεται δὲ ἐν τοῖς μετέχουσιν ἀλήθειά τις. καὶ ὥσπερ ἔχει ἐπὶ ἐπιστημῶν καὶ ἀρετῶν –οὐχ ἕκαστον τῶν ἐπιστημόνων λέγομεν πᾶσαν ἔχειν τὴν ἐπιστήμην, ἀλλὰ ἐπιστήμην τινά, τουτέστιν ἄτομον. ὅσοι οὖν ἐὰν ὦσιν οἱ ἐπιστήμονες, τοσαῦται ἄτομοι ἐπιστῆμαί εἰσιν, καὶ ὅσοι ἐὰν ὦσιν
english: His. We say that the small ones are those who do not commit evil for fear of punishment. Does it not stand, 'His mercy [is] to me'? The magnitude of God's mercy is taken away if you add 'to me'. It is general. We make it somewhat particular. If we make it that [it is for] a diligent one or an expert, we have not made it for that one alone, but for every diligent one, for every expert. Therefore, it is not necessary to have 'to me'. Someone self-loving added it.

But I said in my ecstasy, 'I have shrunk away from the presence of your eyes.' Concerning his former state of being he speaks, in which he sought and was troubled. [This is] ecstasy at the magnitude of the wonder. And being amazed at the economy of the concealment of the goodness of God, I thought it had been cast away from the presence of the eyes of God, from whose presence the one unworthy of His presence, practicing [evil], is cast off. However, this one is not as evil as the one becoming [so] by his own will outside the presence of God. Cain, therefore, was such; for 'Cain went out from the presence of the Lord God' (Gen 4:16). He consented to evil, embraced ungodliness, and became an advocate of thoughtlessness. Concerning Adam, however, it is said that the Lord 'drove out' (Gen 3:24). But he who strives to be inside is driven out. And he was not as evil as Cain.

And he who says these things said: since such things happened, and according to the image, the economy of the concealment of the abundance of your goodness from those fearing you, I thought it had been cast away from the presence of your eyes. And it is possible even thus: just as all those having come by faith are 'the body of Christ' and 'members in part' (1 Cor 12:27), so also of the divine powers, the fullness of the rational [powers] is the body of God. And just as concerning the members of Christ we say that the discerning eyes are called, and the practical hands, and the feet 'not slothful in diligence'—this is 'the eye cannot say to the hand, I have no need of you' (Mark 7:42), nor can the hand say, 'not...

"I am from the body, because I am not an eye." And behold: the eye of the hand is greater, and this discerning eye is not able to observe the economies to say, "I have no need of you"; for you know that the hand has a practice which the eye previously could not do. For indeed it is like this, that the greater cannot say to the less, "I have no need of you." Discerning men are eyes of God. And he says: because I have come upon things and did not perceive them, I am not an eye. I have therefore said this: perhaps I have become outside the eyes of God, the discerning men who see with the intellect.

Because of this, you have heard the voice of my prayer. Because of this, you have heard that I have known how far I had fallen from the eyes of God. Love the Lord, all his holy ones. The holy ones are those who make right what is just toward God, those who keep that which the Savior said: "Render to God the things of God" (Matt 22:21). "Love the Lord"; observe toward what this is said: from which the mercy of God was hidden, they were fearing. And we took the explicit word of John and clarified it thus: "Perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment, but the one fearing is not perfected" (1 John 4:18). Perfect love, therefore, is when someone, loving toward the good, flees from the evil; not because of the fear of punishment does he remain away from evil, but because he has a genuine passion toward the good. And the opposites are incompatible.

For the Lord seeks truth. The truth of God is unique; for "I am the truth," the Savior says (John 14:6). And a certain truth comes to be in those who participate. And just as it is regarding knowledges and virtues—we do not say of each of the knowledgeable ones that he possesses all knowledge, but a certain knowledge, that is, a particular one. So whoever the knowledgeable ones may be, so many particular knowledges they are, and whoever they may be...

english: Those participating in the truth are as many truths as there are participants. I say these things before the end, for there will not be many truths, nor many people who are true, nor many experts, nor many knowings at the end; because if from the believing ones there comes 'one heart and one soul' (1 Sam 18:1) and 'being completed in the same mind and the same judgment' (Phil 2:2)—even if not from all, but rather according to a certain measure—at the final desired end, there will be no difference between one expert and another.

Just as, even if by hypothesis all doctors possessed medicine in an unsurpassed way in all its parts, there were not many doctors; there were many men, but not many doctors. Since therefore the truth is one—for 'grace and truth' (John 1:17) come 'through Jesus Christ'—one truth becomes through itself, not truths as individuals through it. They become through the one, just as partial virtues become through the universal and individual knowings through the universal.

Therefore the Lord seeks these; so strive as far as you are able to receive some truth, for God seeks these. Even if you receive [truth] regarding practical virtues, the truth of practical virtues is judged from the disposition, if one participates in justice through that very thing. Since 'let the righteous pursue justice rightly' (Ps 33:5), pursue that very justice rightly, pursue the practice of the righteous with a disposition of righteousness.

'Love the Lord, all you his saints' (Ps 5:7). He gave a reason; since 'the Lord seeks truth', 'love the Lord', the provider of truths. Thus we also hear righteousness being spoken of in the plural: 'The Lord is righteous and he loved righteousness' (Ps 116:15). But when he speaks concerning universal righteousness, the essence, 'righteousness descended from heaven' (Ps 11:7), he calls the Savior righteousness here. And just as it has become to us as wisdom, so also righteousness.

And they repay those who practice pride excessively. Since he showed the smallness of those who fear, for he also said there are men who trouble them, certain sophists and deceivers, he called these proud. But they practice pride excessively. And it is possible even thus: all evil becomes superfluous instead of being in vain. This indeed is also said in Proverbs: 'Do not love...'

against a man in vain; for even one hating a friend cannot do anything to him, unless God gives it. Therefore he does this in vain. And it is not necessary to strive for vain things. And these therefore the proud do pridefully in excess; for not all those of whom they boast will be subordinates to them, unless God gives it.

Be men, and let your heart be strong, all you who hope in the Lord (Psalm 31:6). Having said this, he anoints all the struggles for endurance, for manliness. And he does not speak of those who fear, but of those who hope. And we say that these are those working for the good of the promises with desire. These therefore are ready to become manly and to be strengthened and to draw near to God. And each one, clinging to Him, becomes one spirit with Him. And if each one of those clinging to the Lord becomes one with Him, when many are the ones clinging to Him, by a way of communion all become one spirit.

To David: of understanding. Blessed are those whose lawlessnesses have been forgiven (Psalm 32:1). The forgiveness of sins is a new genesis, a genesis upon genesis. Because of this it is called regeneration. Just as the repetition denotes song upon song, so also the regeneration is another genesis being added upon a genesis that has arrived. It was necessary, therefore, for the psalm concerning regeneration to have certain virtues in number. And from the fourth square, five times five takes an addition and receives the first of the perfect ones, the six; for the first of the perfect ones, having been added to the fourth of the squares, makes thirty-one. The five times five is a square. A square is that which is equal. These therefore, the numbers having been set forth, have become suitable to the regeneration; for it is necessary to have its constitution from a perfect number and from a square because of stability. The former genesis became corrupt. The first-formed ones turned away from perfect virtue and from the keeping of the divine commandment which they had received from God. It was necessary, therefore, for the second genesis to be more stable. The stable one has [its quality] from the square; it has the perfect one from the six, in the number being composed and partitioned from its own parts. And this must be said: even if the twenty-five is a square, it has its imperfection from sensible things; for the sensible things [are] five...

english: the visible, the audible, the tasted, the smelled, the touched

to be among those being instructed. And since it seemed regarding him to be himself the teacher, it is necessary for the teacher to be helped by the students; having hidden it, he says: 'May God give you understanding in all things.' Therefore understanding is manifold; the word is homonymous, and it has many meanings.

And since he speaks about hidden things here, there lies that which is according to knowledge, that which is kindred to wisdom; for the psalm contains mysteries. And this must be said: it is impossible to understand grammatical words if one does not have understanding of letters, and it is not possible to understand the arguments of philosophers unless one has knowledge of their previously proposed thesis. So also the things of God are impossible to understand without divine understanding.

And why is it that grace is given to David alone, or the understanding is said to be from David? Observe that characteristics are known both from the giver and from the receiver, knowing them. For instance, even the Holy Spirit in the Scripture is called at times Elijah and at times John. Likewise also the Gospel is called at times of God, as of God giving and arranging it: 'set apart' for 'the gospel of God'; and at times from the one ministering it: for 'according to' 'my gospel'; and of those preaching, it is sometimes said they have received the gospel, and at times it is said as having been released: 'repent and believe in the gospel.' Such names, when they mean the same both with and without an addition—with a divine addition and without this, as I said, simply gospel and gospel of God—are the same. Therefore it is the same to say simply gospel and gospel of God. Thus, understanding is from the giving God, and from the prophet and his psalmist who received it, the understanding is said to be.

Blessed are they whose lawlessnesses have been forgiven, and whose sins have been covered (Psalm 32:1). Sin differs from lawlessness. Lawlessness is the sinful practice of one not having law; for the transgressor of law is called lawless. 'Lawlessness reproaches a man' (1 John 3:4). english: "Sin is lawlessness." If, therefore, one has sinned, he has in a certain way lawlessness; but he speaks of two things. For by a connective conjunction, he has shown that there are two. Then: "and sin is lawlessness." Sin is a genus of lawlessness; for he was saying that lawlessness is a species, when the one doing evil does not have law. And this is also called sin: the transgression or violation of the law, which I called lawlessness. It is like saying: "everyone having a horse has an animal"; the animal is a genus. Not everyone having an animal has a horse, but he having a horse has an animal. He who has the species has the genus. Thus also here he speaks, as if he were speaking of the same lawlessness and sin. But in thought there is a difference, because one is general and the other is in part; one is genus and the other is species; for he said that the name of sin lies both against transgression and against lawlessness.

Therefore both kinds sin: "for as many as sinned lawlessly" (Ps 51:2). Behold, these who are without law, they sin. "And as many as sinned in law": these are those having wisdom, having transgressions of the law. Both "sinned." But the forgiveness of lawlessness happens when the divine law, the spiritual one, the one "turning back souls," holds the lawless ones. Then the lawlessnesses are forgiven. And I say thus, the forgiveness of sins does not happen immediately. Jesus forgives if he says: "the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins" (Matt 9:6). And: "Child, your sins are forgiven" (Mark 2:5); for he does not say: "Behold, your sins have been forgiven I." He has given a power that is making new. And the energy having come to pass destroyed the evil. Therefore those whose sins were forgiven are blessed. Consequently, they return to the blameless law of God which turns back souls.

Thus the forgiveness of sins happens when the divine law according to the gospel comes; for this is the "spiritual law" by which souls are turned back, as I said. And those sins which come to pass through transgression of the law and are added, have a covering. The sins are covered. But it is impossible for those baptized once to again find the bath. They are covered through works of repentance. But you say that the sins, having been covered, are saved. Not "love," he says, "but...

Does it [love] remove a multitude of sins? For it does not utterly annihilate sins, but in another way; for he who performs works of love performs them. For no one who shows love toward a neighbor speaks against him, insults him, or acts unjustly. But when he does this, he lacks love toward him.

All these things are examined not as being currently active, not because they are hidden as if they were destined, but because the arriving love has hidden those things, that is, it has departed from them, it has cast them out. And if one must speak briefly, the arriving love stops the sin in its active state, leaving the potential for sin remaining. If anything is examined, it is the activity; for example, the repentant robber had sin in activity; he had repentance; the Savior gave him remission; the activities according to which he had lived were cast away. But the potentials remain, and they are examined.

For one must not pay attention to those who say that evil is a deprivation. There are some, and indeed a whole heresy of the Stoics, saying this: 'It is impossible for one who has cast away virtue to take it up again.' Just as it is impossible for one who has lost sensation to take it back, and therefore through this blindness and deafness are a deprivation, so they reason concerning virtue. But to us, who are simpler, and rather more unlearned, they say that there is no longer such a thing; for they say that there is no repentance after these things, no taking up of virtue again, but the evil remains for ever and brings appropriate punishment.

Therefore, sins are examined in the way I have said; they pass into potentiality; for it is blessed to have the potential for evil. Opposites do not coexist. He who has virtue in activity has the potential for evil, and this is a blessed thing. Therefore, one must not have virtue in potential, but in activity. For this reason also, God from the beginning, having made man 'in image and likeness' (Gen 1:26) of himself and 'upright,' just as the good was in potential, immediately also gave a law to prevent sin, so that sin might always remain in potential.

english: "circumcision and uncircumcision." He received law in that word of the speaker, according to the good law. The Gentiles are lawless; for "law" means "those not having law to themselves." But when they were called to the true [law], not according to the common concept, they are no longer lawless. The blessing may be for both kinds of lawless: the Gentiles, or the Jews who have sin concealed. But they had law earlier, so that the distinction of circumcision toward uncircumcision occurs.

This existed before the gospel when the human race was divided into two kinds of men, circumcised and uncircumcised. But when our Lord pleased to come, he joined both ranks into one new man, having created [him]. The new [man] is not a Gentile, the new [man] is not from circumcision, but one new just as one man had become in the beginning; for there was no difference of circumcision and uncircumcision then.

Just as the one from circumcision and the Greek are created into one new man through repentance, through the knowing of the former conduct—and the former conduct before the law is evangelical. If ever Greeks mock saying, "Christianity was brought into the midst only recently; but we were earlier," we show that before Moses, and before idols were brought into the midst and the making of idols, the polity of men is such as Christians now have, living according to practical and intellectual virtue.

Into that one man therefore he created, and a new one he has made him, a new [man] not a different [one], but a new [man] being set apart from the old. When a succession of commandments occurs, that old one becomes old, as we have often said that the coming law makes the former old. So also the [law] of the Jews according to the shadow is old, since it was received from the gospel. Since [it is] non-successive...

Which is the Gospel—even if heaven and earth pass away, the words of Jesus remain (Matt 24:35)—for this reason it is called a new covenant, because it is non-successive. Thus, the life of the lawless and of the sinners has also been inherited; for the lawlessness of the former has been forgiven, and the sins of the latter have been covered up, and moreover, he has become a man. He no longer speaks concerning a lawless person or a sinner, and he says: 'Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin' (Ps 32:2). Pay attention to what they were saying: sin is a kind of lawlessness.

It can also be referred to the 'underscoring' of the saved ones, the Lord's man I say. Blessed is this one; for sin is not imputed to him, for he did not know it nor did he do it. 'Nor is there deceit in his mouth.' The one 'speaking truth in his heart' according to the psalm that says this: 'Walking blamelessly and working righteousness, speaking truth in his heart' (Ps 15:2), the one speaking truth in his heart does not have deceit in his mouth, he does not have a deceitful word. And it is good also to say: 'Nor is there deceit in his mouth.'

Some do not have deceit in their mouth, but they have it in their heart; for 'your heart' is said to someone, is 'full of deceit.' And toward Elymas the magician the apostle said: 'O full of all deceit' (Acts 13:10). Therefore, it is a great thing not to have deceit in the mouth when the heart does not have deceit; for a cunning person can say all such things as to seem to have no deceit. And I say: no one has deceit in the mouth like the sophists; I do not mean the teachers of rhetoric, but the sophistical ones who are false with their sophisms. A sophism is a falsehood; even if it were ever known to be from true premises, the conclusion is a falsehood.

english: But the phrase 'my bones have grown old' has been placed erroneously thus: 'because I was silent,' these things, the 'my bones have grown old from crying out all day long.' Not 'my bones have grown worn out from crying out all day long,' but 'because I was silent from crying out all day long'; for before this they had the day which 'the sun of righteousness' (Mal 4:2) makes. And he was crying out, this indeed praying, and that indeed glorifying God who grants me the day. Since therefore I was silent from crying out all day long, my bones have grown worn out.

It has been said to us also before that 'bones' refers to the vigorous powers of the soul and the doctrines of piety. Just as these bones hold together the whole body—for from them even the veins and everything is suspended. It is therefore said: 'All my bones shall say, Lord, who is like you?' (Ps 145:17); not that these bones have sensation or intellect. For they do not feel themselves when being ground. Therefore 'my bones have grown old' was received. When it was united to God, then it cried out all day long. But since silence received the cry, my bones have grown worn out.

And I have already said that the unceasing one saw all the sons of men (Ps 32:13), having been cast as 'to the foolish beasts' (Ps 104:25). These, therefore, he saw, the sons of men, from his ready dwelling-place (Ps 104:26). His dwelling-place is like his temple, the state of his being... his throne. This throne is ready and a dwelling-place... 'Your throne is ready from of old, and you are from the age' (Ps 102:25). The ready... about him as a king. And of his throne we take up the thought... it comes, and thus hearing of his temple, we receive him as ready along with it... as if manifesting the state of God, the majesty of God. A soul which does not... his dwelling-place is ready. And this is also possible; one becomes ready from the same participation to make room for God's presence; holiness is briefly produced in the one having it; for that one begins to progress... taking the participation.

A dwelling-place of God is not ready; rather, through progress, something small becomes great as it is measured by its being, and it becomes ready. It is said that the good thing itself is ready, as if one says, 'My heart is ready, O God'; for he who has a prepared heart is a temple of God, a ready dwelling-place for Him. And again: 'Has it not been announced to you, O man, what is good' (Micah 6:8) and what is pleasant, 'but to do justice and to love mercy and to be ready to walk with your Lord God'? And again: 'Pay attention with your ear to the preparation of their heart' (Psalm 103:5).

He looked upon all who dwell in the earth (Psalm 36:6). Others are those dwelling in the earth, apart from the sons of men; for those who have not kept the image, nor have become [earthly], dwell. But the sons of this kind of men do not dwell, but they reside. For He 'causes the sun to rise' (Matthew 5:45) as it is 'upon the good,' and so also 'upon the evil,' He surveys all the sons of men, and those dwelling [in the earth], even irrational animals; for He gives 'food to all flesh' (Psalm 145:16). He flies into a snare; for we do not say the sons of men and those dwelling in the earth are parallel [terms].

He who formed [man] alone [formed] their hearts. In the Scripture, the doing is distinguished from the fashioning; for God made man 'according to His image and likeness' (Genesis 1:26), but He formed the man from the 'dust from the ground' (Genesis 2:7). And Job indeed says both these things: 'Your hands have formed me and made me' (Job 10:8). If he says this word strictly, the inner man becomes [the result], but the outer is fashioned. And as it has been said: 'Remember that you formed me of clay' (Job 10:9). The verb of forming implies a difference; for the one doing is able and will desire to bring into being as parents bring into existence. In the previously read passages, we say that 'to become' differs from 'to be created'; just as to form is not entirely [the same] as itself. Listen then to what he says...

english: He says that the hearts were formed by God in all ways, but 'only alone'. The hearts were formed 'only alone' to join heart to heart in companionship.

They certainly differ, and though many possess them, they possess them with some difference. This indeed is also said in Proverbs: 'Just as faces are not alike to faces, so also the hearts of men' are not alike (Proverbs 27:19). It is therefore difficult to find two similar faces. Even if the myth of Polydeuces and Castor is told, it stands only as a myth. They say the hemispheres are signified by these two names. Therefore they say day by day, living in parts; for the hemispheres are thus: when one semicircle becomes under the earth, the other becomes over the earth, because the semicircles are dissimilar in their likeness. If indeed you cut a circle in the middle, the semicircles are dissimilar. Let that be a myth to me.

But let us grant that such men have also come to be. It is therefore difficult to join face to face in likeness. 'Just as faces are not alike to faces, so also the hearts of men' are not alike (Proverbs 27:19). For indeed 'no one knew the things of man except the spirit of the man which is in him' (1 Corinthians 2:11). If no one knew the things of man except the spirit in him, the things of men have been formed by God individually, each one.

Having formed there a kind of mixture, for he said that they do not fall to the more sensory [understanding], just as a potter forms clay, the hearts, he knows all their works; for since one knows works in a certain way, if from the [works] themselves. We also say at other times that one who understands mechanical works is able to judge whether the parts of the clock are well or not. And upon an image, therefore, heart does not join to heart. Therefore he alone is called 'the knower of hearts of all' according to the prayer sent up by the apostles, when the disciples were making a selection. No one else is able to [know] the heart of...

[A man to] see. Therefore, one cannot separate heart from heart. And Job says, 'He who understands the mind of men' (Job 33:32). Even if another stood by... this [is] of God. He alone shapes the hearts. Each heart... the name of the shaping does not mean the creation of the heart... and indeed the elders, receiving its right which he... have said, 'Good is the shaping of your heart.' They do not say the essence of the heart is good, but the shaping, by which he skillfully worked. Toward the beautiful, he says, it has become... and it is possible to say by a second sense that the 'shaping of the heart' is then good, when it is protected from wickedness or ignorance, as it was in the beginning.

The man having become 'in the image and likeness' (Gen 1:26) of God is not said to have been shaped, but to have been made. But the man having become from clay and matter is said to be a shaping of God: 'Remember that you formed me of clay' (Job 10:9). And concerning both of the active powers of God it is said, 'Your hands shaped me and made me' (Ps 138:7). To fashion the heart... is a shaping of the heart, not to sustain it. So that you may know: the first making of our hearts had no difference; therefore it was not said then that each heart was shaped alone. There was no difference from the others. Here this is said after the subtext.

Regarding: 'one heart and one soul' (Acts 4:32) of the disciples? According to this, 'of those believing' according to being of one mind; for we do not take the whole from all. Regarding: so will the shaping ever cease? —the shaping alone, since this also took a beginning from us. And it took the beginning from us and an end it will reach, when it becomes—just as the Father and the Son are one (John 17:21), so all rational things are. I want it to be in this: 'that just as I and you are one, Father, so may we all be one' (John 17:21). Regarding: does making differ from creation? —it differs. To make signifies bringing into being from non-being, not to fashion; and for some, the name of creation also denotes the adornment of that which has become. The name of creation suffices even for the soulless: 'making...'

english: “[He is] peace and one who creates [new things out of] evils.” And according to what is at hand, we say this: He proves to be a providential one over all things, and he gives peace to them and creates [new things out of] the evils. And in another way the expression was made clear to us thus: he creates evils as if it were an unclean creation, so that it might no longer be unclean; he creates, so that it might become pure, and he creates the two into one new man within him. He creates evils so that they might no longer be evils; for example, he creates evil men so that they might no longer be evil.

Question: regarding the quality? —the quality in the sense of being like it; “for we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works” (Eph 2:10). Regarding the workmanship, he has not said “for good works,” but rather for the sake of being. But they are created “for good works,” so that they might do good works. Question: so that the formation is from the quality? —in such a way as is possible; for the essence was formed from the heart. And the heart is the mind.

And the name of creation is extended even to the sensible things: “and having created the world out of formless matter.” Question: regarding the rational [things] by analogy? —yes, regarding the rational in general. An extension is also found regarding the irrational souls, [the one] understanding all their works. He understands the works, because he knows the heart, and the beginnings of the happening works are taken from perception.

Among us, many receive men from what is within them; and those becoming imitators of God do so for no other reason than that “it is more blessed to give than to receive” (Acts 20:35); for giving is like God, but receiving is not; for each of those receiving is a recipient of something. But being a recipient is a deficiency, and that is to say, the saying that it is good “to give rather than to receive.”

Again: “blessed are the merciful, for they shall receive mercy” (Matt 5:7). There is a certain lesser progress here; for in order to receive mercy, one must show mercy. Another, out of compassion, shows mercy, fearing that a man being so might fall into such [states]. Thus also Christians, out of compassion, nourish those in prison. Others again, having seen someone sometimes struck by disease, pity him because he has become ill. And again others do this even for the sake of the pursuit of glory, so that they might be glorified. But each of these, not being perfect, receives the more and the less; for the perfect is only that which does not [seek]...
more and less

english: Everything comes to an end. And a great giant will not be saved by the abundance of his own strength. This also contains a history: Goliath was a great giant and had an abundance of strength, and he believed in nothing other than in his own luck and his own strength and greatness. And he was also arrogant; therefore he was not saved; for he, having armed himself in the 'name of the Lord' (1 Sam 17:45), was defeated and brought down. And we find many in the Scriptures being cast down great, because they cast great confidence upon themselves.

The Amalekite was prepared for war and seemed to be stronger than Israel; for Israel was not fully prepared for military matters, and yet, as the hands of Moses were being lifted up, the Amalekite was being subdued and humbled, and the lifting of the hands was happening to him, and he was not saved because of his own strength. We say again: if anyone, having a god-fighter's attitude, 'building up lofty things against the knowledge of God,' falls by the strength which he had and is swallowed up, he is by no means saved. Sometimes the God-wise one contends with him and casts him down from where he has conceit.

A false horse for salvation. Again, many think greatly upon a horse, but the God-Word shows that even the conceit of horses is easily broken; for 'these are in chariots and these in horses, but we in the name of the Lord our God shall be magnified' (Ps 20:7). See, 'a false horse for salvation.' To many it was promised that Pharaoh would capture the Hebrews with horses. But they did not even possess one horse, and their salvation has become false, having sinned and having failed. And also in Proverbs: 'A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but salvation is by the Lord' (Prov 21:31). You see that it is false for salvation, if this does not exist from the Lord, even if it is according to a spoken word.

And for thought: it is often said that the body is a horse of the soul, and the soul is the rider or the one mounting it; 'I will strike,' he says, 'the whole horse in frenzy and its rider in madness.' When anyone carries...

When one, enjoying pleasures upon the body and fulfilling his own desire, receives a foolishness, then salvation occurs. A horse is trodden down by God in frenzy, becoming outside of itself; for indeed, being subdued and led away as a slave, it no longer moves according to its own impulses, but stands out from these.
Barhesanes lived in former times, in the days of Antoninus the Roman king. He was at the beginning of the school of Valentinus, moved into the church, and became a presbyter.

17 And in the multitude of his power he shall not be saved. That is, either the one using horses or the power of many horses; for both are true: 'a false horse for salvation,' even if it be many; for it is not upon one horse alone. Often the whole cavalry is a horse. That is, therefore, the multitude of the power of the cavalry used by the riders does not save him, nor the multitude and power of the horses.

18 Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him (Ps 33:18). It is equal to: 'the eyes of the Lord upon the righteous' (Ps 34:8). And this again in the twelfth psalm says: 'Look, hear my prayer, O Lord my God' (Ps 12:2). Therefore, 'the eyes of the Lord upon those who fear him' is not [a fear] of passivity, but 'him'; for there is also a passive fear, which perfect love casts out from those having the fear of God. There is fearing and fearing God; for the fear toward God is not passive, but signifies the surpassing of all. Thus indeed it says: 'the fear of the Lord surpassed all' (Ps 111:10), and: 'there is no deficiency to those fearing him' (Ps 112:7). Being righteous, they are worthy of being watched over by God.

18 Those hoping in his mercy. Behold, those fearing God hope in his mercy; for having done all things, they expect to be shown mercy by him, as it was said a little earlier: 'not of him who wills nor of him who runs, but of the God who shows mercy' (Rom 9:16). And no one is able to keep himself unblemished.

λέγει πάντα, ἵνα ἕκαστος πρὸς ἑαυτὸν τὸ βοήθημα λάβῃ. οὕτω γοῦν αἰτιᾶται αὐτοὺς καὶ περὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν σφαλλομένους καὶ περὶ τῶν χαρισμάτων καὶ περὶ εἰδωλόθυτα κεχηνότας.
english: To guard a city, whether it be the body or the soul, is impossible unless God co-guards it. 'Those hoping in his mercy' [Ps 33:18]; he has mercy on those fearing him, to rescue their souls from death. For this reason, 'his eyes' are 'upon those fearing him' [Ps 33:18-19] and 'those hoping in his mercy', so that he may rescue 'their souls from death' [Ps 33:19]. Death here we do not take to be the common death which the pious and the impious, the righteous and the unjust, all undergo, but it is a death of the soul which consumes the soul from the blessed life.

From this death we are turned away to avoid it; concerning this it is said: 'this soul that sins shall die' [Ezek 18:4]. And again: 'sin, when completed, brings forth death' [Gal 6:8]. And since this death follows sins, God, giving the forgiveness of sins, will rescue those who have received [grace] beforehand from the following death. And he will nourish them in famine, those fearing him and hoping in his mercy. Just as he rescues souls from death, so also he nourishes them in famine.

Indeed, such things have happened many times in history. He nourished the people of the Hebrews during a long journey in the wilderness, providing manna every day by himself. And you will find this in various instances: for example, Elijah was nourished by the widow and by the angel shown to him through bread and the jar of water. And also, while Jezebel was persecuting Elijah and all the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah, the commander of the household of King Ahab, nourished fifty men in two caves, God having prepared him for this. Indeed, he said this without neglect to Elijah when he met him: 'and your servant fearing the Lord' [1 Kings 18:3]. And he who feared the Lord nourished them because of the Lord.

If, therefore, he has restorations—these other things have happened according to history—he again nourishes those fearing his fear and hoping in his mercy, providing for them the bread of life, descending from heaven, which partakes of his flesh as 'true food' [John 6:51]. Being the savior of all, he holds them. He does not do this by a single means, but according to the circumstances: he saves in wars from external enemies, making them [victorious] and not allowing them to fall into captivity, he saves...

He saves those who are doing badly, like a pilot when we are tossed by storms in the sea of life. Furthermore, he gives to each one a spring—in which is 'a spring unto eternal life' (John 4:14)—and he is nourished even when having become in a waterless place. And, 'open your eyes and be filled with bread' (Isa 58:11).

The one having opened the eyes of the soul and having been filled by the manner of chewing the bread of the divine logos does not suffer from famine; for 'the Lord will not let the soul of the righteous starve' (Ps 34:9). Whoever is in desire for bread but is not opening his eyes to his own bread, lives in famine; for the soul has many foods from God within itself.

Our soul waits upon the Lord. This is what is said: since we have known these things, that the eyes of the Lord are watching those who fear him (Ps 33:18)—even if they have at some time been in death, he rescued them; even if they have at some time been in famine, he nourished them; even if we should at some time be in any lack, we wait knowing that we too shall enjoy these things; and our soul, if it should be in death, shall be saved. For he is a helper and a defender of us.

You see that a remainder has become a multitude: 'the Lord looked down from heaven, he saw all the sons of men' (Ps 147:9). If at any time something is being said discordantly and oppositely, observe if these things are being said about one single thing; for then an opposition occurs. But if it is being said about a church or a city or a house, they are not opposites; for the things concerning the one are said, and the things concerning the other are said.

And this you ought to know: that the saints do not offer up their prayers and thanksgivings concerning themselves alone, but concerning all things which they consider. It is not the same to say one thing that must harmonize with one, and a multitude, such as a people or a nation or a city. It is impossible for the same thing to be at once good and bad, or temperate and intemperate.

And the apostle writes to the Corinthians that they have become rich 'in every word and in all knowledge' (1 Cor 1:5). Does he not say again, 'fornication is heard among you' (1 Cor 5:1)? If he were saying these things toward one person, it would be discordant. But since the whole church is being addressed, and such and such are in the collections, he says all things, so that each one may receive help for himself. In this way, too, he charges them concerning those erring about the resurrection, and concerning the gifts, and concerning those having become idolaters.
