english: The subject at hand is: 'Many are the lashes of the sinner.' Here, lashes and evil powers may be said to be meant. 'They seized him, and he did not know' is similar to what was said: 'While the evil one was turning away from me, I did not perceive him.' The evil one was approaching; he provided no place for himself, having been persuaded by the apostolic opinion which says: 'Do not give place to the devil' (Eph 4:27).

I have not exhausted his examples. One of the ancient philosophers is said to have scourged himself so that he might fall from his own city, so that he might be accused by his fellow citizens. Fearing lest he should even utter a single word in pain, he bit his own tongue and cut it and threw it to the one who was assaulting him. That man was not able to say 'I did not know'; for indeed he knew a little, unless he had secured safety from some other source. But the holy man did not. Isaiah was sawn with a wooden saw.

And behold the wickedness of Manasseh the apostate, who practiced idolatry. And when the idol that he himself had set up fell, after Isaiah looked upon it and other things, they set forward accusers and two charges were brought against him: one, that, saying Moses said, 'No one has seen my face and shall live,' this man says, 'He saw the Lord of Sabaoth sitting upon a throne' (Isa 6:1). But if he stood precisely in the truth, I perceived his slandering. He did not say at all that he did not see his face. He saw it concealed, so that we might show them to be slanderers according to the word.

This, therefore, was the charge brought against him, and a second, that, regarding the ruler of the discerning race, of the holy priesthood, of the royal people, he said, 'Ruler of Sodom,' and regarding the people whom God loved and whom God honored, he said, 'People of Gomorrah.' Because of these two charges they slandered him, even though they previously knew that he did not say such things about him, but when the idol fell, they acted so that they might not appear as if they were avenging a god who was not manifest, but instead they attached a charge to him.

Isaiah might also say, 'whips were drawn against me, and I did not know.' Consider the malice of Manasseh; so that he might remain suffering for a long time, he was sawed with a wooden saw, so that the flesh being removed by those mills might prepare more pain and more duration.

Regarding the question: do they present punishments as if for a wrongdoer, and because of this they are whips? But I did not know them as whips, for I struggled and was crowned through them. Then I tested them, to see if I was such a person as those seemed to punish. Hypothetically: perhaps they also whipped Susanna, those who worked the slander against her; for there was such terror in her falling, as to say, 'distress is all around me.' If they offered these atrocities as if for an adulteress, they were whips. But she did not know them; for she was not lawless.

Let virtue, therefore, be like fish-glue to the saints. Let fire be offered, such as the burnings of shameful passion. She did not know that the present thing is a burning, that is, she was not tested; but the fish-glue, being bodily, is consumed by the fire, and then the fire of Him who was anointed is poured out, and he was not previously harmed. But for him whose virtue is a bonfire, the fish-glue-like substance remains always, and the fire never prevails against the one possessing virtue.

Regarding: 'He set the Most High as his refuge, and no whip shall strike his tent' (Ps 91:7): we find many having been whipped and having died in the whipping. If, therefore, we say that the one being whipped with sensible things does not feel their pains, it is not a struggle. This is not a great thing, and anyone could endure this. But they did not know, and this happens while being forced by the whips into being tested and being made to do something against their will. Behold, the examples of Susanna have become manifest; let the example of Joseph also be taken: how whips were presented as if for a lawless person, and neither of the two knew anything.

source_text: Ναβουθαὶν ἐπεβουλεύθη καὶ ἐμαστίχθη ὡς θεὸν εὐλογήσας, ὡς ὁ διάβολος εἶπεν ἀντὶ τοῦ βλασφημήσας, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνω· μὴ γὰρ ἐξωμόσατο τὴν θεοσέβειαν. ἐπερ · οὐ λέγεται καταχρηστικῶς· "ἀπὸ μαστίγων γλώσσης σε κρύψει"; τί ἐστιν ἡ "3μάστιξ τῆς γλώττης"3; –μὴ αἰσθητικῶς αὐτὸ λαμβάνεις. λόγος ψευδής ἐστιν, συκοφαντία. οὕτω καὶ αἱ πονηραὶ δυνάμεις ἐπεὶ καθάπτονται μᾶλλον τῶν μαςτίγων τοῦ ἡγεμονικοῦ τοῦ ἀφυλάκτως πρὸς αὐτὰς ἐσχηκότος, "3μάστιγες"3 λέγονται. καὶ ὅτι τοιοῦτο αὗται αἱ μάστιγες, "3συνήχθησαν"3. τὸ δὲ συναχθῆναι κατά τινος λογικοῦ ἐστιν. 15 διεσχίσθησαν καὶ οὐ κατηνύγησαν. ἡ ἐπὶ κακοῖς ὁμοφροσύνη φαῦλον μέγα ἐστίν, βλαβερόν 219 ἐστιν. συνεφώνησαν οὖν ποτε οἱ ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ ἐλθόντες εἰς τὸ πεδίον Σενναά, ὅπου καὶ Ναβουχοδονοσσὸρ ἤγειρεν τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ. καὶ ὅρα ὅτι φαῦλόν ἐστιν τοῦτο. ἑρμηνεύεται δὲ "3ὀδόντων ἐκτιναγμός"3. πολλάκις δὲ οἱ ὀδόντες ἀντὶ λόγων λαμβάνονται· "ὀδόντας" γοῦν "ἁμαρτωλῶν συνέτριψεν", καὶ οὐ δήπου λέγομεν ὅτι ταύτας τὰς αἰσθητὰς μύλας· οὐδὲ γὰρ τοῦτό ποτε ἱστορήθη. καί· "τὰς μύλας τῶν λεόντων συνέθλασεν κύριος". οὐ περὶ τῶν αἰσθητῶν τῶν τετραπόδων καὶ ἀγρίων λέγει θηρῶν ταῦτα λέγει, ἀλλὰ ἀνθρώπων τοιούτων. ἡ ἐπὶ κακοῖς οὖν ὁμοφροσύνη φαυλότατόν ἐστιν. ὁ δὲ τούτων σκορπισμὸς καὶ ἡ διαίρεσις ἀγαθόν τί ἐστιν. ἐὰν αἰσθηθῶσιν ἐκεῖνοι ὅτι διὰ κακίαν ἰδίαν ἐξ 139 ὁμοφρονούντων καὶ φειδῷ θεοῦ ἐσκορπίσθησαν –οἷον συνεφρόνησάν ποτε Σαδδουκαῖοι καὶ Φαρισαῖοι κατὰ Παύλου, ὅτε καὶ εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν αὐτὸν ἤγαγον, καὶ δέδωκεν αὐτοῖς αὐτὸν ὁ χιλίαρχος ἵνα δῆθεν διαγνῶσίν τι περὶ αὐτοῦ. σπουδὴν δὲ εἶχαν λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἀναιρῆσαι. αὐτοὶ δὲ τοῦτο ἠξιώκεισαν ἐνεχθῆναι αὐτὸν καὶ στῆναι ἐπὶ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν. "γνοὺς ὅτι τὸ ἕτερον μέρος Σαδδουκαίων ἐστίν, τὸ δὲ ἕτερον Φαρισαίων", εἶπέν τι τὸ διαλύον καὶ διασχίζον τὴν ὁμοφροσύνην αὐτῶν· εἶπεν γὰρ ὅτι· "περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι σήμερον", καὶ ἐσχίσθησαν ὡς τοὺς μὲν λέγειν· "3οὐδὲν ἄτοπον λέγει"3, τὸ δὲ ἐπικεῖσθαι. εἰ ἦσαν κατανυγέντες ἐκ τῆς διασχίσεως ταύτης, οὐκέτι ἐπεβούλευον τῷ Παύλῳ. οὐ κατηνύγησαν οὖν, οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τὸ αἴτιον τῆς διαιρέσεως. καὶ ὁ ∆αυὶδ γοῦν εὔχεταί που καὶ λέγει· "καὶ καταδίελε τὰς γλώσσας αὐτῶν"· τότε γὰρ καταδιαιροῦνται αἱ γλῶσσαι αὐτῶν, ἐὰν ἄρξωνται μαχόμενα λέγειν. τοῦτο γοῦν καὶ τοῖς κατὰ Σωσάννης πρεσβυτέροις ὑπῆρκται· διῃρέθησαν αἱ γλῶσσαι αὐτῶν, ἄλλα εἶπεν ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ἄλλα ὁ δεύτερος. εἰ ἦσαν κατανυγέντες, ἐπαύοντο τῆς κατηγορίας καὶ οὐχ ὑπέμενον ἃ ὑπέστησαν. "διεσχίσθησαν" οὖν "καὶ οὐ κατηνύγησαν". ὁ διασχίσας αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ τῷ κατανυγῆναι αὐτοὺς καὶ μετανοῆσαι τοῦτο πεποίηκεν. αὐτοὶ δὲ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τὸ αἴτιον τῆς διασχίσεως καὶ τῆς διαιρέσεως αὐτῶν. ἐπερ · τὸ "οὐ κατενύγησαν"; –οὐ μετενόησαν. κατανυγῆναί ἐστιν τὸ ἀθετῆσαι πρότερον ἑαυτοῦ λογισμὸν καὶ διάθεσιν πρώτην. ἀμέλει γοῦν ὅτε ἐν συναισθήσει γέγονεν τῶν παρελθόντων ὁ Ἀχαάμ, λέγει ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ἠλίᾳ· "εἶδες πῶς κατενύγη ὁ Ἀχαάμ"; κλαίων γὰρ ἐπέστρεψεν. καὶ ταύτην τὴν μεταβολὴν αὐτοῦ κατάνυξιν αὐτοῦ εἴρηκεν. ὁ δὲ ἅγιος ἐὰν λέγῃ· "ὅπως ἂν ψάλῃ σοι ἡ δόξα μου καὶ οὐ μὴ κατανυγῶ", "3οὐ μὴ μεταμεληθῶ"3. ἐπὶ δὲ τῶν ἄλλων συμβαίνει κατανυγῆναι τῶν μὴ ὀρθῶς γινομένων. 16 ἐπείρασάν με, ἐξεμυκτήρισάν με μυκτηρισμόν. δέον αὐτοὺς κατανυγέντας ἀποβαλεῖν τὴν κατ' ἐμοῦ ὀργήν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπ̣έβαλ̣ον, ἐπέθεντο, ἐπείρασάν με, ἐξεμυκτήρισάν με. πλὴν εἰ καὶ ἐπείρασάν με, οὐχ εὗρόν με οἷον ἐβούλοντο, οὐκ εἰσῆλθον εἰς πειρασμόν, εἰς τὰς πάγας τοῦ πειρασμοῦ αὐτῶν οὐκ ἐλήμφθην· τούτῳ γὰρ ἑρμηνεύεται καὶ τό· "μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειραςμόν". "ἐξεμυκτήρισάν με", εὐτέλισάν με. καὶ πάλιν ἀνδρείως ἐγὼ στὰς τὸν μυκτηρισμὸν αὐτῶν τὸ οὐδὲν ἔδειξα. 16 ἔβρυξαν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τοὺς ὀδόντας αὐτῶν. βρύχει τις τοὺς ὀδόντας ὁτὲ μὲν κατ' ἄλλου, ὁτὲ δὲ καθ' ἑαυτοῦ, ὅταν μεταμεληθῇ περιπεσὼν ἀνιαροῖς ἐξ ὧν ἔπραξεν· "ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων"· ἐπεὶ γὰρ γνόντες ὅτι παρὰ τὰς ἑαυτῶν ἀσεβείας καὶ ἁμαρτίας κολάζονται, ἐν μεταμελείᾳ γινόμενοι κλαίουσιν καὶ βρύχουσιν τοὺς ὀδόντας. ἄλλος δὲ βρύχει· διὸ "ἔβρυξεν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τοὺς ὀδόντας αὐτοῦ", περὶ τοῦ διαβόλου λέγεται, καὶ περὶ τῶν φαύλων ὧδε· "ἔβρυξαν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τοὺς ὀδόντας αὐτῶν". ἀποτυχόντες τοῦ σπουδαζομένου ἔβρυξαν ὡς μάτην κακοποιήσαντες ἢ πείρᾳ περιπεσόντες τῶν προς ἃ ἐβουλήθησαν ποιῆσαι, παθόντες ἃ δια θεῖναι ἠθέλησαν ἄλλον. ἐπερ · τοὺς λόγους οὖν δεῖ λαβεῖν τοὺς ὀδόντας; –ἐὰν μεταμέλειαν
english: Nebuchadnezzar plotted and was scourged as one blessing God, just as the devil said instead of blaspheming, and he did not realize; for he did not cast off godliness. Furthermore, it is not said improperly: 'I will hide you from the lashes of the tongue' (Psalm 52:2). What is this 'lash of the tongue'? Do not take it in a sensory way. It is a false word, a slander. In this way also the evil powers, since they are overcome more by the lashes of the ruling faculty being unguarded against them, are called 'lashes.' And that these lashes are such, they 'were gathered together.' To be gathered together is according to some logic. They were split apart and were not unified. Agreement upon evils is a great evil, it is harmful.

Thus, those coming from the east and coming into the plain of Sennacherib, where also Nebuchadnezzar raised his image, once agreed in one mind. And see that this is evil. It is interpreted as 'a scattering of teeth.' Often teeth are taken instead of words; for instance, 'he crushed the teeth of the sinners,' and we do not mean these sensory millstones; for this was never recorded. And: 'The Lord crushed the millstones of the lions.' He does not speak of the sensory, four-footed, and wild beasts, but of such humans. Therefore, agreement upon evils is most trivial. But the scattering and the division of these is something good.

If those realize that because of private malice they were scattered from those being in agreement, and by the sparing of God—just as the Sadducees and Pharisees once agreed according to Paul, when they also brought him into the council, and the high priest gave him to them so that he might be bound to know something about him—they had taken haste to overthrow him. But they deemed themselves worthy to have him led away and to stand upon the steps. 'Knowing that the one part belongs to the Sadducees and the other to the Pharisees,' something said that dissolved and split their agreement; for he said: 'Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am judged today' (Acts 23:9), and they were split, some saying: 'He says nothing absurd' (Acts 23:9), and the other part, the lying. If they had realized from this split, they would no longer have plotted against Paul. They were not unified, therefore; they did not know the cause of the division. And David, indeed, prays and says: 'And cut off the tongues...'

Their tongues are divided; for then their tongues are divided when they begin to fight in speech. This indeed happened to the elders according to Sosannas; their tongues were divided, the first saying one thing and the second another. If they had realized [their error], they would have ceased the accusation and would not have endured what they underwent.

Thus 'they were split' and 'they did not realize'. The one who split them did so so that they might realize and repent; but they did not know the cause of their splitting and their division. Regarding 'they did not realize'—they did not change their mind. To realize is to set aside one's former thought and original disposition. Indeed, when Ahaziah realized what had passed, God says to Elijah, 'Have you seen how Ahaziah realized?' (2 Kings 9:27), for he returned weeping. And regarding this change of his, He called it his realization. And the Saint, if he says, 'so that my glory may sing to you and I may never realize,' he means 'may I never change my mind.'

Regarding other matters, realization happens concerning things not going rightly. 'They tested me, they mocked me with a sneer.' It was necessary for them, having realized, to cast away their anger against me, but instead they laid upon me, they attacked, they tested me, they mocked me with a sneer. However, even though they tested me, they did not find me as they wished; they did not enter into temptation, I was not seized by the snares of their temptation; for this is also what is interpreted: 'lead us not into temptation' (Matt 6:13). 'They mocked me' means they treated me with contempt. And again, bravely standing against their sneer, I showed nothing.

'They gnashed their teeth at me.' One gnashes his teeth sometimes against another, and sometimes against himself when he changes his mind, having fallen into the cruelties of what he has done; 'there will be weeping and the gnashing of teeth' (Matt 13:42), because knowing that they are punished because of their own impiety and sin, they weep and gnash their teeth in repentance. Another gnashes; therefore 'he gnashed his teeth at me' is said concerning the devil, and concerning the wicked here: 'they gnashed their teeth at me.' Failing in what they were striving for, they gnashed as if having done evil in vain or having fallen into a trial of what they intended to do, suffering what they intended to do to another. Regarding the words, then, must we take the teeth?—if [there is] repentance.

source_text: σημαίνῃ καὶ ὀργὴν τῶν μὴ ἀνυσάντων ὃ προέθεν̣το ποιῆσαι, λαμβάνομεν τοῦτο, ὅτι "ἔβρυξαν τοὺς ὀδόντας", ἵνα ἡ βρῦξις τῶν ὀδόντων μεταμέλειαν αὐτῶν σημαίνει, ἢ μεταμέλειαν ἢ ὀδύνην ἐπελθοῦσαν αὐτοῖς διὰ τοῦ το ἀποτετευχέναι. ἐὰν δὲ ἄλλως θέλῃς τοὺς ὀδόντας λαβεῖν, οὐκ ἀπὸ το̣ῦ 220 ῥητοῦ τούτου· ὅτι πολλάκις ἔνεστιν ἀληθὲς θεώρημα λαβεῖν, οὐ μὴν ἀπὸ τοῦδε τοῦ ῥητοῦ. καὶ διὰ τὸ ἀληθὲς εἶναι, παραδέχονται αὐτὸ οἱ μὴ δυνάμενοι ἐξομαλίζειν πρὸς τὰς λέξεις τὰ νοήματα. οἱ ὀδόντες πολλάκις τῆς ψυχῆς λέγονται αἱ μασητικαὶ αὐτῆς δυνάμεις. ταύταις δὲ ταῖς μασητικαῖς δυνάμεσιν ταῖς λεπτυνούσαις τὰς τροφάς, εἰ δεόντως χρήσοιτο, ἐσθίει τὸν "ἄρτον τῆς ζωῆς", τὸν καρπὸν τοῦ "ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς", τὰς σάρκας Ἰησοῦ. εἰ δὲ 140 κακῶς αὐταῖς χρήσοιτο, ἐσθίει τὰς σάρκας τοῦ δράκοντος. αἱ σάρκες δὲ τοῦ δράκοντος δόγματα ἄθεά εἰσιν, ἁμαρτίαι μεγάλαι εἰσίν· ὡς γὰρ συνπληροῦται Ἰησοῦ σῶμα ἐκ τῶν δογμάτων, ὡς λέγει ὅτι· "εἰκῆ φυσιούμενος" σπουδῇ "νοὸς σαρκὸς καὶ μὴ κρατῶν τὴν κεφαλήν, ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα συναρμολογούμενον αὔξει τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ θεοῦ". τοῦτο λέγει· ὁ σάρκινον ἔχων νοῦν, τουτέστιν ὁ σαρκίνως καὶ αἰσθητῶς προσιέμενος, εἰκῆ φυσιούμενον ἔχει τὸν νοῦν σάρκα ὄντα, καὶ οὐ κρατεῖ τὴν κεφαλὴν τῶν δογμάτων, οὐ κρατεῖ αὐτοῦ τοῦ σωτῆρος, ὅς ἐστιν τῶν δογμάτων κεφαλή. καὶ τὰ μεγάλα δὲ τῶν θεολογουμένων κεφαλὴ τοῦ τοιούτου σώματός ἐστιν, "ἐξ οὗ συναρμολογούμενον τὸ σῶμα διὰ πάσης ἁφῆς καὶ συνδέσμων αὔξει τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ θεοῦ". οὕτω γοῦν καὶ ἡμεῖς, ὅταν πλείονες λόγοι καὶ κεφάλαια πολλὰ εἰς ἓν ἔχωσιν τὴν ἀναφοράν, λέγομεν σεσωματοποιῆσθαι τὸν λόγον. ἐὰν λάβωμεν ὅτι αἱ μασητικαὶ τῆς ψυχῆς δυνάμεις, ἀληθὲς μέν τι λέγομεν, οὐ πρὸς τὸ προκείμενον δέ. ἐὰν δὲ καὶ τοῦτο λάβῃς, ὅτι χρῶνταί ποτε ταῖς μασητικαῖς ταύταις δυνάμεσίν τινες ἐπιβουλευτικῶς κατὰ τό· "εἰ δὲ ἀλλήλους δάκνετε καὶ κατεσθίετε", καί· "τοὺς κατεσθίοντας τὸν Ἰσραὴλ ὅλῳ τῷ στόματι", καὶ αὗται ἀναφέρουσιν κόλασιν, καὶ δύναται καὶ οὕτω νοηθῆναι ὅτι· "ἔβρυξαν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τοὺς ὀδόντας"· τούτους τοὺς ὀδόντας ἔβρυξαν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο συντριβὴν αὐτῶν ὑποστήσονται· "ὀδόντας" γὰρ "ἁμαρτωλῶν συνέτριψας". 17 κύριε, πότε ἐφόψῃ; πότε ἐπισκέψῃ ὥστε ἐκείνους μὲν κωλῦσαι, ἐμὲ δὲ ἔξω ποιῆσαι τῶν βλαβῶν; τὸ γὰρ "3ἐφόψῃ"3 καὶ "3ὄψῃ"3 πολλάκις εἰρήκαμεν ὅτι τὴν μακροθυμίαν σημαίνει τὸ παρασιωπῆσαι. "κύριε, πότε ἐφίδοις"; ἐὰν γὰρ ἐφίδοις, καὶ ἐμὲ εὐεργετήσεις ἐπιβλέψας ἐπ' ἐμὲ καὶ ἐλεήσας με, κἀκείνους ἐκτὸς ποιήσεις τῆς σπουδῆς τῆς εἰς τὸ κακόν, ὥστε μηδὲ ἐμὲ βλαβῆναι ὑπ' αὐτῶν μηδὲ αὐτοὺς ἐνμεῖναι ἔτι τῇ κακίᾳ τῇ θηριώδει ἣν ἐπιτηδεύουσιν ἔτι. 17 ἀποκατάστησον τὴν ψυχήν μου ἀπὸ τῆς κακουργίας αὐτῶν. εἶπεν ἐπικειμένους πολεμίους πολλοὺς καὶ πολλὰ αὐτὸν κακωτικῶς διαθέντας. καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀρχῆς τοῦ ψαλμοῦ τοῦτο παρίσταται· "δίκασον, κύριε, τοὺς ἀδικοῦντάς με, πολέμησον τοὺς πολεμοῦντάς με", καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς· "καὶ ἕως οὗ εἶδες, κύριε"; "ἔβρυξαν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τοὺς ὀδόντας αὐτῶν". "συνήχθησαν κ̣ατ' ἐμοῦ μάστιγες, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνων". λέγει οὖν ὅτι· ἔξω αὐτῶν ποίησόν μου τὴν ψυχήν· καὶ γὰρ ἔξω ἦν αὐτῶν· τοῦτο γὰρ τὸ τῆς ἀποκαταστάσεως ὄνομα μνημονεύει. οὐδεὶς ὑπάγων εἰς τόπον, ἔνθα οὐδέποτε γέγονεν, λέγεται ἀποκαθίστασθαι, ἀλλὰ ὁ ἐλθὼν ἔκ τινος πατρίδος ἐπ' ἄλλην πατρίδα ἢ ἐκ τόπου εἰς ἕτερον τόπον. λέγει οὖν ὅτι· τὴν ψυχήν μου ἁγίαν οὖσαν ἠθέλησαν παγιδεῦσαι, διαφθορᾷ αὐτὴν ὑποβαλεῖν. τότε δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς κακουργίας τῶν πονηρῶν ἀποκαθίσταται, ὅταν μηδὲν ὑπ' αὐτῶν πάθῃ, ὅταν μὴ ποιωθῇ κατ' αὐτούς. ἡ Σωσάννα ἐπὶ σωφροσύνῃ ἀνετράφη καὶ ἄγαν ἦν σώφρων παιδευθεῖσα κατὰ τὸν νόμον Μωσέως. τὸ ὅσον ἧκεν εἰς τοὺς ἐπιθεμένους αὐτῇ πρεσβυτέρους ἑάλω μοιχείᾳ. παρεκάλεσεν κἀκείνη λέγουσα· "3ἀποκατάστησον τὴν ψυχήν μου"3, εἰς τὴν αὐτὴν σωφροσύνην ἄγαγε ἀπὸ τῆς τούτων κακουργίας. ταῦτα ἐρεῖ καὶ πᾶς τις ἐπιβουλευόμενος. καὶ ἡ τῶν μαρτύρων δὲ ψυχὴ ἀπεκατέστη ἐν μηδενὶ πειρασθεῖσα. ὅτι δὲ τὸ ἀποκαταστῆναι τοῦτο σημαίνει, ἐν ἑνὶ τῶν ψαλμῶν λέγει· "σὺ εἶ ὁ ἀποκαθιστῶν τὴν κληρονομίαν μου ἐμοί". κατὰ τοῦτο τὸ σημαινόμενον λέγομεν τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀποκατεστάσθαι 221 εἰς τὸν παράδεισον, ὅτι γέγονεν αὐτῷ εἴσοδος ἐκεῖ, ὅτε ἤκουσεν ὁ μετανοήσας· "σήμερον μετ' ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ". "ἀποκατάστησον" οὖν "τὴν ψυχήν μου". εἰς τοσοῦτόν εἰσιν κακουργήσαντες ὡς θῆρες ἄγριοι κατ' ἐμοῦ γεγενῆσθαι. 17 ἀπὸ λεόντων τὴν μονογενῆν μου.
english: It also signifies the anger of those who did not endure what he intended to do; we take this from 'they gnashed their teeth', so that the gnashing of the teeth signifies their destruction, or a pain coming upon them because of what they encountered. But if you wish to take the teeth otherwise, it is not from this specific word; for often it is true to take a theological insight, though not necessarily from this word. And because it is true, those who are unable to harmonize the meanings with the words accept it.

The teeth are often called the masticatory powers of the soul. And with these masticatory powers which mince the foods, if one were to use them properly, he eats the 'bread of life', the fruit of the 'tree of life', the flesh of Jesus. But if he were to use them badly, he eats the flesh of the dragon. And the flesh of the dragon are impious doctrines, they are great sins; for just as the body of Jesus is filled up from the doctrines, as it says: 'vainly puffing oneself up' in haste 'with a mind of flesh and not holding the head, from which the whole body being joined together increases the growth of God'.

This says: he who has a fleshly mind, that is, he who approaches carnally and sensually, has a mind vainly puffing itself up being flesh, and does not hold the head of the doctrines, he does not hold the Savior, who is the head of the doctrines. And the great [things] of those being theologized are the head of such a body, 'from which the body being joined together through every ligament and sinew increases the growth of God'. In this same way also we, when more words and many headings have their reference to one thing, we say the word has been embodied.

If we take that the masticatory powers of the soul [are the teeth], we say something true, but not regarding the immediate context. But if you also take this, that some use these masticatory powers treacherously against that: 'if you bite and devour one another' (Gal 5:15), and: 'those devouring Israel with the whole mouth' (Rev 9:5), and these refer to punishments, it is also possible to think thus: 'they gnashed their teeth against me'; they gnashed these teeth, and because of this they will undergo destruction; for 'you crushed the teeth of the sinners' (Ps 58:7). Lord, how long will you look on?

When you visit so as to forbid them, and to make me outside of the harms? For regarding 'to turn away' and 'to look away', we have often said that to pass by signifies long-suffering. 'Lord, when will you have pity?' For if you have pity, you will also do good to me, looking upon me and having mercy on me, and you will set even them outside of their haste toward evil, so that they do not harm me, nor do they remain any longer in that beastly malice which they are still practicing.

Restore my soul from their malice. He says this because lying enemies are present, many and having much planned maliciously against him. And from the beginning of the psalm this is presented: 'Judge, Lord, those doing wrong to me, fight against those fighting against me' (Psalm 35:23), and the following: 'And until I saw, Lord' (Psalm 34:19); 'they gnashed their teeth against me' (Psalm 35:16); 'whips were gathered against me, and I did not know' (Psalm 38:11).

He says therefore: make my soul outside of them; for indeed it was outside of them; for this is what the name of 'restoration' remembers. No one enters into a place where it never was, it is said to be restored, but one having come from one fatherland to another fatherland, or from one place to another place. He says therefore: they wished to ensnare my soul, being holy, to subject it to corruption. Then it is restored from the malice of the wicked, when it suffers nothing from them, when it does not act against them.

Susanna was overturned regarding her self-control, and she was very much self-controlled having been educated according to the Law of Moses, despite how far she had fallen into adultery by the elders attacking her. She pleaded, saying: 'Restore my soul' (Psalm 31:6), to lead her back into that same self-control from the malice of these men. All who are plotting against one say these things. And the soul of the martyrs is restored, having been tested in nothing.

For as to what this 'to restore' signifies, in one of the psalms he says: 'You are the one restoring my inheritance to me' (Psalm 71:19). According to this meaning we say the man is restored into Paradise, because entrance there has become possible for him, when the penitent heard: 'Today you will be with me in Paradise' (Luke 23:43). 'Restore' therefore 'my soul'. They have acted with such malice toward me as to have become wild beasts. 17 [Restore me] from lions, my only one.

english: "Restore my only-begotten from the lions" (Ps 51:7). He says that he has his soul as only-begotten. He had it as only-begotten; he had it as alone. It is not possible for more than one soul to be tested, since therefore it is only-begotten to me.

And in another way: "God made man upright" (Gen 1:26), "in his own image" and "likeness" he created him. When it remains in this state according to which it was created, it does not become outside himself; it does not become outside himself. Since therefore it is the person of the Savior saying this—which Jesus had as a soul—it does not belong to anyone else.

And our souls become those of the rulers; for whoever is defeated by someone, to him he is also surrendered. And it is indeed possible to fall away from the true Lord to other masters and from one to others, when discordant sins occur; for the one having repented is restored from the malice of those surrounding it into goodness. Since therefore the soul of Jesus "has been tested in every way according to likeness without sin" (cf. Heb 4:15), it never belonged to anyone else except to the one who took it. Because of this he calls it his only-begotten.

And it must be said also thus: "my only-begotten"; for all souls become of the Savior: "receiving the end of faith the salvation of souls" (Heb 2:4). Concerning salvation, therefore, is the seeking and searching of a prophet. They are, therefore, "receiving the salvation, the end of faith" of the Savior. They are indeed members of him, all of them becoming his body. But this one is to him differently from those; for this one he chose to have as an instrument and a temple, so that through it he might dispense the energies, through it the salvation.

So also, having been born in Hades, he did not remain there; for he was only-begotten of him. And "only-begotten" often signifies "alone." Aetius the Arian, the father of Eunomius, who overwhelmed him, used to say: "as great" (meaning), he says, "are they being granted to Christ because he is the only-begotten of God." He says: "and others are only-begotten; the world is only-begotten, the sun, the earth." I say to him: it is not the same to be called only-begotten and an only-begotten offspring and an only-begotten child. Only Jesus is said to be "only-begotten Son" (John 1:14); for it is said: "we beheld his glory, a glory as of the only-begotten from the Father" (John 1:14). And the "only-begotten from the Father" child...

It is not 'only-begotten'. And it is always so: 'For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son' (John 3:16). He never said 'only-begotten' simply, but 'only-begotten Son'. And again: 'because they did not believe in the name of the only begotten Son of God' (John 1:18). If something were a unique creation, as you say, 'monogenes', but not a unique work—for there are also other works of God—it would not be a unique creation.

Therefore, when the saint says: 'Look upon me and have mercy on me, for I am alone and poor', he means 'I am alone'. And Elijah, saying: 'I alone am left, and they seek my life to take it from me' (1 Kings 19:10), it would have been said 'alone', not 'son' or 'child'. And here he says: 'my only one from the lions', the cruel ones, those having risen up against me. Save and redeem my soul, which is mine alone; for this one alone did not know sin, this one alone 'has been tested in all things without sin' (1 Cor 10:13).

Furthermore: how was he restored? He did not fall into sins, but rather, how much he was reverent toward the cruelty of those lying in wait, that he might not suffer this. Now we speak from the perspective of the holy man. And the examples of Susanna and Joseph are clear. And the devil himself has devices, sophistic thoughts, which only he and every diligent person can know. For Paul says: 'we are not ignorant of his devices' (2 Cor 2:11). His thoughts are his methods, his very wiles, the sophistic thoughts through which he wants to campaign against us.

Therefore, 'restore' us; for the state of being frightened was entirely a pre-passion. And he wants to bring us out from that pre-passion; for he did not say 'from my wickedness'. Furthermore: to what state of indifference? He did not say, while being frightened, 'restore me to indifference', but to a state where he no longer even has pre-passion. I have a feeling that I am disturbed. 'Restore' therefore 'my soul'. 'Why are you sorrowful, my soul, and why are you troubled within me? Hope in God, for I shall yet praise him' (Psalm 42:5); for he did not say to another; he spoke to his own mind: 'Why are you sorrowful and why are you troubled within me?'. You have Him who stops the disturbance. As if someone were saying while burning and being agitated: 'Why do you burn so? There is a physician able to...'

english: To be freed from the fever. 'Hope in God, for I will confess to him' (Ps 34:8). Once she persuaded herself to hope in God, she was restored from dread and turmoil, which dread and which turmoil arose from the malice of evil powers and from the devil himself. 'From lions, my only-begotten one' (Ps 22:1). He named these malicious ones and lions those who wish to fight, those who attack and come like whips against him.

Since 'he has been tested in all things, yet without sin, according to the likeness' (Heb 4:15), we grant her a pre-passion. But pre-passion is not sin; for if you do not grant this, you introduce another essence into the soul, and it would have neither glory nor worthiness of praise and crowns if it were not shaken. For you have in the Gospel that: 'she began to be terrified and to be in distress' (Mk 5:38); for is not the 'beginning' something other than the pre-passion? This beginning is only the beginning itself; it has nothing with it. This alone, before the choosing of evils, chose the good. This has often been said.

The essence of the rational [soul] is receptive of those things it is naturally disposed to receive. It is receptive of passion, desire, grief, turmoil, and fear. When something presents itself that moves fear, the rational essence is certainly troubled. Sometimes, however, it establishes the turmoil immediately as if nothing were with it. This they call pre-passion.

You say: is it the same to say 'a man' and 'a doing man'? If I say a man has died, I do not speak of the 'doing' man, such as the righteous man. The death of the righteous is not necessarily the dissolution of the soul from the body, but the ceasing of being righteous. This is the corruption of the righteous. Often, being ignorant of the false opinions of the ungodly, we fall into them. And falling into those, we lose the right opinion. You ask: how do you say that I have not understood? I do not call him righteous. But if another understands as has been said and calls him righteous, he is the same [man] both righteous and unrighteous. Listen then, because...

What have I said regarding the opinion of the Protagoreans—for Protagoras was a Sophist—they say that being for those that exist is in appearing. They say: 'I appear to you now sitting; but when away, I do not appear sitting; it is unclear whether I sit or do not sit.' And they say that all existing things are in appearing; for example, I see the moon, but another does not see it; it is unclear whether it is or is not. To me, the healthy one, there comes a perception of honey that it is sweet, but to another that it is bitter, if he is feverish; it is therefore unclear whether it is bitter or sweet. And thus they wish to dogmatize incomprehensibility.

If then we also say: 'Since it does not appear to me, by what reasoning has he spoken, I consider him unjust and impious.' If it appears to another, by what reasoning has he spoken, he appears just and pious to that one. And another again does not even stand by the things said by him; neither is he pious nor impious, and we fall into the Protagorean opinion. Let us see then: it is necessary first to understand things and thus to judge or not to judge. He who does not speak of him correctly nor healthily spoken, what kind of intellect of the words does he speak of?

But how then does Job speak? (Job 3:3) If I say: 'Let the day perish in which I was born,' let the genesis perish; for I have come from better things to worse; for it is profitable for me that the evil should perish. As if Jeremiah speaks concerning the people of the Hebrews—and each of the captured Hebrews will say—'Let the day of captivity perish,' he does not say this: 'let there be no more captivity.' english: of the life that is imminent. Furthermore, does he not sin then? — does not he who insults Satan sin? Does the impious one, 'in being cursed,' curse the impious one, 'Satan, he curses his own soul'? He curses Satan not because he is a creation of God, but because he is evil and impious. And he himself is also impious. Therefore he curses himself, and this curse is not empty. If someone curses him because he is impious, he hates the cause, which is that perceived satanic thing. And impiety is the cause. And perhaps he has ceased, or if not ceasing, he will be punished. If the captives are now cursing the day of their captivity, they do not say this so that they might no longer be subject to the captivity—'do they perhaps have the captivity as a cause'—and be exalted by it.

Furthermore, does he then curse 'that day'? And why did he also add 'that'? For one day does not differ from another. Then he says: 'May he who is about to grasp the great whale curse it' (Psalm 70:1). Why did he not say: 'He who made the sun, he who constructed the cosmos,' but 'he who is about to grasp the great whale'? For the Savior has come and, 'having grasped the great whale,' described the genesis of humans, so as to give them another genesis, the 'from water and spirit' (John 3:5), which is principally called regeneration. And regeneration is genesis upon genesis, just as 'repetition' is song upon song. And he called the resurrection of the dead regeneration; for he says to the disciples: 'You also will sit in the regeneration on twelve thrones' (Matthew 19:28), instead of 'in the resurrection, in the age to come' (1 Corinthians 15:52).

If I say: 'May I not see this day,' being in affliction or disease, do I say 'may I not see' regarding the time, since it has passed? For time does not turn back. Furthermore, has he said that that cause of his genesis is sin? — I do not say this again, but that he who curses a day or blesses a day does not bless or curse with respect to time, but with respect to the things that have happened in time. I say: does he not say 'it is better to dissolve and be with Christ' (Philippians 1:23)? He does not say that being released from this life is better. Furthermore, will he say that being joined to it is better or worse? — neither worse nor better. Furthermore, is it indifferent? — if this is indifferent, then the opposite [is also...]

It is indifferent. Or, is it not [considered] as evil, but as toward the better? Opposites do not coexist. If one of these is good, the other is evil, and if the other is evil, the other good must be accepted, as it is regarding virtue and vice, injustice and justice, piety and impiety. If the other is bad, the remainder is good. But when neither of the opposites is bad, neither is the remainder. White and black are opposites; and since white is indifferent, being neither good nor evil, so too is the black of the white.

Or, do you say that the outside of the body becomes good according to the one saying 'to dissolve'? Look from the end: the one having dissolved becomes in Christ. Or, is this comparative? Pay attention to what you say. The things said to be comparative are said as being of the same kind, not as being opposed; just as when I say, 'Sodom was justified because of you' (Gen 19:28), it is not that Sodom has been justified. 'Because of your own sins, O Jerusalem' (Jer 15:9), because a prophet was killed and has become a traitor to the Savior. That Sodom incited one man, Lot. 'That [Sodom] was justified because of you.' Not simply was it justified—for it has not been justified—but 'because of you.' And if it says again: 'He loved wickedness rather than goodness, and deceitful lips rather than to speak righteousness' (Ps 52:3), these things are said comparatively, not oppositely; for this is said because, once one is decided, the other is immediately placed.

The 'dissolving' then [is] 'and to be in Christ'—if you say it is indifferent to 'remaining in the flesh,' and this is indifferent; for it has been shown to us that the things being compared and added have this state: if the other is bad, the remainder is not important. If it is important to be 'with Christ, the one having dissolved,' the turning away from the world, being outside the flesh, or being in the flesh, even if it is, according to you, inferior, [it is] good. The inferior is intended to perish, so that he may become a master of the greater. And I say the loss thus: the hindrance, his ceasing. english: To perish is to no longer endure. One is agitated by the name of destruction and of disturbance. But one ought not to be agitated. Paul, therefore, was not agitated by such things: 'in part,' he says, 'we know and in part we prophesy; if the perfect comes, the partial will be done away with' (1 Cor 13:10). And they think that being done away with is a worse thing than perishing. Thus we have often said that the partial is done away with not utterly, but that the partial exists, and we received such an image regarding the earnest money.

Furthermore: how do we give, as righteous or as a sinner? It is not this alone you wish to learn; for many things are understood by him. If you had remembered what you heard, you would not always have been agitated about these things. I said: let a king be the ruler of the inhabited world, about whom all are filled with the conviction that he is righteous and whatever he does, he does as a righteous man. 'Bless, O my soul, the Lord' (Ps 103:1). If I keep it thus active toward what was set by the Creator, it is only-begotten. But if at other times it acts otherwise and serves someone, it is no longer the only-begotten of the possessor, but at times it is his, and at times it becomes outside of him.

And in order that I might receive according to the Gospel: he who departed from his father's house became a stranger outside of himself; his soul was no longer his own. But indeed, when he repented, he says: 'having entered into himself' (Luke 15:17). Consequently, he became his own; his soul consequently became his own. This is similar to 'know thyself.' He who knows himself is within himself.

'I will confess to you in a great church, in a heavy people I will praise you' (Ps 18:24). Then a great and many church is called, when it is filled from each side by many; for it is not called a great and many church if it is from small and lowly men. 'He speaks wisdom among the perfect,' says the apostle. These, becoming the same and 'being completed by the same mind and the same judgment,' are a many and great church. And just as I say a wise church when those filling it from each side are wise, and I say a stable and knowledgeable city when the citizens filling it from each side are stable and knowledgeable, so I say a many and great church of those filling it having greatness—but greatness of soul and of mind, not of the body. Again, he says 'a heavy people' regarding the...

For they have become accustomed to call things that are honorable and most precious 'heavy'. This too the Scripture witnesses; for how much the Queen of Sheba came to Solomon, it says, 'in great power' (1 Kings 10:1). And it says the 'heavy power' is her possession, which she had brought. She brought many precious stones, many delicacies, gold, silver, and other accompaniments of wealth. And that power of wealth was called 'heavy' instead of 'precious' or 'valuable'.

Therefore he says that when each of those who complete the people—as I have said concerning the church—is most precious and honorable, for 'glory and honor and peace to everyone who works the good' (cf. Rom 12:10/1 Pet 5:10), if the one working the good possesses glory and honor, the people are an honor. Moreover, it is said about it that it was a 'royal priesthood, a holy nation' (Exod 19:6). The 'holy nation' is completed from all those who are holy, and the 'royal priesthood' is composed of many healers of God. Therefore, 'in a people, I will praise you greatly' (Ps 5:11).

He also prepares him, so that he may also be able to send up a hymn. But he is able to do this when he becomes straight according to the soul and the mind; for 'praise is fitting for the upright' (Ps 5:11). May those who hate me unjustly not rejoice over me (Ps 35:25). Great boldness is in saying these things. They hate me unjustly. They do this, though I provide no pretext or cause for them to lie hostile toward me. Since, therefore, the enemies rejoice when I fall into evils, let me not fall into evils so that they might rejoice over me or assail me; for he who wishes to lead someone into lawlessness rejoices over him, being evil, when he falls into what he strove to surround him with. Let this, therefore, not be to me, so as to make those who hate me unjustly rejoice.

Those who hate me without cause and roll their eyes (Ps 35:19). The 'unjustly' and 'without cause' are the same, 'without reason', and 'rolling eyes' against me; they do not only speak against me with words, but they also roll their eyes. And since often, when the heterodox, regarding those who do us harm, agree with those toward whom they roll their eyes with their own minds, they are of one mind in impiety, because to me they are peaceful...

source_text: ἐλάλουν καὶ ἐπ' ὀργὴν δόλους διελογίζοντο. ἓν εἶδος τῆς ἀσεβείας τοῦτο· εἰρηνικὰ λαλοῦντες οὐκ εἰρηνικὰ ἔπραττον. τοῦτο δὲ ἀδικῆσαί ἐστιν. εἰρηνικὰ λαλεῖ ἐν τοῖς φίλοις, ἐν τοῖς ἑταίροις ὡς φιλάλληλος, δόλους δὲ διαλογίζεται ἐπ' ὀργῇ. πᾶς δόλον εἰς τὸν πλησίον ἔχων ὀργιζόμενος αὐτῷ τοῦτο ποιεῖ. καὶ λέγω· ἡ ὀργὴ ὄρεξίς ἐστιν τιμωρίας. πάντως δὲ ὁ δόλῳ τινὶ προσερχόμενος βλάψαι ἐκεῖνον θέλει, ὥστε ὁ δόλιος καὶ ὀργίλος ἐστίν. τῷ δὲ δοκεῖν οὔκ ἐστιν πολλάκις ὀργίλος φαινόμενος εἰρηνικὰ λαλῶν. τοῦτο γοῦν καὶ ἐν Ἰηρεμίᾳ λέγεται περί τινος· "τῷ πλησίον αὐτοῦ λαλεῖ εἰρηνικὰ καὶ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔχει τὴν ἔχθραν". "ἐμοὶ" οὖν, φησίν, "εἰρηνικὰ ἐλάλουν". οὐκ "εἰρηνικὰ" ἁπλῶς "ἐλάλουν", ἀλλ' "ἐμοί"· ἐμὲ ἀπατῆσαι θέλοντες εἰρηνικὰ ἐλάλουν· οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἀληθῶς εἰρηνικὸς ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖ τινι εἰρηνικὰ ἄλλην ἔχων διάνοιαν κατ' ἐκείνου. αὐτίκα γοῦν ὁ σωτὴρ λέγει πρὸς ἑτέροις "τοὺς εἰρηνοποιοὺς μακαρίους" εἶναι, "ὅτι υἱοὶ θεοῦ εἰσιν". υἱῶν θεοῦ ἐστιν τὸ εἰρηνικοὶ εἶναι. εἰρηνοποιοὺς δὲ εἶπεν τοὺς ποιοῦντας εἰρήνην. ὅταν εἰς συμφωνίαν καὶ φιλίαν ἄγωσιν τοὺς διεστηκότας τῇ προαιρέσει, εἰρηνοποιοί εἰσιν. καὶ ἐφ' ἑαυτῶν δὲ εἰρηνοποιοί εἰσιν. πρότερον δὲ εἰρήνην ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ποιήσαντες, ὥστε μηδὲ λογισμοὺς μαχομένους ἔχειν ἑαυτοῖς ἢ ἔργα· τότε εἰρήνην ἐποίησαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς. ταύτην δὲ τὴν εἰρήνην καὶ εἰς ἑτέρους μεταφέρουσιν· οἷοι γὰρ ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοί, καὶ τοὺς διδασκομένους θέλουσιν εἶναι. εἰρηνεύειν διδάσκουσιν τὴν ψυχὴν πρὸς τὸ σῶμα καὶ τὸ σῶμα πρὸς τὴν ψυχήν· ὅταν γὰρ ἡ ψυχὴ "ὑπωπιάζῃ τὸ σῶμα καὶ δουλαγωγῇ", καὶ ἄρχῃ μὲν ἡ ψυχή, ἄρχηται δὲ τὸ σῶμα, εἰρήνη ἐστὶν σώματος καὶ ψυχῆς. ὥσπερ οὖν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς κατεσκεύασαν εἰρήνην, οὕτω καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἄλλοις τοῖς στεργομένοις καὶ ἀγαπῶσιν ἢ καὶ μαχομένοις τοῦτο πράττουσιν. διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἐν τῇ ∆ιδαχῇ τῇ βίβλῳ τῆς κατηχήσεως λέγεται· "εἰρηνεύσεις μαχομένους". ὁ δὲ ἄλλους μαχομένους εἰς εἰρήνην καὶ συναλλαγὰς φέρων ἑαυτὸν πρότερον εἰρήνευσεν, οὐκ ἔχει μάχην ἐν ἑαυτῷ, οὐκ ἔχει λογισμοὺς μαχομένους. 21 καὶ ἐπλάτυναν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τὸ στόμα αὐτῶν. τὸν λόγον ἑαυτῶν ἐπλάτυναν ἐπ' ἐμὲ εἰρηνικὰ λαλοῦντες. ὁ νοῦς δὲ αὐτῶν ἐστενεύετο ὑπὸ τοῦ δόλου εἰς ταὐτὸν συναγόμενος οὐκ ἐπαινετῶς, ἀλλ' ὥστε μὴ ἔχειν τὰς οἰκείας ἀρετάς. δύναται καὶ τοῦτο· "ἐπλάτυναν ἐπ' ἐμὲ" ὡς εἰρηνικὰ λαλοῦντες καὶ ἐπ' ὀργῇ δόλους διαλογιζόμενοι ἔδοξάν με ἀπατᾶν. τότε λοιπὸν ἤρξαντο πλατὺ καχάζειν καὶ πλατύνειν ἐπ' ἐμὲ τὸν λόγον αὐτῶν. ἔχεις ἐν ἱστορίαις σύμβολα τοιαῦτα· ἡ ∆αλιλὰ ἡ εἰςαγομένη ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ τῶν Κριτῶν πόρνη δόλοις ἐβουλεύετο ἐπ228 αγαγέσθαι τὸν Σαμψών, ἵνα δῷ τοῖς ἀλλοφύλοις τοῖς φονεῦσαι αὐτὸν ἐθέλουσιν. καὶ ἔλεγεν ὅτι· "ἐν τίνι ἀσθενήσει σου ἡ ἰσχὺς ἢ τίνι ὡς εἷς τῶν 146 ἀνθρώπων ἀσθενὴς γενήσῃ"; ἔλεγεν αὐτῇ οὐ τὸ ἀληθές. εἶτα ἐκείνη νομίσασα ὅτι ἠλήθευεν, ἐδέσμει αὐτὸν καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ἐποίει καὶ ὥσπερ ἐπικερτομοῦσα ἔλεγεν· "ἀλλόφυλοι ἐπὶ σέ, Σαμψώ". ἴδε, ἐπλάτυνεν ἐπ' αὐτὸν τὸ στόμα. πάλαι μὲν παρεκάλει, ἐστωμυλεύετο. ὅτε δὲ ἔδοξεν εἰληφέναι αὐτὸν ἐντὸς ἀρκύων, ἐπικερτομοῦσα ἔλεγεν· "ἀλλόφυλοι ἐπὶ σέ, Σανψώ". καὶ ὅρα, ὅτι ἡ πάλαι εἰρηνικὰ λαλοῦσα καὶ ἐπὶ ὀργῇ δόλους λογιζομένη ὅτε ἔδοξεν ἐνκρατὴς γενέσθαι, ἐπλάτυνεν τὸ στόμα μεγαλορημονοῦσα λοιπόν. 21 εἶπαν Εὖγε εὖγε, εἶδαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἡμῶν. εἰώθασιν οἱ δοκο̣ῦντες ἐσχηκέναι ὑποχείριον ὃν ἐβούλοντο, οὕτω λαλεῖν· "3εὖγε εὖγε, ὃ ἐβουλόμεθα, ου εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἡμῶν· οὐκέτι σ̣ε τοιοῦτον ὁρῶμεν, οἷος ὑπελάμβανες εἶναι, ἀλλ' ὡς ἡμεῖς ἠθέλαμεν. εὑρήκαμέν σε εὐάλωτον"3. 22 εἶδες, κύριε, μὴ παρασιωπήσῃς. τὸ "3μὴ παρασιωπήσῃς"3 τὸ "3μηκέτι μακροθυμήσῃς"3· ἐκ πολλῶν γὰρ λέξεων τοῦτο ἐδείξαμεν· "ἐσιώπησα ἀπ' αἰῶνος, μὴ καὶ ἀεὶ σιωπήσομαι"; ἐμακροθύμησα, οὐκ ἐπεξῆλθον τοῖς κακοῖς πραττομένοις. μὴ καὶ ἀεὶ τοῦτ' ἔσται. ἀγαθότης πάλιν γνωρίζεται τοῦ ἀπειλοῦντος τῷ ἤδη κολαστέῳ, ἵνα διὰ τῆς ἀπειλῆς διεγείρῃ καὶ εἰς μετάνοιαν αὐτὸν ἀγάγῃ. καὶ ἐν ἄλλῳ ψαλμῷ λέγει· "τῷ δὲ ἁμαρτωλῷ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Ἵνα τί σὺ ἐκδιηγῇ τὰ δικαιώματά μου καὶ ἀναλαμβάνεις τοὺς λόγους μου διὰ χειλέων σου; σὺ δὲ ἐμίσησας παιδείαν". εἶτα ἐπὶ τέλει· "ταῦτα ἐποίησας, καὶ ἐσίγησα"–οὐκ ἐπεξῆλθον– "ὑπέλαβες ἀνομίαν ὅτι ἔσομαί σοι ὅμοιος"· ἀλλ' οὐκ ἀεὶ ἡ μακροθυμία μένει· "ἐλέγξω" γάρ "σε καὶ παραστήσω κατὰ πρόσωπον" τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου. καὶ αἱ ἀπειλαὶ οὖν τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ ἀγαθότητα πολλὴν γίνονται.
english: They were speaking and calculating deceits in anger. This is a kind of impiety; while speaking peaceably, they were not acting peaceably. This is an injustice. One speaks peaceably to friends and companions as a lover of peace, but calculates deceits in anger. Anyone who approaches a neighbor with any deceit and is angry with him does this. And I say: anger is a desire for punishment. For anyone approaching with deceit wants to harm that person, so that the deceitful one is also an angry one. And many times, appearing not to be, he seems to be speaking peaceably.

This indeed is also said in Jeremiah concerning someone: 'He speaks peaceably to his neighbor, but holds enmity within himself' (Jeremiah 9:4). 'To me,' he says, 'they spoke peaceably.' They did not simply speak 'peaceably,' but 'to me'; wanting to deceive me, they spoke peaceably; for the truly peaceful man does not speak peaceably to someone while holding another intention against him. Immediately also the Savior says to others that 'the peacemakers are blessed,' 'because they are sons of God' (Matthew 5:9). To be peaceful is to be sons of God. And he said 'peacemakers' to mean those making peace. When they lead those who have been divided by intention into harmony and friendship, they are peacemakers. And they are peacemakers toward themselves also.

First, having made peace within themselves, so that they do not have fighting thoughts or works within themselves, then they made peace in themselves. And they carry this peace also to others; for they want those being taught to be as they themselves are. They teach to make peace between the soul and the body and the body and the soul; for when the soul 'subdues the body and brings it into subjection,' and the soul rules and the body is ruled, it is a peace of body and soul. Just as they constructed peace within themselves, so they do this toward others who are beloved and loving, or even toward those fighting. Because of this, it is also said in the Didache, the book of instruction: 'You shall make peace with those who fight.' He who brings others who are fighting into peace and social dealings has first made peace himself; he has no strife within himself, he has no fighting thoughts.
21 And they opened their mouths against me. They opened their word against me, speaking peaceably. But their mind was groaning under the deceit.

Being led to the same end, not in a praiseworthy way, but so as to lose one's own virtues. This is also possible: 'they spread [the lie] against me' (Ps 50:21), as they spoke peaceably, but while calculating deceits in anger, they thought I was being deceived. Then they began to flatter and to spread their word against me.

You have such symbols in history: Delilah, who was brought in the book of Judges (Judg 16), a prostitute, was plotting with deceits to have Samson brought, so that she might give him to the other nations who wished to kill him. And she was saying: 'In what weakness will your strength be, or in what way will you become as weak as one of the hundred and forty men?' She was not telling him the truth. Then, having thought that he believed, she bound him and did other things, and as she was cutting his hair, she was saying: 'Other nations against you, Samson.' See, she spread the mouth [the lie] against him. Formerly she spoke peaceably, she was flattering. But when it seemed that she had caught him within her snare, as one cutting hair, she was saying: 'Other nations against you, Samson.' And behold, she who formerly spoke peaceably and calculated deceits in anger, when it seemed he had become self-controlled, spread the mouth [the lie] while now acting grandiosely.

'Well done, well done, our eyes have seen' (Ps 50:21). Those who think they have obtained the hand they wanted, thus they speak: 'Well done, well done, what we wanted, our eyes have not seen; we no longer see you as you were supposed to be, but as we desired. We have found you easy to capture.'

'You have seen, Lord, do not remain silent' (Ps 50:22). The 'do not remain silent' is the 'do not long-suffer any longer' (Ps 50:23); for from many words we showed this: 'I was silent from eternity, shall I also be silent forever?' (Ps 50:24). I was long-suffering, I did not go out against the evils being done. This shall not be forever. Goodness is again known by the one threatening the one already being punished, so that through the threat he may be stirred up and be brought to repentance. And in another psalm he says: 'To the sinner God said: Why do you declare my judgments and take up my words through your lips? But you hated instruction' (Ps 51:16). Then at the end: 'Having done these things, and I was silent'—not going out—'you assumed lawlessness, that I would be like you' (Ps 51:20). But long-suffering does not remain always; for 'I will convict' 'you and present against your face' your sins. And therefore the threats of God happen out of much goodness.

english: The title 'Judge' is introduced alongside 'the righteous'. 22 Lord, do not turn away from me. May such a thing not be done to me, that I should turn away from you, you who are the helper, the protector. For God distances himself from the wicked, just as he draws near to those approaching. For the great apostle James writes, 'Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you' (James 4:8). It is as if you were saying even to the wicked, 'Draw near to virtue, and it draws near to you.' We do not receive the presence of God in a place, but in relationship and disposition.

23 Arise, O Lord, and attend to my judgment. The voice is one of boldness. No one being accused concerning adultery or murder or anything else says to God, 'Arise, and attend to my judgment'; for you know that the attention of the judgment will condemn him. Therefore, the voice 'attend to my judgment' is one of speaking with boldness regarding cleanliness and regarding being blameless. 'Attend to my judgment,' [he says], 'examine that which is against me and that which is against them, and that which they say against me in vain, that they are hating me without cause.' Often 'Arise' signifies a stirring up. For we often say, 'Arise this man so that he may pay attention to himself,' and it does not signify a physical bodily form. If, however, you wish it as from sleep, it is said, 'Arise; why do you sleep, Lord?' God sleeps not, wishing to pass by unobserved. Therefore, this does not speak maliciously, but wishes to learn the cause, since your wisdom does nothing by chance. Even if you are patient, even if you withhold the punishment, even if you do not cast down those laying hands on me unjustly, tell me the cause; for thus, having known the cause, a wise person will be even more patient and will endure even more. 23 My God and my Lord, unto my judgment. You, and my God and my Lord, arise for me unto the judgment, judge me. He does not pray for his enemies to suffer evil; for the prayer of one holy who loves his enemies is that those enemies should no longer be enemies, that they should no longer be such people. It seems, however, to signify the punishment. For punishment is...

For the lover of pleasure, to become outside of pleasures; for the uncontrolled, to become far from self-control. He wishes them to perish because they are such. And this, however, is not for everyone to say: 'God' therefore 'and my Lord'; for he who does what he says to Him truly calls the Savior 'Lord'; for he says: 'Why do you call me, Lord, Lord, and do not do what I say?' (Luke 6:46). And again: 'They acknowledge God, but deny Him by their works' (Titus 1:16).

The saints call God 'God' not by mere voice, but having been made intimate with Him and serving Him like priests, becoming healers. But they also serve Him by doing His will; for 'not everyone' 'who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven' (Matthew 7:21). He is called 'God' in the sense that He is Creator: 'In the beginning' 'God made the heaven and the earth' (Genesis 1:1). Thus it is also said, 'God of spirits and of all flesh,' according to the creation. But otherwise He is called 'God' of the saints, according to worship. In this way, God of the patriarchs has been said. And according to creation, as was being signified, He was God of all, of all things which He has made. And again, He is Lord of all, being to them the very being and governing them under His providence. But in another way, He is Lord of those doing His will, of those practicing what was commanded, and as a master to slaves. 'Judge me, Lord, according to Your righteousness' (Psalm 7:9). 'According to Your righteousness judge me.'

It seems again that what is said exceeds and contradicts with other words. But the difference is not made by the meaning, but by the voice. 'He shall not be justified,' he says, 'before You every living thing,' instead of 'no living thing.' And he says 'living' meaning living according to soul, most rightly; not 'before You.' As if they are nothing toward You. Just as you would say also concerning lamps, that they do not shine before the sun. But this does not indicate that they do not shine.
