"μὴ παρασιωπήσῃς" οὖν, ἀλλ' ἐπινεύσας δὸς ἃ ᾐτησάμην· ἡ γὰρ παρασιώπησις ἐνίοτε μελλησμὸν καὶ μακροθυμίαν σημαίνει, ἐνίοτε δὲ καὶ μακροθυμίαν, ὅταν ἐπὶ ἁμαρτήμασιν γίνηται· "ταῦτα ἐποίησας, καὶ ἐσίγησα". ἀντὶ τοῦ "οὐκ ἀνταπέδωκά σοι". εἰ ἤμην κάτοικος, οὐδὲ ἐτόλμων αἰτήσασθαι καὶ προσεύξασθαι. κάτοικοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ ὑπεύθυνοι κακίᾳ καὶ ἀσεβεία. λέγεται γοῦν ἐν Ἰηρεμίᾳ· "ἀπὸ προσώπου βορρᾶ ἐκκαυθήσεται τὰ κακὰ ἐπὶ τοὺς κατοικοῦντας τὴν γῆν". οὐκ "ἐπὶ τοὺς παροικοῦντας". καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀποκαλύψει Ἰωάννου τρὶς ἑξῆς λέγεται· "οὐαὶ οὐαὶ οὐαὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς κατοικοῦντας τὴν γῆν". εἰ ἤμην 191 οὖν κάτοικος, οὐκ ἂν εἶπον· "μὴ παρασιωπήσῃς". 13 καὶ παρεπίδημος καθὼς πάντες οἱ πατέρες μου. ὁ πάροικος καὶ παρεπίδημος αὐτός ἐστιν. Παῦλος γοῦν ἐν τῇ κατ' Ἑβραίους ἐπιστολῇ κατάλογον ποιησάμενος πάντων τῶν διὰ πίστεως εὐαρεστησάντων εἶπεν αὐτοὺς παροίκους καὶ παρεπιδήμους. οὐδεὶς ἐκείνων κάτοικος, οὐδεὶς ἔνδημός ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ παρεπίδημος. ἄλλοθεν ἐλήλυθεν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦτον, οὐχ ὧδε γεγέννηται. οἱ κατὰ ἀρετὴν πατέρες οὖν πάντες πάροικοι ἦσαν ἐν τῇ γῇ καὶ παρεπίδημοι, ὡς οἱ πατριάρχαι κ̣αὶ ἄλλοι γεννήσαντες κατὰ θείαν παίδευσιν, οἷον προφῆται, διδάσκαλοι, νομοθέται. 14 ἄνες μοι, ἵνα ἀναψύξω πρὸ τοῦ με ἀπελθεῖν καὶ οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ ὑπάρξω. ἀνάψυξιν ὧδε ἐπαινετὴν λέγει τὴν ἰσοδυναμοῦσαν τῇ· "κατατρύφησον τοῦ κυρίου". "εὗρον ἀναψυχὴν ἐμαυτῷ", λέγει ὁ Ἐφρέμ. ἐκείνη δὲ ψεκτή ἐστιν ἡ ἀναψυχή. ἀναψύχει οὖν τις ἐπαινετῶς, ὅταν τῆς ἀρετῆς ἀπολαύῃ, ὅταν "κατατρυφήσῃ τοῦ κυρίου", ὅταν ἔνφασιν καὶ ἔννοιαν λάβῃ τοῦ "παραδείσου τῆς τρυφῆς". ἐπεὶ τοίνυν λείπει μοι πολλά–διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ δέησιν ἀναπέμπω, ἵνα τῶν λειπόντων π̣ληρωθῶ· τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ ψαλμοῦ εἶπεν· "γνώρισόν μοι, κύριε, τὸ πέρας μου καὶ τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν ἡμερῶν μου, τίς ἐστιν, ἵνα γνῶ τί ὑστερῶ ἐγώ". ὅταν γνῷ τὰ ὑστεροῦντα καὶ ταῦτα κτήσηται, ταῦτα γεωργήσ̣ιμα σχῇ, ἀναψύχει. τοῦτο οὖν λέγει ὅτι· ἄνες μοι μένειν ἐν τῇ ζωῇ ταύτῃ, ἵνα παιδευθεὶς ἀναψύξω, πρ̣ὶν̣ ἀπέλθω̣ ἐκ τοῦ βίου τούτου καὶ οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ ὑπάρξω. οὐ τοῦτο λέγει ὅτι· "οὐχ ὑπ281 άρξω", ἀλλὰ τοιοῦτος, οἷος βούλομαι εἶναι· οὐ γὰρ εἰς ἀνυπαρξίαν χωρεῖ ἡ ψυχή, ἀλλὰ ἄκουε· καταλλήλως τοῖς λέγουσιν ἐκλαμβάνειν δεῖ τοὺς λόγους. ἐὰν ὁ δίκαιος λέγῃ καὶ ὁ σοφὸς κατὰ θεόν· "πάντα σπουδάζω ἵνα πλουτήσω", μὴ περὶ τὸν αἰσθητὸν πλοῦτον ἐκλάμβανε τὸ λεγόμενον. ἐὰν δὲ ἄλλος ᾖ τις ἢ πραγματευτὴς ἢ ἰατρὸς . καὶ οὗτος οὖν ὁ ἅγιος σοφός ἐστιν. λέγει γοῦν "οὐκ ἄλλον ἔχειν ὑπομονὴν ἢ τὸν κύριον καὶ τὴν ὑπόστασιν παρ' αὐτοῦ". οὗτος οὖν ὁ σοφὸς κἂν τοῦτο λ̣έγῃ ὅτι· ἄνες με ζῆν ἠλπικότα ἐν ταύτῃ μόνῃ τῇ ζωῇ, ἵνα ἀναψύξω φαγὼν καὶ πιὼν κατὰ τό· "φάγωμεν καὶ πίωμεν, αὔριον γὰρ ἀποθνῄσκομεν", ἀλλὰ κατάλληλον τῷ προσώπῳ καὶ τὴν ἀναψυχὴν δεῖ λαβεῖν καὶ τὸ "ἄνες μοι" καὶ τὸ "μηκέτι ὑπάρχειν". ἀθάνατός ἐστιν ὁ λέγων. ἐὰν οὖν λέγῃ· "οὐκέτι ὑπάρξω", οὐ τοῦτο λέγει ὅτι· "εἰς τὴν παντελῆ φθορὰν χωρῶ, εἰς ἀνυπαρξίαν καταστρέφω", ἀλλά· "οὐκέτι ὑπάρχω οὕτως ὡς εὔχομαι ὑπαρχθῆνα̣ι̣". "πρὸ τοῦ με" οὖν "ἀπελθεῖν" οὕτως, ἀπελθεῖν τοῦ βίου, "καὶ οὐκέτι ὑπάρξω" ὡς ηὐξάμην γενέσθαι. ἐὰν λέγῃ ἁμαρτωλὸς ὅτι· "νουθέτησόν με, παίδευσόν με, ἵνα μηκέτι ὑπάρξω"–μὴ γὰρ ἵνα εἰς τὴν παντελῆ φθορὰν χωρήσῃ. 1–2 εἰς τὸ τέλος· τῷ ∆αυὶδ ψαλμός. ὑπομένων ὑπέμεινα τὸν κύριον, καὶ προσέσχεν μοι. ὁ προ̣κ̣είμενος ψαλμὸς ῥηθείη ἂν καὶ ὑπὸ παντὸς ἁγίου τοῦ καρτερῶς καὶ μεγαλοψύχως διαγαγόντος τὸν βίον καὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοῦ κυριακοῦ· λέξεις γὰρ ἀπ' αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀπόστολος λαβὼν ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ἑβραίους περὶ Χριστοῦ αὐτὰς ἐξε̣ίληφεν εἰρημένας. αὐτὸ τοῦτο ὅλως· "θυσίαν καὶ προσφορὰν οὐκ ἠθέλησας", ἕως· "ἐν κεφαλίδι βιβλίου γέγραπται περὶ ἐμοῦ". ἐστὶν δὲ μονοπρόσωπος ὁ ψαλμός. τὸ αὐτὸ πρόσωπον τὸ ἀρξάμενον μέχρι τοῦ τέλους τοῦ ψαλμοῦ ἀπαγγέλλει καὶ ψάλλει. λέγει οὖν εὐχαριστικῶς πρὸς τὸν θεόν· "ὑπομένων ὑπέμεινα τὸν κύριον, καὶ εἰσήκουσεν τῆς δεήσεώς μου". τὸ "ὑπομένων ὑπέμεινα" τοιαύτην ἔχει διάνοιαν, ὡς εἴ τις λέγοι· "ἰατρικῶς ἰάτρευσα, γραμματικῶς ἔγραψα". εἰσὶν ὑπομένοντες οὐχ ὑπομενητικῶς, ἀλλὰ ἢ ὑπὸ πολλῆς ἀναισθησίας ἢ ἐνίοτε διὰ φιλοδοξίαν. λέγει γοῦν ὁ ἀπόστολος· "οὐ μὴ παραδῶ τὸ σῶμά μου ἵνα καυχήσωμαι". ἕνεκα ἐπαίνου
english: unspoken and glorified. 'Do not disregard me, for I am a sojourner in this land.' Do not disregard me while I am praying, entreating, weeping, and bearing tears—such things as 'those who sow in joy shall reap.' Therefore, 'do not disregard me,' but having responded, give what I have requested; for disregard sometimes signifies delay and patience, and sometimes indeed patience, when it occurs regarding sins: 'having done these things, I was silent' (Psalm 39:8), instead of 'I have not repaid you.' If I were an inhabitant, I would not have dared to ask and to pray. For the inhabitants are those responsible for wickedness and impiety. For it is said in Jeremiah: 'from the face of the north shall the evils be burned upon those inhabiting the land' (Jeremiah 50:39), not 'upon those sojourning.' And in the Revelation of John, it is said three times: 'woe, woe, woe upon those inhabiting the land' (Revelation 18:7). If I were, therefore, an inhabitant, I would not have said, 'do not disregard me.'

And I am a stranger just as all my fathers were. The sojourner and the stranger are one and the same. For Paul, having made a list of all those who were well-pleasing through faith in the Epistle to the Hebrews, called them sojourners and strangers (Hebrews 11:13). None of them is an inhabitant, none is a native, but a stranger. He has come from elsewhere into this place; he was not born here. Therefore, all the fathers according to virtue were sojourners in the land and strangers, such as the patriarchs and others who produced according to divine instruction, such as prophets, teachers, and lawgivers.

Refresh me, so that I may find refreshment before I depart and no longer exist. Here, refreshment is called praiseworthy, being equivalent to 'delighting in the Lord.' 'I found refreshment for myself,' says Ephrem. And that refreshment is a slight thing. One refreshes praiseworthily when he enjoys virtue, when he 'delights in the Lord,' when he perceives and receives the understanding of the 'paradise of delight.' Since, therefore, much is lacking to me—for this is why I send up a petition, so that I may be filled of the things lacking—for this also he said at the beginning of the Psalm: 'Lord, make known to me my end and the number of my days, what it is, so that I may know what I lack' (Psalm 39:4). When he knows the things that are lacking and acquires these, he finds refreshment through such possessions. Therefore, he says: refresh me to remain in this life, so that having been instructed, I may [be refreshed]...

I shall refresh myself before I depart from this life and no longer exist. He does not say, 'I shall not begin to be,' but rather, 'I shall be such a person as I desire to be'; for the soul does not move into non-existence. Listen, accordingly, to what is said to people: one must take the words in their proper sense. If the righteous man or the wise man says according to God, 'I strive for all things so that I may become rich' (cf. Prov 28:20), do not take what is said to mean material wealth. But if someone else were a rhetorician or a physician—and this one is therefore a holy wise man—he says, 'I have no other endurance except the Lord and the subsistence from Him.'

Thus, if this wise man says, 'Let me live most hopefully in this only life, so that I may refresh myself having eaten and drunk according to: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die' (Luke 12:19), one must take the refreshment appropriately to the person, both the 'let me' and the 'no longer to be.' He who says this is immortal. Therefore, if he says, 'I shall no longer be,' he does not say, 'I move into complete destruction, I turn into non-existence,' but rather, 'I shall no longer be in the way that I desired to have been.' If a sinner says, 'Admonish me, discipline me, so that I may no longer be'—for it is not so that he may move into complete destruction.

1–2 unto the end; the Psalm of David: 'Waiting, I waited upon the Lord, and He attended to me' (Ps 40:1). The preceding Psalm could have been spoken by any saint who has lived his life with patience and magnanimity, and by the Lord's man; for the Apostle, taking words from it, has set forth in the Epistle to the Hebrews concerning Christ those things having been said. This is the whole: 'A sacrifice and an offering You did not desire' (Heb 10:5), until: 'It is written about me in the head of a book' (Ps 40:7). And the Psalm is single-personed. The same person who began announces and sings until the end of the Psalm. He therefore says thankfully to God: 'Waiting, I waited upon the Lord, and He heard my prayer.' The 'waiting, I waited' has such a meaning as if someone were to say, 'I healed medically, I wrote grammatically.' They are waiting, not in a manner of mere waiting, but either through much insensitivity or sometimes through ambition. For the Apostle says: 'I will not deliver my body so that I may boast' (1 Cor 9:27), because of praise.

source_text: ἐπιπροεὶς ιν τὸ σῶμα καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν οὐχ "ὑπομένων ὑπέμεινεν"· ἀεὶ γὰρ 192 ἐπιστημόνως καὶ ὡς ἔδει ὑπέμεινεν, οὐχ ἵνα θήραν ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων δέξηται ἢ δόξαν ἢ ἐπαίνους. ὁ οὖν οὕτως ὑπομένων ὡς δεῖ, ὡς ἐὰν λέγω ὅτι· "κατὰ σοφίαν σοφῶς ἐποίησα". ἐλέχθη ἐν τῷ προλαβόντι ψαλμῷ ὁ θεὸς ὑπομονὴ εἶναι τοῦ δικαίου· "καὶ νῦν τίς ἡ ὑπομονή μου; οὐχὶ ὁ κύριος"; ὁ ἀπὸ ταύτης τῆς ὑπομονῆς τλητικῶς φέρων τὰ προσπίπτοντα ἐπίπονα ἐρεῖ· "ὑπομένων ὑπέμεινα τὸν κύριον". σὺν διαθέσει ὑπομονητικῇ καὶ τὰ ἐπίπονα ἤνεγκα· πολλοὶ γάρ, ὡς εἶπον, τὰ ἐπίπονα φέρουσιν διά τι. ἐστὶν οὖν̣ ὁ θεὸς ὑπομονὴ τοῦ ἁγίου. καὶ ἐν Ἰηρεμίᾳ γοῦν λέγεται· "θρόνος δόξης ὑψούμενος ἁγίασμα ἡμῶν, ὑπομονὴ Ἰσραήλ, κύριε τοῦ Ἰσραήλ". ὁ τοίνυν κατὰ ταύτην τὴν ὑπομονὴν πεποιωμένος καὶ παρονομαζόμενος ἀπ' αὐτῆς ἐρεῖ· "ὑπομένων ὑπέμεινα τὸν κύριον". ὡς δοῦλος λαλεῖ. ὁ δουλεύων τῷ θεῷ "κύριον" αὐτὸν δι' αὐτῶν τῶν πράξεων καὶ τῶν φρονημάτων καὶ τῶν λόγων ὁμολογεῖ. οὗτος "ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ κύριον Ἰησοῦν" λέγει· οὐδὲ γὰρ πᾶς ὁ ὀνομάζων τὸν Ἰησοῦν κύριον ἐν πνεύματι τοῦτο ποιεῖ. καὶ ὑποκριταὶ γοῦν τοῦτο ποιοῦσιν. "πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· κύριε κύριε". καὶ τί λέγει αὐτοῖς; "οὐδέποτε ὑμᾶς ἔγνων". οὐδέποτε ἔγνων δουλεύσαντάς μοι. καὶ πάλιν· "τί με λέγετε κύριε κύριε, καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω"; ὁ τοίνυν οὕτω κύριον Ἰησοῦν καλῶν τῷ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ ποιεῖν τοῦ οὐρανίου, ε᾿̣κεῖνος "ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ" κύριον αὐτὸν καλεῖ. δούλου οὖν ἐστιν ἡ φωνή. 2 καὶ εἰσήκουσεν τῆς δεήσεώς μου. ἐνλιπὴς ὢν̣ ᾐτ̣ου´̣μ̣ην τινά, καὶ προσχὼν ὁ θεὸς τῇ δεήσει μου πεπλήρωκεν ταῦτα. ἐπεί περ "ὑπομένων ὑπέμεινα ····· ·χ̣··κ̣··ν̣· τη`̣ν ἐντολὴν περὶ ἧς ὁ σωτὴρ 282 ἔλεγεν· "ὁ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος, οὗτος σωθήσεται". καταπαύ σαντος δέ ἐστιν τὸ "ὑπέμεινα". ἐπερ · καὶ ποῖον εἶχεν ὁ κύριος πρόσωπον; – μὴ γὰρ ἐξ ἀνάγκης εἰρήκαμεν. ἐὰν οὖν ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ σωτῆρος λαμβάνῃς–μέχρι γὰρ προπαθείας γέγονεν, οὐ γέγονεν ἐν πάθεσιν. "ἤρξατο" γοῦν Ἰησοῦς "θαμβεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν". μέχρι ἀρχῆς γέγονεν αὐτῷ τὰ τοιαῦτα. προπάθεια̣ν οὐ λέγομεν ἐν ἀτρέπτῳ γίνεσθαι· οὐ λέγομεν γάρ τινα ἄλλον ἄτρεπτον παρὰ τὴν τριάδα. ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ἡ ψυχή, ἣν ἀνέλαβεν Ἰησοῦς, ἄλλη ἐστὶν παρὰ τὴν τριάδα, πέφυκεν δέχεσθαι προπάθειαν καὶ ἀρχὴν τοῦ θαμβεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν. καὶ λ̣έγω̣ ἀποστολικόν· "ἀντὶ τῆς προκειμένης χαρᾶς ὑπέμεινεν σταυρὸν αἰσχύνης καταφρονήσας". εἰ μὴ γέγονεν ἀλύσ̣κων ἐν προπαθείᾳ, οὐκ ἦν ἀνδραγάθημα οὐδὲ ἆθλον. ἐπερ · τὸ "προσέσχεν μοι"; –ἀντὶ τοῦ "ἐπένευσεν". 3 καὶ ἀνήγαγέν με ἐκ λάκκου ταλαιπωρίας καὶ ἀπὸ πηλοῦ ὕλεως. ἐὰν ἕκαστος τῶν ἁγίων τοῦτο λέγῃ, "λάκκον ταλαιπωρίας" τὸν περὶ γῆν τόπον λέγει· λάκκος γάρ ἐστιν, ὅπου συνστρέφεται τὰ ὕδατα τὰ ὑψόθεν πίπτοντα. πολλαχοῦ οὖν τῶν θείων γραφῶν καὶ ὁ περὶ γῆν τόπος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ σημαίνεται· ὅταν γὰρ ἐν τῷ εἰκοστῷ ἐνάτῳ ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ σωτῆρος κατὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον λέγηται· "ἔσωσάς με ἀπὸ τῶν καταβαινόντων εἰς λάκκον". οὐδὲ γὰρ καταβαίνω ἐγὼ ε̣ἰς̣ λ̣άκ̣κον. ἄλλων ἕνεκα ἐκεῖ γέγονα. οὐκ ἄλλος με κατεβίβασεν. ἔτι δὲ ἐναργέστερον τοῦτο φαίνεται ἐκ τοῦ· "προσελογίσθην μετὰ τῶν καταβαινόντων εἰς λάκκον, ἐγενήθην ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀβοήθητος ἐν νεκροῖς ἐλεύθερος". οὔκ εἰμι τω῀̣ν ἀγομένων εἰς τὸν λάκκον, ἀλλὰ "προσελογίσθην". ἐκείνοις ἐμαυτὸν προσελόγισα. "ἐγενόμην" οὖν "ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀβοήθητος". οὐκ ἀβοήθητος ὢν γέγονεν ὡς ἀβοήθητος· ὅτε γὰρ ἦλθον ἐπὶ τῷ συνλαβεῖν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι, εἰ μὴ ἑαυτὸν ἐκδεδώκειν, οὐκ ἠδύναντο αὐτὸν λαβεῖν. εἰ "ἐν νεκροῖς ἐλεύθερός" ἐστιν, οὔκ ἐστιν τῶν κατὰ φύσιν εἰς τὸν ᾅδην γινομένων διὰ προαίρεσιν καὶ πρᾶξιν, ἀλλ' ἑαυτὸν εἰς τοῦτο προσελογίσατο. "ἀνήγαγέν με" οὖν "ἐκ λάκκου ταλαιπωρίας". ὁ ὑπωπιάσας τὸ σῶμα ἑαυτοῦ καὶ δουλαγωγήσας καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς περιπατῶν ἔτι ἐν οὐρανοῖς κτησάμενος τὸ πολίτευμα, ἐκεῖνος ἀνήχθη ἀπὸ λάκκου ταλαιπωρίας καὶ ἀπὸ πηλοῦ ὕλεως. καὶ νῦν μὲν δυνάμει 193 ἀνήχθη ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τῆς ὕλης καὶ τοῦ πηλοῦ, ἀφ' οὗ πέπλασται τὸ σῶμα πήλινον. "καὶ ἔπλασεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον χοῦν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς". καὶ ἔτι ὁ Ἰὼβ λέγει· "μνήσθητι ὅτι πηλόν με ἔπλασας". ταῦτα δὲ λέξει καὶ Ἰησοῦς κατὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον· γέγονα εἰς τὸν λάκκον τῆς ταλαιπωρίας, συνελογίσθην, ἵνα αὐτοὺς τῆς ταλαιπωρίας ἐλευθερώσω καὶ ἀπὸ πηλοῦ ὕλεως· δι' αὐτοὺς γὰρ εἰς τὸν πηλὸν τῆς ὕλεως γέγονα.
english: He does not merely say 'having endured, I remained' as if to please the body and soul; rather, he endured with knowledge and as was necessary, not to receive a prize, glory, or praise from men. To endure thus is to say, as I might say, 'I acted wisely according to wisdom.' It was said in the preceding psalm that God is the endurance of the righteous: 'And now, what is my endurance? Is it not the Lord?' (Psalm 70:5). He who bears the heavy things falling upon him through this endurance says, 'Having endured, I remained with the Lord.' He bore the heavy things with an enduring disposition, for many, as I have said, bear the heavy things for some [other] reason. God is therefore the endurance of the holy. And in Jeremiah it is indeed said: 'A throne of glory rising, our holiness, endurance of Israel, Lord of Israel' (Jeremiah 33:16). He who is therefore established according to this endurance and is named from it says, 'Having endured, I remained with the Lord,' speaking as a slave. He who serves God calls him 'Lord' through his deeds, his mindsets, and his words. This one says, 'In the Holy Spirit, Lord Jesus'; for not everyone who calls Jesus Lord does so in this Spirit, but hypocrites indeed do this. Many will say to me on that day, 'Lord, Lord' (Matthew 7:21-23), and what does he say to them? 'I never knew you.' I never knew you having served me. And again: 'Why do you call me Lord, Lord, and do not do what I say?' (Matthew 7:23). Therefore, he who calls Jesus thus Lord, doing the will of his Father in heaven, is the one who calls him 'in the Holy Spirit' Lord. The voice is therefore that of a slave.

And he heard my prayer. Being in distress, I cried out, and God, attending to my prayer, has fulfilled these things. For I 'having endured, I remained' [obeyed] the commandment concerning which the Savior said, 'He who endures to the end, this one will be saved' (Matthew 24:13). The 'I remained' is a state of having come to rest. And what kind of face did the Lord have? For we have not spoken out of necessity. If, then, you take it from the face of the Savior—for it has become a matter of pre-passion, it has not become a matter of passions—Jesus 'began to be amazed and distressed' (Mark 14:33). Such things happened to him until the beginning. We do not say that pre-passion occurs without disturbance; for we do not say that anyone other than the Trinity is without disturbance.

For the soul, which Jesus took up, is something other than the Trinity; it is of a nature to receive passion and the beginning of being terrified and distressed. And I say according to the apostles: 'Instead of the joy set before him, he endured the cross, despising shame' (Heb 12:2). If it had not become a victor in passion, it would not have been a feat or a contest.

Furthermore: the 'pay attention to me' [is] instead of 'he sighed'. And he brought me up out of the pit of misery and from the clay of matter. If each of the saints says this, 'the pit of misery' refers to the place concerning the earth; for a pit is a place where the waters falling from above gather. Often, in the divine writings, both the place concerning the earth and Hades are signified by this name; for when in the twenty-ninth [Psalm] it is said according to the man: 'You have saved me from those going down into the pit' (Ps 29:15), I do not myself go down into a pit. Because of others, I have been there. No one else brought me down.

Moreover, this appears more clearly from: 'I was counted among those going down into the pit; I became as a helpless man among the dead, yet free' (Ps 29:15). I am not one of those being led into the pit, but I 'was counted'. I counted myself among those. Therefore, I 'became' 'as a helpless man'. Not being helpless, he became as helpless; for when the Jews came to seize him, if he had not delivered himself, they would not have been able to take him. If he is 'free among the dead', he is not one of those becoming [members] of Hades by nature through choice and action, but he counted himself into this.

Therefore, he 'brought me up' 'from the pit of misery'. He who humbled his own body and enslaved it, and while still walking upon the earth, having acquired his citizenship in the heavens, he was lifted up from the pit of misery and from the clay of matter. And now indeed he was lifted up in power from the world and from matter and from the clay, from which the clay body has sailed. 'And God formed man from dust from the earth' (Gen 2:7). And even Job says: 'Remember that you formed me of clay' (Job 10:9). And Jesus will also say this according to the man: I have become into the pit of misery, I was counted, so that I might free them from misery and from the clay of matter; for because of them, I have become into the clay of matter.

source_text: ὅταν τοίνυν τὸ σῶμα τοῦτο τὸ φθαρτὸν εἰς ἄφθαρτον μεταβάλῃ, οὐκέτι ὁ περικείμενος αὐτὸ ὑπὸ πηλοῦ κατέχεται καὶ ταλαιπωρίας, ἀλλ' ἐρύσθη ἀπὸ τούτων. 3 καὶ ἔστησεν ἐπὶ πέτραν τοὺς πόδας μου. καὶ περὶ τοῦ καθόλου δικαίου τοῦτο λεγέσθω. "πέτραν" δὲ ἐν τούτοις ἀκουστέον τὸν ἀρραγῆ καὶ ἀδ̣ιαίρετον τ̣οῦ θεοῦ λόγον, ὃν οὐδεμία ζάλη ἢ τρικυμία κινεῖ. πολλαχοῦ οὖν τῶν ἱερῶν λόγων μνήμη πέτρας γίνεται οὐκ ἐπὶ αἰσθήσεως δυναμένη λημφθῆναι· ὅταν γὰρ λέγῃ ὁ ἅγιος εὐχαριστητικῶς πρὸς τὸν θεόν· "ἐν πέτρᾳ ὕψωσέν με", οὐ τοῦτο λέγει ὅτι· "ἐν τῇ αἰσθητῇ πέτρᾳ μετεωρίσας με ἔθηκεν", ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὸν ἀρραγῆ καὶ ἀδιαίρετον λόγον. ἑρμήνευσεν δὲ ταύτην τὴν πέτραν ὁ Παῦλος καὶ εἶπεν τίς ἐστιν, ὅτι ὁ Χριστός· "ἔπινον γὰρ ἐκ πνευματικῆς ἀκολουθούσης πέτρας, ἡ πέτρα δὲ ἦν ὁ Χριστός". καὶ πάλιν ὁ αὐτὸς οὗτος ὑμνῳδὸς μεθ' ἕτερα λέγει· "κατεπόθησαν ἐχόμενα πέτρας οἱ κραταιοὶ αὐτῶν". οἱ τῶν Αἰγυπτίων πλησιάσαντες τῇ πέτρᾳ τὸ οὐδὲν ὤφθησαν. καὶ ὥσπερ "ἡ ῥάβδος ἡ Ἀρὼν κατέπιεν τὰς ῥάβδους" τῶν ἐπαοιδῶν τῶν Αἰγυπτίων̣, τουτέστιν ἐνίκησεν αὐτούς. ὅταν οὖν λέγῃ· "κατεπόθη ὁ θάνατος", "κατεπόθη Ἰσραήλ". ὅταν οὖν ἐνγίσωσιν τῇ πέτ̣ρᾳ οἱ δοκοῦντες εἰ῀̣ναι κραταιοί, σοφισταί, ἐριστικοί τινες ἢ καὶ πνεύματα πονηρά, καταπίνονται, τὸ οὐδὲν ἀποδείκ̣νυντα̣ι̣. ἐπὶ τα̣ύτην οὖν τὴν 283 πέτραν, τὸν Χριστόν, ᾗ πλησιάσαντες οἱ ἐγγίζοντες κραταιοὶ τῶν Αἰγυπτίων καταπίνονται, ἵστανται οἱ τοῦ εὐεργετουμένου πόδες ἐκ τοῦ κλονεῖσθαι καὶ τρικυμίας ὑφίστασθαι καὶ πολεμίους ἔχειν. ἡ ὑπομονὴ γίνεται. οὐκ ἀεὶ δὲ αὐτὰ πάσχει ὅταν ἐν τῷ λάκκῳ τῆς ταλαιπωρίας ἐστίν, ὅτε ἐν τῷ πηλῷ τῆς ὕλεως, ἡ ὑπομονὴ γίνεται. οὐκ ἀεὶ δὲ αὐτὰ πάσχει. ὅταν δὲ τούτων ἐκτὸς γένηται τέλος τῆς ὑπομονῆς λαβούσης, ἵστανται λοιπὸν οἱ πόδες τοῦ εὐεργετηθέντος ἐπὶ τὴν εἰρημένην πέτραν. 3 καὶ κατηύθυνεν τὰ διαβήματά μου. καὶ ὅρα γε ὅτι πόρρω τῆς ἱστορίας ἡμᾶς ὁ λόγος ἀπάγει. οὐδεὶς ἑστηκὼς διαβαίνει, οὐδεὶς διαβαίνων ἕστηκεν̣. ὅταν τις τοίνυν κατὰ Χριστὸν βεβαιωθῇ ὥστ' ἀνειπεῖν· "τίς ἡμᾶς χωρίσει ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ"; τὰς δ̣ιαβάσ̣εις ἔχει κατευθυνομένας· σπεύδει γὰρ ἀεὶ ἐπὶ τὰ ὑπέρτερα, ἐπὶ τὰ οὐράνια κατευθύνοντος τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ διαβήματα τοῦ τρέχοντος· "οὐ" γὰρ "τοῦ θέλοντος οὐδὲ τοῦ τρέχοντος, ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἐλεῶντος θεοῦ". 4 καὶ ἐνέβαλεν εἰς τὸ στόμα μου ᾆσμα καινόν. "εἰς τὸ στόμα" τοῦ ἔσω ἀνθρώπου, τουτέστιν εἰς τὸν λόγον μου. "ᾆσμα καινόν"· πολλάκις ἡμῖν ···τα περὶ καινοῦ, πῶς λέγεται. τὸ ἀδιάδοχον ἀεὶ καινόν ἐστιν, τὸ δὲ διαδεχθὲν παλαιόν. καὶ διὰ πλειόνων παραδειγμάτων πολλάκις ἀποδέδεικται. 4 ὕμνον τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν. ὁ τῷ ὄντι ἀναχθεὶς ἀπὸ τῶν προειρημένων περιστατικῶν τοῦ τε λάκκου τῆς ταλαιπωρίας καὶ τοῦ πηλοῦ τῆς ὕλεως ἀδιάδοχον νίκην ἔσχεν. ·······της ἀδιαδόχου τὸ ἐπινίκιον καινόν ἐστιν. τί δέ ἐστιν τοῦτο τὸ ᾆσμα καινόν, ἑρμηνεύει· "ὕμνος" ἐστὶν "τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν". ὅταν τὸν θεὸν ὑμνῶμεν, ὅταν διάλημψιν αὐτοῦ λάβωμεν, ὡς ἐφικτόν ἐστιν, ἐν τέλει γινόμενοι καινὸν̣ ᾆσμα ᾄδομεν· τὸ γὰρ ἐν τῷ τέλει ἀδιάδοχόν ἐστιν. διὸ καὶ ὁ ὕμνος ὁ ἐν αὐτῷ εὐχαριστητικῶς ἀναπεμπόμενος τῷ θεῷ ᾆσμα καινόν ἐστιν. 4 ὄψονται πολλοὶ καὶ φοβηθήσονται καὶ ἐλπιοῦσιν ἐπὶ κύριον. "ὄψονται πολλοὶ" ἀναχθέντα με ἀπὸ λάκκου ταλαιπωρίας καὶ ἀπὸ πηλοῦ ὕλεως καὶ στάσιν τῶν ποδῶν εἰληφότα ἐν τῇ πέτρᾳ καὶ κατευθυνόμενα τὰ διαβήματά μου καὶ ᾄδοντά με καὶ ὑμνοῦντα, "καὶ φοβηθήσονται" ὥστε καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐλθεῖν εἰς τὴν τοιαύτην ἀγωγήν, "καὶ ἐλπιοῦσιν" 194 ὥστε καὶ αὐτοὶ τυχεῖν τούτων τῶν ἤδη ἐμοὶ ὑπαρξάντων. 5 μακάριος ἀνήρ, οὗ ἐστιν τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου ἐλπὶς αὐτοῦ. ὁ ∆αυὶδ ἔσχεν ποτὲ μονομάχιον πρὸς τὸν Γολιὰ καὶ οὐκ ἤλπισεν οὐκ ἐπ' ἀσπίδι. ὁρᾷς ὅτι τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου ἐλπὶς αὐτοῦ γέγονεν. λέγεται δὲ πρὸς τῷ κυρίως σημαινομένῳ τῆς ἐλπίδος–οὐδὲν δὲ ἕτερόν ἐστιν ἐλπὶς ἢ ἀγαθῶν προσδοκία–πολλάκις καὶ τὰ ἤδη ὑπαρξαντά τινες ἐλπίδια ἑαυτῶν λέγουσιν. οἱ πλούσιοι γοῦν λέγουσιν "τὸ ἐλπίδιόν μου" οὐ τὸ προσδοκώμενον, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἤδη παρόν. καὶ τὸ ὄνομα οὖν τοῦ κυρίου ἤδη ἐλπίδα ὑπάρξασαν ἡγοῦνται οἱ ἤδη αὐτὸ ἔχοντες. 5 καὶ οὐκ ἐπέβλεψεν εἰς ματαιότητας καὶ μανίας ψευδεῖς. ὁ ἐπιβλέψας ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον οὐκ ἐπιβλέπει ἐπὶ ματαιότητας καὶ μανίας ψευδεῖς. οὐκ ἐπιβλέπει ἐπὶ παντε̣υ̣χίαν, οὐκ ἐπὶ μέγεθος σώματος, οὐκ ἐπὶ στρατιωτικῇ χειρί, οὐκ ἐπ' ἄλλῳ τινὶ τῶν δυναμένων ἀποτυγχάνεσθαι. "μανίαι" δὲ λέγονται "ψευδεῖς" αἱ μαντεῖαι. εἰσὶν
english: When this corruptible body is changed into incorruption, it is no longer held by the surrounding mud and distress, but has been rescued from these things. 'And he set my feet upon a rock.' Let this be said generally concerning the righteous. Regarding 'rock,' let the unbroken and indivisible Word of God be heard in these matters, which no storm or tempest moves. Often, indeed, the memory of a rock becomes a memorial of the holy words, not capable of being grasped by sensation; for when the saint says thankfully to God, 'Lift me up on a rock,' he does not say, 'He placed me suspended on a sensible rock,' but upon the unbroken and indivisible Word.

Paul interpreted this rock and said who it is, that it is Christ: 'for they drank from a spiritual following rock, and the rock was Christ' (1 Cor 10:4). And again this same hymnographer says with other things: 'their strong ones laid down the rock they were carrying.' Those of the Egyptians, approaching the rock, were seen as nothing. And just as 'Aaron's rod overcame the rods' (Exod 7:12) of the Egyptians who were singing, that is, he conquered them. When therefore it is said, 'Death is swallowed up' (1 Cor 15:54), 'Israel is swallowed up.' When those who think themselves strong—sophists, certain contentious men, or even evil spirits—approach the rock, they are swallowed up, proving themselves to be nothing.

Upon this rock, Christ, whom the approaching strong ones of the Egyptians are swallowed up by, the feet of the one being benefited stand, to be saved from shaking and tempest and having enemies. Endurance is produced. He does not always suffer these things when he is in the pit of distress, when he is in the mud of matter; endurance is produced. But he does not always suffer these things. When he comes out of these, the end of endurance having been received, the feet of the one having been benefited stand, therefore, upon the said rock. 'And he directed my steps' (Ps 119:133). And see how the Word leads us far into the history. No one standing walks, no one walking stands. When someone is therefore made firm according to Christ so as to be able to say, 'Who shall separate us from the love of God?' (Rom 8:35), his steps have directed paths; for he always hastens toward the higher things, toward the heavenly, being directed by God.

The steps of the runner: for it is 'not of him who wills nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy' (Ps 107:13). And he cast into my mouth a new song (Ps 40:9). 'Into the mouth' of the inner man, that is, into my word. 'A new song': often for us... regarding the new, how it is said. That which is uninterrupted is always new, while that which has been succeeded is old. And through many examples it has often been demonstrated.

A hymn to our God. He who was lifted up from the aforementioned circumstances of the pit of misery and the mire of matter obtained an uninterrupted victory. The victory of the uninterrupted is a new triumph. What is this new song? It explains: it is a 'hymn' 'to our God.' When we hymn God, when we receive His praise, as far as possible, becoming in perfection, we sing a new song; for that which is in perfection is uninterrupted. Therefore also the hymn which is sent up to God thankfully within it is a new song.

Many shall see and shall be afraid and shall hope in the Lord (Ps 37:7). 'Many shall see,' having seen me lifted up from the pit of misery and from the mire of matter, and having my feet established upon the rock, and my steps being directed, and me singing and hymning; 'and they shall be afraid' so that they too might come into such a guidance, 'and they shall hope' so that they too might attain these things which already exist for me.

Blessed is the man whose hope is the name of the Lord (Ps 37:7). David once had a single combat against Goliath and did not hope in a shield. You see that the name of the Lord has become his hope. And it is said regarding the Lord being signified by hope—and there is no other hope than the expectation of good things—that often some say of things already existing, 'my hope.' The wealthy indeed say 'my hope,' not regarding what is expected, but what is already present. And therefore, those who already possess the name of the Lord consider it to be hope.

And he did not look toward vanities and false delusions. He who looks toward the Lord does not look toward vanities and false delusions. He does not look toward wealth, nor toward greatness of body, nor toward military might, nor toward any other of those things which are able to fail. And 'delusions' are called 'false,' the divinations. They are...

source_text: δὲ καὶ μανίαι οὐ ψευδεῖς· οἷον οἱ θεολημπτούμενοι, οἱ χριστολημπτούμενοι θεοφοροῦνται, καὶ οὔκ εἰσιν αὗται αἱ μανίαι ψευδεῖς, ἀλλὰ ἀληθεῖς, ἀντὶ τοῦ "ἡ κατακωχή"· εἰ μὴ γὰρ ἦσαν καὶ ἀληθεῖς μανίαι, οὐκ ἂν ἔλεγεν· "ὁ μὴ ἐπὶ μανίας ψευδεῖς ἐσχηκὼς τὴν ἐλπίδα". οἱ κατὰ Φρύγαν, πῶς ταῦτα λέγεται οὐκ ἠγνοηκότες, καθ' ἓν σημαινόμενον κα̣ὶ τὴν μανίαν καὶ τ̣ὴν ἔκστασιν λαβόντες τοὺς πνευματοφόρους ἄνδρας λέγουσιν ἐν ἐκστάσει λελαληκέναι, πεπροφητευκέναι. καὶ ἀληθεύουσιν μὲν ὅτι κατ' ἔκστασιν, οὐ μέντοι τὴν παραφοράν, οὐ τὴν παραφροσύνη̣ν. ἐὰν γοῦν λέγῃ Παῦλος· "εἴτε ἐξέστημεν, θεῷ", οὐ μανίαν λέγει, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐκστῆναι τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων καὶ ····· 284 ····· ········ δεδωκότα. λέγεται δὲ τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο καὶ ἐπὶ θαυμασμοῦ· "καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐπιστρέψουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἐπιζητήσουσιν κύριον τὸν θεὸν αὐτῶν καὶ ∆αυὶδ τὸν βασιλέα αὐτῶν· καὶ ἐκστήσονται ἐπὶ τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς αὐτοῦ". θαυμασμὸν ὧδε σημαίνει. 6 πολλὰ ἐποίησας σύ, κύριε ὁ θεός μου, τὰ θαυμάσιά σου. πειραθεὶς τῶν εἰρημένων εὐποιιῶν ἐπεὶ μὴ μόνων τούτων τῶν α᾿̣γα̣θῶν ἀπήλαυσεν, ἀλλ' , ἵν' οὕτως εἴπω, μητρόθεν εἰς ταῦτα ἤχθη–καὶ αὐτὴ οὖν ἡ χρίσις αὐτοῦ παιδίου ὄντος παραδόξως γέγον̣εν, καὶ λέγει ὅτι· "πολλὰ ἐποίησας σύ, κύριε ὁ θεός μου, τὰ θαυμάσιά σου". πολλὰ καὶ μεγάλα ἐστίν, "καὶ τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς σου", καθ' οὓς ποιεῖς τὰ θαυμάσια, "οὐδεὶς ὁμοιωθήσεται". οὐδεὶς δυνήσεται τοιαῦτα θαυμάσια ποιῆσαι, οὐδεὶς δυνήσεται ἐξαγαγεῖν τινα ἐκ λάκκου ταλαιπωρίας καὶ ἀπὸ πηλοῦ ὕλεως καὶ στῆσαι τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πέτραν καὶ κατευθῦναι τὰ διαβήματα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ ἄλλα. τὸ "οὐκ ἔστιν τίς ὁμοιωθήσεται" ἐὰν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα λέγηται, οὐ περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ λέγει· οὐδεὶς γὰρ τῶν γενητ̣ῶν ὁμοιωθήσεται. ὁ δὲ υἱὸς οὐχ ὁμοιωθήσεται· ἀίδιος γάρ ἐστιν, εἰκὼν καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς θεοῦ ὑποστάσεως. οὔκ ἐστιν τῶν ἐπὶ μέλλοντι ἔχων τὸ ὁμοιωθῆναι· ὅμοιος γάρ ἐστιν. ἐπερ · τὸ "τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς"; –διαλογισμοὶ κυρίως λέγονται οἱ λογισμοὶ οἱ περὶ τῶν καθέκαστα. ὥσπερ ὁμιλία ἐστὶν ψυχῆς τὸ διαλογίζεσθαι καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν προφορᾷ ἅμα πο̣λλὰ εἰπε̣ῖν, οὕτω καὶ οἱ λογισμοὶ οἱ τῶν καθέκαστα διαλογισμοὶ λέγονται. παραδέδοται τόπος ἐπιχειρηματικὸς ἐρωτῶν, εἰ ταὐτόν ἐστιν τὸ ἐπίστασθαι τῷ διανοεῖσθαι, καὶ εἴρηται, ὅτι οὐ ταὐτόν ἐστιν· πολλὰ μὲν γὰρ ἔστ̣ιν ἄφ̣ν̣ω ἐπίστασθαι, πολλὰ δὲ διανοεῖσθαι οὐχί, ὥστε οὐ ταὐτὸν τὸ ἐπίστασθαι τῷ διανοεῖσθαι. δύναται καὶ ὅλου̣ γένους λαβεῖν ἔννοιαν καὶ ὅλου εἴδους. ἐπιστῆσαι δὲ τοῖς καθέκαστα, ἕκαστον καθ' ἑαυτὸ διανοηθῆναι ἅμα οὐ δύναται. ἐπερ · ἵνα τὸ διανοηθῆναι ἐπὶ τῆς αἰσθήσεως; –ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τῶν καθέκαστα διανοητῶν. ὡς οὐκ ἔστιν ἅμα πολλὰ εἰπεῖν, πολλὰ δὲ εἰδέναι, λόγος δέ τις τῆς ψυχῆς ἐστιν ἡ διάνοια, οὐ δυνατὸν ἅμα πολλὰ διανοεῖσθαι. ὁ θεὸς οὖν διαλογισμοὺς τοιούτους ἔχει ὥστε ἅμα πάντα εἰδέναι, ὅμως δὲ ἑτέρως ἢ ὡς οἱ ἄνθρωποι· καὶ γὰρ ἐν Ἰσαίᾳ εἶπεν ὅτι· "ὡς ἀπέχει ὁ οὐρανὸς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, οὕτω διανοήματα ὑμῶν ἀπὸ 195 τῆς διανοίας μου". τὴν ὑπεροχὴν τῆς ἑαυτοῦ διανοίας ἠθέλησεν ἐξ αἰσθητικοῦ παραδείγματος δεῖξαι· οὐ γὰρ τοπικῶς ἀφέστηκεν ἡ αὐτοῦ διάνοια τῆς διανοίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἀλλὰ μεγέθει ὑπεροχῆς. 6 καὶ τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς σου οὐκ ἔστιν τίς ὁμοιωθήσεται. οὐδεὶς τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁμοιοῦται. ὡς εἰ ἔλεγες· "οὐδεὶς τῇ δημιουργίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ ὁμοιωθήσεται". κἂν γὰρ ὦσιν δημιουργοὶ παρὰ ἀνθρώποις, ἀλλὰ οὐ τὴν ὑποκειμένην ὕλην κατασκευάζουσιν τῶν γινομένων. οἷον ὁ τέκτων ἐὰν ποιῇ κλίνην ἢ θρόνον οὐχὶ καὶ τὸ ξύλον ποιεῖ ἐν τῇ τέχνῃ. τὸ τέλος μόνον ἐπιτίθη̣σιν̣ τῇ π̣ρολαβούσῃ ὕλ̣ῃ. ὁ δὲ θεὸς οὐχ εὑρὼν ὕλην τὸ εἶδος αὐτῇ ἐπιτίθησιν, ἀλλὰ συνυφίστησιν αὐτὴν τῷ εἴδει. 6 ἀπήγγειλα καὶ ἐλάλησα, ἐπληθύνθησαν ὑπὲρ
english: And indeed these manias are not false; for instance, those receiving God or those receiving Christ are god-bearers, and these manias are not false but true, instead of being 'repressed.' For if they were not also true manias, he would not have said: 'he who has had a false hope regarding madness' (1 Cor 6:9). Those according to the Phrygians, not having been ignorant of how these things are said, taking both the meaning of madness and of ecstasy, call the spirit-bearing men as having spoken in ecstasy or having prophesied. And they speak truly regarding ecstasy, but not regarding derangement or insanity.

If indeed Paul says: 'whether we have gone out of our minds, [it is] to God' (1 Cor 6:9), he is not speaking of madness, but of standing outside of human [limits] and... [gap]... having given. And this word is also said regarding wonder: 'And after these things the sons of Israel will turn back and will seek the Lord their God and David their king; and they will be astonished at the Lord and in His good things' (Ps 142:7). He signifies wonder here.

'You have done many things, Lord my God, Your wonders' (Ps 142:5). Having been tested by the doing of the things spoken, since he did not only enjoy these good things, but—so that I may say this—was drawn to these from childhood—and so indeed His anointing while being a child has happened paradoxically, and he says: 'You have done many things, Lord my God, Your wonders.' Many and great things are, 'and with Your thoughts' (Ps 142:4), according to which You do wonders, 'no one shall be like [You].' No one is able to do such wonders; no one is able to bring someone out of the pit of misery and from the mud of matter and set his feet upon a rock and direct his steps and the other things.

The 'there is no one who shall be like' if said in reference to the Father, does not speak concerning the Son; for none of the begotten shall be like [the Father]. But the Son is not [to be] compared; for He is eternal, the icon and character of the divine essence. There is not...

Having the future of becoming like [Him]; for he is like. Regarding: the 'thoughts'? Thoughts are primarily called the thoughts concerning each individual thing. Just as the act of reasoning is a conversation of the soul, and it is not possible to say many things at once, so also the thoughts concerning each individual thing are called thoughts.

A logical place is given for asking whether knowing is the same as reasoning, and it has been said that they are not the same; for there are many things known without reasoning, and many things reasoned about without being known, so that knowing is not the same as reasoning. One is able to grasp a concept of a whole genus and of a whole species. But to know each individual thing, each being reasoned about by itself, it is not possible to do all at once. Regarding: so that the reasoning is upon sensation? But it is upon the individual things being reasoned about. Just as it is not possible to say many things at once while knowing many things, since the intellect is a kind of speech of the soul, it is not possible to reason about many things at once.

God, therefore, has such thoughts that He knows all things at once, yet in a different way than men; for in Isaiah He said: 'As the heavens are far from the earth, so are your thoughts from my thought' (Isaiah 55:9). He wished to show the superiority of His own intellect through a sensory example; for His intellect has not stayed away from the intellect of men locally, but by a greatness of superiority. And with your thoughts no one shall be like. No one is like the thoughts of God. Just as you would say: 'No one shall be like the creation of God.'

For even if they were creators among men, they do not construct the underlying matter of the things coming into being. For example, if a craftsman makes a bed or a throne, he does not make the wood by his art. He only imposes the end upon the previously taken matter. But God, not finding matter, imposes the form upon it, but rather composes it with the form. I have declared and I have spoken, they were multiplied beyond...

english: Regarding number. You know that if we do not conceive something as necessary and do not desire to report it to another, how can we ever say 'thus and thus', when we know that we have not sat down to say what we intended? And this one therefore says: 'I have reported and I have spoken'. Since none of your thoughts is like 'I have reported and I have spoken'. It can also be taken this way: 'I have reported' according to the intention, according to the thought, and 'I have spoken' perceptibly according to the utterance; for first it is necessary to conceive, then thus to speak.

Regarding: 'They were increased beyond number'? —the thoughts, to which none is similar. You did not desire sacrifice and offering. Therefore he says: 'He brought me up out of the pit of misery and out of the mire of filth, having set my feet upon a rock, having directed my steps' (Ps 40:2). How much it was necessary to sacrifice and to offer as a burnt offering to God regarding these Christological words and the even greater benefits! But you did not desire the perceptible burnt offerings, the bodily sacrifices from the slaughter of animals and others, the shadowy ones. 'A body he has prepared for me' (Ps 40:6). Instead of these, the apostle has interpreted that this body is the logical and bloodless sacrifice. When therefore a greater sacrifice is found, then he no longer wants the former; they are no longer desired by him.

Let not the [words] of the Diimorites trouble you; for they say: 'Do you see that [it is] a body'? —for the one saying 'a body he has prepared for me', this he says as 'only'; for even one having a perfect man has a body, but not only. And I said the psalm was one-personed from the beginning; for from the beginning to the end the same speaking person has entered. Just as he said here: 'but a body he has prepared for me', and in the following he says: 'those seeking my soul, let them seek it'. Behold, he has a soul also, behold, he has a body also.

And since the word is concerning the perceptible sacrifices superseded by the Spirit, he spoke of the succeeding sacrifice. It is not the soul that becomes the sacrifice according to this meaning, but the body. And it is also good that [it is not] 'he prepared', but himself 'he has prepared', 'the Holy Spirit having come upon' Mary 'and the power of the Most High having overshadowed her' (Lk 1:35). Because of this, you no longer desired those sacrifices and offerings, since 'a body he has prepared for me' which is to be offered on behalf of all. You did not desire a physical sacrifice and offering, since I have prepared for us a body, which we are able to perform as a sacred rite and sacrifice to you; 'I urge you through mercies to present your bodies as a logical sacrifice' (Rom 12:1). In other [interpretations] it is said: 'And you have prepared ears for me.' One interpreter says this: since you did not desire a sensory sacrifice and offering, 'you have prepared ears for me,' through which I hear those things concerning the things made manifest by the sensory, such as the intellectual sacrifice of understanding: 'sacrifice to God a sacrifice of understanding.' Furthermore, if you call me to a lecture, you no longer seek sensory things being performed, so that what is said might be like: 'The Lord's instruction opens my ears' (Ps 119:16). An unmusical man does not have ears for hearing musical words.

And another of the interpreters said: 'You have dug out ears for me,' since you removed their dullness, you removed that which obstructs hearing. Furthermore: regarding Jesus, how do we receive him? —I said that the 196 allegories are not smoothed out to match the histories. And often I omitted the matter of Abraham and the two women. I said to you that the soul of Jesus is not an unshakeable essence. It is of the same kind as the others, and everything it has that is good, it has from the Word of God. Since therefore it also has the ability to hear well, it has that from the Savior. It surpasses the temple in which it is housed.

7 You did not seek burnt offerings and [things] concerning sin. Nor did you seek, nor did you still delight in the things of the shadow. 'What multitude of your sacrifices to me [is there]? I am full. I do not want the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of lambs' (Ps 50:6). 8 Then he said: 'Behold, I have come' (Isa 6:8). Then I, for whom a body was prepared, said: 'Behold, I have come,' instead of [saying]: since the purpose of his coming is this, to receive the end of the shadow, so that sacrifices and burnt offerings are no longer brought, I have come, in order to fulfill the sacrifice by becoming a burnt offering.

8 It has been written in a heading of a book concerning me. The heading of a book is called 'all inspired Scripture'; for the main point of the Scripture is the life [rule of life] concerning Christ. According to a second account, let it also be said concerning others; for if the coming were not about to happen, the old writings would not have prefigured the Gospel. Furthermore: was this written during the Pentateuch? —He says every Scripture is a book, whose heading is the end for which the writings are given, which is salvation, the coming. "ἀμνός" ἐστιν "τοῦ θεοῦ αἴρων τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου". τὸ λεχθῆναι ὅτι ὁ Ἀδὰμ παρέβη "διὰ παρακοῆς" καὶ ὁ σωτὴρ "δι' ὑπακοῆς" δεδικαίωται, οὐ τὴν ἀναφορὰν ποιεῖται περὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος, ὅς ἐστιν τύπος τοῦ μέλλοντος, ἐπεὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Ἀδὰμ "τύπος τοῦ μέλλοντός ἐστιν"; "τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο μέγα ἐστίν, ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω εἰς Χριστὸν καὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν". ὅτι δὲ οὐ πάντως, εἰ πεν λέγεται βιβλίον, ἐπὶ τῆς αἰσθήσεως δεῖ λαβεῖν αὐτό, ὁ Ἰεζεκιὴλ ἀκούει ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ· "χάνον τὸ στόμα σου", καὶ ὁρᾷ ἐπὶ τῆς θεοῦ χειρὸς βιβλίον, καὶ λέγει ὅτι· "λάβε αὐτὸ καὶ φάγε, καὶ πλησθήσεται ἡ κοιλία σου". τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός, σοὶ καταλιμπάνω τὸ ἀκόλουθον σκοπεῖν. εἰ δὲ κατὰ τὸ μᾶλλον καὶ τὸ ἧττον ἐν θελήμασιν ἐν διαθέσει εὑρίσκεται, ἔσται καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἔχων διάθεσιν καὶ ὁ υἱός, τουτέστιν ποιότητα, καὶ οὕτω καὶ θείαν τροφὴν δέχετ̣αι εἰς ἑαυτήν. μηκέτι θέλοντός σου θυσίαν ἢ προσφορὰν ἢ ὁλοκαυτώματα τὸν πνευματικὸν νόμον τροφὴν ἔσχον. 10 εὐηγγελισάμην δικαιοσύνην ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ μεγάλῃ. english: Therefore, was the world foretold for this reason? So that He might bring the generation of the world to its completion through humans, and after this generation of humans, so that the epidemic might take place. 'Lamb' is 'of God, who takes away the sin of the world' (John 1:29). Regarding the saying that Adam transgressed 'through disobedience' and the Savior 'through obedience' is justified (Rom 5:19), it is not making a comparison concerning the Savior, who is a type of the one to come, since Adam himself 'is a type of the one to come'; 'this great mystery is, and I say it refers to Christ and the Church' (Eph 5:32).

But since it is not entirely, if a book is said to be, it must be taken according to perception; Ezekiel hears from God: 'open your mouth' (Ezek 3:3), and he sees a book upon the hand of God, and says: 'take it and eat, and your belly shall be filled' (Ezek 3:3). 'And I ate', he says, 'and it became sweetness in my belly'. And he says: 'this book is written within and without' (Ezek 3:3). According to the spiritual and intelligible things it is written within, according to the sensible and manifest things without. But the wise man devours both and finds harmony between the symbols and the originals.

And in Isaiah he says again: 'and these words shall be as the words of the book of the sealed, if they give it to a man knowing letters, saying: take, read. He says: I cannot, for it is sealed' (Isa 29:11). And the illiterate man says: 'I do not know letters'. He was asking whether it differed if it were sealed or not sealed. And we take again the God-breathed Scripture, the one knowing letters but unable to read because of the placed seals being the circumcised people, and the one not knowing letters being from the Gentiles.

'To do, O God, your will I have desired' (Ps 40:8). Therefore 'I said: behold, I have come' (Heb 10:7), since the will was desired to do your will after you did not desire me for sacrifice and offering. Those who hold false doctrines concerning Christ say that there are different wills; for even here he says: 'I have come, I desire to do your will', in the Gospel: 'I have descended from heaven not to do human will, but the will of him who sent me' (John 6:38). Therefore, concerning those saying that there are two wills, we say that: the different wills occur either according to more or less or...

In opposition. The one progressing in virtue desires righteousness, and the one perfected [does too], and the will of the perfected is not the same as that of the one progressing or the one being led in. For there becomes either a multitude or a duality of wills according to the more and the less, and it also happens in opposition, when one chooses good things and another evil, and one wills to be saved and another to sin. Therefore, such a will as this, to approach the Son having opposition, is the extreme of impiety.

Furthermore, I also direct [this] toward the Manichaeans. One must act toward these: the will of the Savior is found to be good; for he says, having come down from heaven, 'that I might do the will of God' (John 6:38). And to do the will of God is good. And again: 'The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost' (Luke 19:10). And again: 'If you wish, you are able to cleanse me' (Mark 10:51). If this is the will of the Son, he wills all things that are beneficial. But since the will of the Father is being opposite to him, I leave it to you to consider. If it is found according to the more and the less in wills and in disposition, then both the Father and the Son will have a disposition, that is, a way of acting, and the Father is no longer without body, nor is the essence without connection. Nor is it to be said according to the more and the less, nor in opposition; for the will of the Son is demonstrated to be good. Yet it is not right according to God to say, however, that this is his will, to perfect the will of the Father. It is not right according to God to say [this]. Nor is it opposite, nor according to the more and the less. Therefore, one must take these things regarding the man.

And 'your law in the midst of my belly' (Psalm 119:11). It is spiritual food containing [itself] in the belly of the inner man. And the law, which is evident everywhere, is spiritual food; for it is not sensible food. This belly is often praised, and in the [psalm]: 'From the fear of you in the belly we have received' (Psalm 119:11). And just as this belly receives in the belly from the divine spirit—which is the fear of God—so also it receives divine food into itself. english: Consisting of great things, concerning which Paul says, 'we speak wisdom among the perfect' (1 Cor 2:6), so that the sum of these is a 'great church.' This is not the righteousness according to the law, about which the apostle says, 'having become blameless according to the righteousness in the law' (Rom 3:19). This then righteousness I preached to the great church; for if the letter and the shadow were not preached to the great [ones], but to infants.

But what kind of righteousness? —about which the Savior was saying, 'unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees' (Matt 5:20), is this not according to the shadow? Therefore yours—of the disciples—the Savior says, let the righteousness exceed theirs. And he says that theirs was with ignorance. Because of this, let us not be ignorant of the righteousness of God, but let us preach it.

10 Behold, my lips I will not restrain. 'Lips' here means the word. Often when he is called to say something to small and imperfect men, we restrain our lips; we do not have them released, but we descend with them, we speak cryptically, we speak proverbially, and our lips are restrained. But when to the perfect and a great church, since he does not restrain his lips, since he does not hinder them from speaking anything. And it is possible also to say this: as the [psalmist says]: 'and in his law he will meditate day and night' (Ps 1:2). He never restrains his lips, always bringing forth the words of God. And the 'always' hear it thus: as it is necessary and as it is fitting to do this; for even if he is silent, he speaks in his mind, and even while sleeping, when he sleeps as a righteous man, he does this with the word. And through silence, he remembers something good.

10–11 Lord, you have known my righteousness (Ps 26:3). Since much of what is said has testified to himself—for 'to preach righteousness in a great church' is great and, so that I may say this, beyond man—he says to God: 'you have known my righteousness' (Ps 26:3). This [righteousness], which I announce, I possess and have practiced according to it. And if the psalm were even speaking about the man of the Savior, that: since he did not know sin, but the sin that has come to be, it is productive of righteousness. And this is also possible: even if some, being ignorant, speak blasphemy against me, but you know my righteousness. As also Susanna said: 'you know that...'

What false things testify against me? I have not hidden your truth in my heart. He who has known the righteousness of God does not hide the truth joined to it in his heart. Truth is called joined to righteousness when it says: 'Truth has risen from the earth, and righteousness has stooped from heaven' (Ps 85:11). Regarding the Savior, he says righteousness is stooping from heaven; for he says: 'He bent the heaven and came down.' And 'risen from the earth' means having reached the end of the visitation. But it can also be understood thus: when from the earth, that good and beautiful soul has risen after having heard the word and having been fruitful. Therefore righteousness stoops from heaven. And in another psalm he says: 'Mercy and truth met, righteousness and peace kissed' (Ps 85:10). Those who read histories find that wars and disturbances arise from unrighteousness. But truth has the mercy of God; for if God does not show mercy, no one is able to know the truth, how much and what it is. Therefore 'mercy and truth met.' And mercy is also possible, such as he who loves his neighbor as himself is merciful to his neighbor and himself requires the same mercy from him; for indeed the truth is made manifest. Just as righteousness leads peace, so also the mercy of truth. Moreover, both are one and the same. If then Jesus and his words are ashamed, his truth is ashamed. 'And I have spoken my salvation' (Ps 116:16). The confession of the truth is my salvation. If he also says the truth concerning Christ, he again says Christ is the salvation, and 'I have spoken my salvation and revealed your truth.' I speak of the salvation being the Christ whom I make manifest. 'I have not hidden your mercy and your truth from a great assembly' (Ps 51:1). We say that mercy is joined to the truth. And 'a great assembly' means those from the Gentiles who have believed, having been gathered from all the Gentiles. And the wise man says this, and Jesus also according to the man. 'And you, Lord, do not distance your mercies from me' (Ps 51:1). I have come to your mercies, blamelessly and as is necessary. Do not therefore distance them, so that I may remain such. 'Let the [mercy] quickly overtake us...'
The text ends abruptly with a fragment of a quote.

english: “Your mercies, Lord, for we have become extremely poor” (Ps 51:1). If the mercies are lengthened, poverty occurs. He who is guarded from that from which the mercies did not lengthen is rich; and he is rich in having received the truth and mercy. “Your mercy and your truth have taken hold of me continually” (Ps 51:1). Your mercy and your truth have taken hold of me, the one in need. “Do not lengthen” therefore “your mercies” (Ps 51:1), so that your truth, being taken hold of, and the mercy joined with it, might remain thus.

“For evils surround me, of which there is no number” (Ps 51:8). For this reason, “do not lengthen your mercies from me” (Ps 51:1), because many evils surround me, not falling under number, that is, because of multitude—if the heavy things are signified, because of multitude they do not have a number. But if the other evils, the practical ones about which it is said, “a fool does evils in laughter” (Prov 26:11), they are not in any word or number; for they are not of things that exist, they are thoughts of men, transgressions of divine laws. Therefore, take the double meaning of the evils.

“My iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see” (Ps 51:13). And it is also possible to take it thus: “for evils surround me” (Ps 51:8) not falling under number—as has been said now, in two ways—for this reason: “for my iniquities have overtaken me” (Ps 51:13). But from another beginning it is to be read, joining the “for evils surround me” (Ps 51:8) to “but you, Lord, do not lengthen your mercies from me” (Ps 51:1), “for evils surround me, of which there is no number” (Ps 51:8). Let both then be considered: “your mercy and your truth have taken hold of me continually” (Ps 51:1). Here, therefore, he says this: he calls the habits iniquities, and the iniquities' powers are being brought under. “My iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see” (Ps 51:13); for they are harmful to the eyes of the mind, providing blindness to the inner eye of man. Since, therefore, they have overtaken me, I am not able to see. And these habits can also be taken...

The previous explanation dealt with the active powers. And they themselves, having seized me, pursued and seized me by the hand, and because of this I am not able to see; for the lawlessnesses of the inner man are harmful to the eyes. They were multiplied beyond the hairs of my head (Ps 51:11), and my heart has forsaken me (Ps 31:10). If you wish, these sins, they seize [one] when someone falls by them and sins; for having suffered this, the intellect of the soul is harmed. And if also the active powers of them, they are often called similarly by the name of passion.

“And my heart has forsaken me” (Ps 31:10). Since the lawlessnesses that seized me and removed my sight “were multiplied beyond the hairs of my head” (Ps 51:11), “my heart has forsaken me” (Ps 31:10), I no longer have the heart of a wise man; for the heart of the one saying these things is fleshy. When therefore the fleshy heart forsakes someone, it becomes stony.

“Be pleased, Lord, to save me” (Ps 51:11). Since the lawlessnesses seized [me] and I am not able to see and they were multiplied beyond the hairs of my head (Ps 51:11), “be pleased to save me” (Ps 51:11), so that the heart may not remain forsaken. If the word was about these hairs of this head, he has spoken hyperbolically; for if lawlessnesses occur, they are not able to exceed the number of the hairs of the head. Therefore it is spoken hyperbolically.

But if not, he says this: for the hairs of my head—that is, the unfeeling movements that are not truly fitting to the mind—are hairs; for the unfeeling things in us are also hairs that touch. This therefore he says: having seized my lawlessnesses and being no longer able to see, the hairs of my head were multiplied, the things unfeelingly thought, the things thoughtlessly intended. Because of this my heart, the mind itself, has forsaken me. It is no longer my mind, being dragged down into sin. Lord, to help me.

source_text: πρόσχες. αἰτῶ σε γὰρ εὐδοκῆσαι τοῦ ῥύσασθαι οὐκ ἄλλου χάριν ἢ ἵνα π̣ρόσχῃς τῷ βοηθῆσαί μοι. βοηθεῖς δέ μοι, ἐὰν ἐκτὸς τῶν κρατούντων πολεμίων με ποιήσῃς. 15 καταισχυνθείησαν καὶ ἐντραπείησαν ἅμα οἱ ζητοῦντες τὴν ψυχήν μου τοῦ ἐξᾶραι αὐτήν. ἔλεγον μονοπρόσωπον εἶναι τὸν ψαλμ̣όν. καὶ ἐὰν ἄνθρωπος ᾖν ὁ λέγων, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων δέησιν ἀναπέμπει περί τε τοῦ σώματος καὶ τῆς ψυχῆς. ἐα`̣ν οὖν "ὁ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου υἱός", ὁ ἐκ τῆς Μαρίας προεληλυθὼς ναός, λέγῃ ταῦτα, ἐροῦμεν πρὸς τοὺς λέγοντας σῶμα μόνον ἀνειληφέναι διὰ τοῦ τὸ εἰρῆσθαι· "σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι", –ἰδοὺ καὶ τοῦτο λέγει, τὸ αὐτὸ δὲ πρόσωπόν ἐστιν τὸ ἀπ̣αγγέλλον. ἐντρέπονται καὶ αἰσχύνονται οἱ γνω῀̣σιν λαμβάνοντες τῆς ἀληθείας. 15 ἀποστραφείησαν εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καὶ ἐντραπείησαν οἱ θέλοντές μοι κακά. μέγα πρᾶγμά ἐστιν τὸ τὴν κακίαν εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω ἀποστραφῆναι· τὸ ἔνπροσθεν γὰρ ἐλαύνειν βλαβερόν ἐστιν. "εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω" οὖν "ἀποστραφείησαν" ὡ´̣στε μὴ αὐξῆσαι τὴν ὁδόν, μὴ ἐλάσαι ἐπὶ τὸ χεῖρον. 16 ἐνδυσάσθωσαν παραχρῆμα αἰσχύνην αὐτῶν οἱ λέγοντές μοι· εὖγε εὖγε. ἐστὶν εὐχόμενος περὶ ὧν λέγει "παραχρῆμα", ἵνα̣ μὴ ἐπιμείνωσιν ἐν τῷ κακῷ, ἵνα̣ μὴ ἀδιαλείπτως λέγωσι̣ν· "εὖγε εὖγε εὖγε". ἐπιχαιρεκάκων ἐστὶν λέγειν "εὖγε εὖγε" ἐπ̣ὶ τ̣οῖς παθοῦσιν α᾿̣νάρεστόν τι. 17 ἀγαλλιάσαιντο καὶ εὐφρανθείησαν ἐπὶ σοὶ πάντες οἱ ζητοῦντές σε, κύριε. εἰπὼν πε̣ρὶ τῶν ἐναντίων, ἵν̣α καὶ αἰσχυνθῶσιν καὶ ἐντραπῶσιν καὶ εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω ἀποστραφῶσιν ἐπιχαιρε̣κ̣άκως λέγοντες "εὖγε εὖγε", λέγει· "ἀγαλλιάσαιντο καὶ εὐφρανθείησαν ἐπὶ σοί, κύριε, οἱ ζητοῦντές σε". τότε ἀγαλλιώμε̣θα καὶ εὐφραιν̣όμ̣εθα, ὅταν ζητήσαντες εὕρωμέν σε· ἀγαλλιᾶται γὰρ καὶ εὐφραίνεται ὁ ζ̣η̣τῶν τι, ὅταν αὐτὸ εὕρ̣ῃ. κἂν οὖν ἐπίπονα, κἂν ἄλλα βλάπτοντα 200 ἐπέλθῃ, ζητοῦμέν σε εὑρεῖν βοηθόν. τότε̣ δε`̣ φαινόμενος βοηθεῖς κ̣αὶ λέγεις· "ἔτι σοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐρῶ· ἰδοὺ πάρειμι". 290 17 καὶ εἰπάτωσαν διὰ παντός· μεγαλυνθήτω ὁ κύριος. ἐπεὶ εὑρόντες σε εὐχαριστοῦντες "εἰπάτωσαν διὰ παντός· μεγαλυνθήτω ὁ κύριος", ἔχοιεν ἐκεῖνα τὰ δι' ἃ ὑμνεῖν ὀφείλουσιν καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι. εἰπάτωσαν διὰ παντός δύναται δὲ καὶ τοῦτο· μὴ ὑπάρξοι ποτὲ αὐτοῖς ἀχ̣αριστία. 17 οἱ ἀγαπῶντες τὸ σωτήριόν σου. τὴν δικαίου σωτηρίαν ἢ τὸν αἴτιον αὐτοῖς γινόμενον σωτηρίαν μέλλουσαν. "διὰ παντὸς Μεγαλυνθήτω ὁ κύριος, λεγέτωσαν". ἀγαπῶντες τὸ σωτήριόν σου καὶ μεγαλύνουσιν διὰ παντὸς ἐπ' αὐτῷ τὸν θεόν. 18 ἐγὼ δὲ πτωχὸς καὶ πένης εἰμί· κύριος φροντιεῖ μου. διὰ τοῦτο παρακαλῶ ὑπαρχθῆναί μοι τὴν σὴν βοήθειαν κ̣αὶ εὐδοκῆσαί σ̣ε τοῦ ῥύσασθαί με, ὅτι "πτωχὸς καὶ πένης εἰμί". οὐ δύναμαι ἐμαυτῷ ἐπαμύνειν, οὐ δύναμαι ἔξωθεν ἐμαυτὸν τῶν ἐπικειμένων ποιῆσαι, εἰ μὴ σὺ βοηθήσῃς. "πτωχὸς" οὖν "εἰμι καὶ πένης". διαφορὰ δὲ τούτων καὶ ἄλλοτε εἴρηται. 18 βοηθός μου καὶ ὑπερασπιστής εἶ μου σὺ εἶ· ὁ θεός μου, μὴ χρονίσῃς. ἐπεὶ σὲ βοηθὸν ἐπεκαλεσάμην καὶ ὑπερασπιστὴν προβάλλ̣οντα ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ τὴν ἀσπίδα σου–α̣ὑ´̣τη δέ ἐστιν ἡ ἀλήθεια· "ὅπλῳ" γὰρ "κυκλώσει σε ἡ ἀλήθεια αὐτοῦ"–, "μὴ χρονίσῃς", μὴ ὑπὲρ δύναμιν ὁ ἀγών μοι γένηται. ὅτ̣ε οἶδας καίριον εἶναι ἐπινεῦσαι καὶ βοηθῆσαι καὶ ῥύσασθαι, τοῦτο γενέσθω· ὁ´̣σον γὰρ ἧκεν ε̣ἰς τὴν ἐμὴν δύναμιν καὶ τὴν φύσιν, ἀσθενής εἰμι ἐμαυτῷ βοηθῆσαι, ἔξω ἐμαυτὸν ποιῆσαι τῶν ἐπικειμένων κακῶν. 290 1–2 Εἰς τὸ τέλος· ψαλμὸς τῷ ∆αυίδ. μακάριος ὁ συνίων ἐπὶ πτωχὸν καὶ πένητα. καὶ τοῦτον τὸν ψαλμὸν ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ σωτῆρος ἐκλα̣μβάνουσιν πολλοὶ διὰ τ̣ὸ κ̣εῖσθαι ὧδε ῥητὰ λημφθέντα ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ ὡς ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος εἰρημμένα καὶ περὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος πραχθέντα καὶ θεωρηθέντα. "μακάριος", φησίν, "ὁ συνίων ἐπὶ πτωχὸν καὶ πένητα". καὶ πρὸς τὸ ἦθος ἐξηγ̣ήσαντο πολλοὶ τοιαῦτα ὅτι· διάφοροί εἰσιν οἱ πενόμενοι καὶ οἱ πτωχοί· καὶ ὁ τούτοις κοινωνῶν ὀφείλει κατὰ ἀναλογίαν τὴν κοινωνία̣ν π̣οιεῖν· τότε γὰρ συνετῶς ποιεῖ. οὐ πάντα ἀποροῦντα τροφῆς δεῖ τρέφειν. οὐκ ἔστιν δὲ ἀπορῶν τροφῆς διὰ τὸ ἀσώτως πρότερον ἐζηκέναι–μέθαις ἐσχόλασεν, πάντα ἃ εἶχεν ἀσέμνως καὶ φαυ´̣λως κατεδαπάνησεν–, ἄλλος δὲ ἢ διὰ νόσον μακρὰν ἢ διὰ πολυπαιδίαν. δεῖ οὖν μετὰ συνέσεως παρέχειν ἑκάστῳ. εἴ τις οὖν μὴ ἔχει πᾶσιν διδόναι, ἐκείνοις̣ οἷς ὀφείλει δοῦναι, μετὰ συνέσεως ὀφείλει τοῦτο ποιεῖν, εἰ δὲ δύναται, καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις οἰκτίρμων γινόμενος κατὰ τὸν ἐν τ̣οῖς οὐρανοῖς πατέρα, ἀνατέλλων οὐ μόνον ἐπὶ ἀγαθοὺς τὸν ἥλιον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπὶ πονηρούς ἀνατέλλων οὐ μόνον ἐπὶ ἀγαθοὺς τὸν ἥλιον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπὶ πονηρούς. ὅταν
english: Pay attention. For I ask you to be pleased to rescue [me], not for the sake of another, but so that you might attend to helping me. And help me, if you make [me] outside of those ruling wars.

Those seeking my soul were greatly ashamed and were simultaneously ensnared. They were saying that the Psalm is about a single person. But if the one speaking is a man, he sends up a prayer concerning both, both for the body and for the soul. Therefore, if 'the Son of Man'—the Temple who has come forth from Mary—says these things, we shall say to those saying that only the body was taken: 'But He said, "He shall keep my body"'—see, even this He says, and it is the same person who is announcing it. Those who know the truth are turned back and are ashamed.

Those wishing evil upon me turned back toward the rear and were ensnared. It is a great thing to have turned the evil toward the rear; for to continue onward is harmful. Therefore, 'turning toward the rear' means 'they turned back' so as not to increase the road, not to rush forward. May those saying to me, 'Well done, well done,' be immediately clothed in shame. There is a wish regarding what he says, 'immediately,' that they may not remain in the evil, that they may not unceasingly say, 'Well done, well done, well done.' To say 'well done, well done' mockingly when something unpleasant is happening to those suffering is [wrong].

May all those seeking you, O Lord, rejoice and be glad. Having spoken concerning the adversaries, so that they also might be ashamed and be ensnared and turn toward the rear, saying mockingly 'well done, well done,' he says: 'May all those seeking you, O Lord, rejoice and be glad.' Then we rejoice and are glad when, having sought, we find you; for he who seeks something rejoices and is glad when he finds it. Even if, therefore, troublesome or other harmful things come upon [us], we seek to find you as a help. Then, appearing to be a help, you say: 'I will say while you are still speaking: Behold, I am here.'

And let them say at all times: Let the Lord be magnified. Since, having found you, they give thanks, saying, 'Let them say at all times: Let the Lord be magnified,' they might have those things for which they owe praise and rejoicing. It is possible to 'say at all times'; may ingratitude never exist for them. Those who love your salvation. The justice...
salvation, or the cause becoming salvation to them, or about to become salvation. 'Let the Lord be magnified always, let them say.' Loving your salvation, they magnify God always because of it.

18 But I am poor and needy; the Lord cares for me. Therefore I pray that your help may come to me and that you may be pleased to rescue me, because 'I am poor and needy.' I am not able to encourage myself, I am not able to do for myself from the outside regarding the things lying ahead, unless you help. 'Poor' therefore 'I am, and needy.' The difference between these two has been said at other times.

18 You are my helper and my protector; you are my God, do not delay. Since I have called you as a helper and a protector putting forth your shield for me—and this is the truth; for 'truth shall surround you as a weapon' (Ps 5:12)—'do not delay,' lest the struggle become too much for my strength. When you know it is the right time to care, to help, and to rescue, let this happen; for as far as my power and my nature reach, I am weak to help myself, to do for myself regarding the impending evils.

290 1–2 To the end; a psalm of David. Blessed is he who shows compassion to the poor and needy. And many take this psalm from the person of the Savior because of the way words lying here are received in the Gospel as having been spoken by the Savior and having been done and seen concerning the Savior. 'Blessed,' he says, 'is he who shows compassion to the poor and needy.' And many have explained such things regarding the character of the act, saying: the needy and the poor are different; and he who shares with these ought, according to analogy, to practice sharing; for he acts with understanding. It is not necessary to feed all those who are in want. Nor is it the case of one lacking food because he previously sought it thoughtlessly—he indulged in drinking, and everything he had he consumed unseemly and foolishly—but rather [one lacking] because of sickness or because of much childhood dependency. It is therefore necessary to provide to each with understanding. If anyone does not have enough to give to all, he ought to do this with understanding to those to whom he is obligated to give; and if he is able, he should also become a benefactor to others, according to the Father in the heavens, who causes the sun to rise not only upon the good but also upon the evil (Matt 5:45).

κοινοῦ τὸ "ἐν τῇ γῇ" λάβε. 3 καὶ μὴ παραδῷ αὐτὸν εἰς χεῖρας ἐχθρῶν αὐτοῦ. οὐ παραδίδωσιν τὸν τοιοῦτον "εἰς χεῖρας ἐχθρῶν αὐτοῦ". πολλοὺς ἔχει ὁ τοιοῦτος ἐχθ̣ρούς, πολλοὺς ἐφεδρεύοντας ἔχει· ἐπεὶ γὰρ χειρὸς τῶν διωκ̣όντων ὁ ἐπιδιδόμενος αὐτοῖς. 4 κύριος βοηθήσει αὐτῷ ἐπὶ κλίνης ὀδύνης αὐτοῦ. ὧδε περὶ τοῦ πτωχοῦ λέγει· κἂν ἐπὶ κλίνης γένηται νοσῶν καὶ ὀδυνηρὸν ᾖν αὐτῷ τὸ τοιοῦτον, βοηθεῖ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός. ἔχε τὰ περὶ τῶν παραλυτικῶν ἐν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις εἰρημένα· ἐν κλίνῃ ὀδύνης ἔμεινεν ὁ τριάκοντα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἐνιαυτοὺς βεβλη̣μένος κλινήρης ὥστε μηδὲ σαλευθῆναι δύνασθαι μηδὲ διαναστῆναι. καὶ ἄλλοι δὲ Ὀχοδίας οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς κοίτης ἔπεσεν ἐκ τοῦ ὑπερῴου καὶ ἀπέθανεν. εἰ δὲ πρὸς ἀναγωγήν, τὸ σῶμα πολλάκις κλίνη ὀνομάζεται τῆς ψυχῆς. καὶ πολλαί εἰσιν γραφαὶ συναγορεύουσαι τῇ τοιαύτῃ θεωρίᾳ. ὅταν τις οὖν ἐν τῷ φθαρτῷ σώματι ᾖν καὶ τῷ γ̣ηΐνῳ σκήνει ὃ "βρίθει νοῦν πολυφρόντιδα, "ἐπὶ κλίνης ὀδύνης" ἐστίν· ἀλλ' ὅταν βοηθήσῃ αὐτῷ θεός, ποιει῀̣ αὐτὸν ὑπωπιάζειν τὸ σῶμα καὶ δουλαγωγεῖν, καὶ οὐκέτι ἐπὶ τοῦ σώματος βέβληται, ἀλλ' αὐτὸς λοιπὸν αἴρει τὸν κράβακτον̣ καὶ περιπατεῖ. τὸ σῶμα οὖν κλίνη ἐστίν. ὁ φιλήδονος, ὁ φιλοπαθής, ὁ τὰ τοῦ σώματος ἀποδεχόμενος καὶ πράττω̣ν ὀδυνᾶται ἐπὶ κλίνης, ἀλλὰ βοηθεῖ αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτὸν ὑγιῆν, ἵν' ὑγιὴς γενόμενος μηκέτι αὐτὸς ᾖν βεβλημ̣ε´̣νος ε᾿̣πὶ τη῀̣ς κ̣λίνη̣ς, ἀλλὰ αὐτὸς αὐτὴν βαστάζῃ, καὶ ὡς λέγουσιν οὕτως, ὅτι ὅταν ἄρχῃ ἡ ψυχὴ τοῦ σώματος. ἐπερ · ποῖοί ει᾿̣σιν ο̣ι῾̣ ε῾̣ξ̣ήκοντα δυν̣ατοί, οἵ εἰσιν ἐν εὐλογίᾳ παραλαμβανόμενοι, οἱ κύκλῳ τῆς στρωμνῆς; ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ἕως ἐννεακαίδεκα καὶ ἀπὸ . οὗτοι οὖν εἰσιν οἱ ἑξήκοντα δυνατοὶ οἱ περὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ
english: However, since one cannot satisfy everyone, let him do this with understanding. This can be understood regarding the Savior: for he 'became poor through us' [2 Cor 8:9] and not for the sake of another. 'He became poor through us' so that he might free us from poverty and turn us away from want. He says, 'the one who did not know sin, for our sake made sin' [2 Cor 5:21]—this is his poverty—'so that we might become the righteousness of God in him.' [Fragmentary text] It was asked... it was not sustained. Even if sin occurred, it was not so that sin might remain, but so that he might free the... 'You know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that being rich he became poor for us' [2 Cor 8:9]. And the paradox is this: 'being rich' he is poor, and this poverty makes us rich, for it is a creative poverty. He is not poor at all, but in relation to his wealth.

2 In a day of evil the Lord will deliver him. He delivered Jesus 'in a day of evil' [Matt 27:22-23], when those surrounding him were saying, 'Crucify, crucify him; we have no king but Caesar.' And it was also asked from that evil day, how he, having become sin, became a creator of righteousness. The name of understanding is taken for the sake of doing good to brothers in need; for the apostle says regarding an offering: 'Understand what I say; for God will give you understanding in all things' [1 Cor 12:8]. And understanding is the knowledge of things joined together and things not joined together. Joined things are those that are similar, those that are equal, when we bring one thing to another and find that it has identity either by similarity or by equality. The one, therefore, having understanding, knows which things are joined to which and which are not.

3 The Lord will preserve him and let him live and make him blessed in the land. This can be said of both: the Lord preserves the poor and the needy. For this reason he also led the one understanding into himself. Where has it ever been said: when you see a suffering person and one who has arrived suddenly under another pretext, look there for a physician; see that the word of the divine providence has touched the physician, a compassionate physician, so that, sympathizing with the sufferer, he might help him medically. But he blesses the poor and needy man and makes him live in the land, or the one understanding and having received understanding upon...

The poor and the needy. If you speak concerning the Savior, you protect him and provide for him to live; for even though 'he was crucified in weakness, but lives by the power of God' (Heb 13:3). Take 'in the earth' in a common sense.

And do not hand him over into the hands of his enemies. Such a person does not hand over 'into the hands of his enemies.' Such a person has many enemies, many who are attacking him; for he is a blessed man and has understanding toward the poor and the needy according to all the clarifications provided, and he has many [enemies] attacking him; for God will rescue him from their hands. But he who is given over to them is not rescued from the hand of those persecuting him.

The Lord will help him upon his bed of pain. Here, concerning the poor, he says: even if he should be upon a bed of sickness and such a thing should be painful to him, God helps him. Have the things said in the Gospels concerning the paralytics: one remained in a bed of pain for thirty-eight years, thrown down on a bed so as not to be able to be shaken or to rise up (John 5:5). And others like these were recorded in the Gospels as paralytics. But not everyone upon a bed of pain and sickness is rescued. For instance, one fell from the bed from on high and died.

But if toward a restoration, the body is often called the bed of the soul. And there are many scriptures gathered together for such a theory. When someone is in the corruptible body and dwells in the earth, he 'reaps a much-wise mind' (Job 4:7), [he] is 'upon a bed of pain'; but when God helps him, he makes him to lift up the body and to carry it away, and he is no longer thrown down upon the body, but he himself afterwards lifts up the bed and walks. The body, therefore, is a bed.

The lover of pleasure, the lover of passion, the one accepting and doing the things of the body, suffers upon a bed, but God helps him and makes him healthy, so that, having become healthy, he may no longer be thrown down upon the bed himself, but he himself may carry it, and as they say, so that the soul may begin of the body. What then are those sixty powerful ones, who are received in blessing, who are around the bed? From Abraham to nineteen and from... these, therefore, are the sixty powerful ones concerning the body of...

"ἐγὼ" οὖν τοῦτο "εἶπα Κύριε, ἐλε´̣ησον". διὰ τοῦ εἰπεῖν· "κύριε, ἐλέησόν με", ἔδειξα ὅτι ἐμαυτῷ οὐκ ἠδυνάμην ἐλεηθῆναι. 5 ἴασαι τὴν ψυχήν μου, ὅτι ἥμαρτόν σοι. σοὶ ἥμαρτον. οὕτω πλησίον σχεδὸν πάντες ἁμαρτάνομεν εἰς θεὸν πολλὰ ἀγνοο̣ῦντες τῶν περὶ αὐτοῦ, πολλὰ παρο ρῶντες τῶν κατὰ τοὺς νόμους αὐτοῦ δεῖ ποιεῖν. "ἥμαρτον" οὖν "σοι", ἀλλὰ ε̣ἰπὼν "Κύριε, ἐλέησόν με", ἔσ̣χ̣ο̣ν τὸ τῆς αἰτήσεως. 6 οἱ ἐχθροί μου εἶπον κακά μοι Πότε ἀποθανεῖται, καὶ ἀπολεῖται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ; ἔλεγον τὸν ψαλμὸν τοῦτον ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ σωτῆρος κατὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον λέγεσθαι. καὶ ἐπεὶ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ γεγόνασιν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι οἷον προδόται τῆς ἀληθείας, οἱ μὴ νοήσαντε̣ς τὸν ἐπιδημήσαντα, γέγονεν δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν μαθητῶν ὑπάρχων, περὶ τῶν ἐχθρῶν λέγει τῶν κατ' αὐτοῦ ἐπεληλυθότων ὁτὲ μὲν ἑνικῶς εἰς τὸν Ἰούδα ἀνάγων τὸν λόγον τὸν ἔξαρχον τῆς προδοσίας, ὁτὲ δὲ πληθυν̣τικῶς διὰ τοὺς ἀκολουθοῦντας αὐτῷ καὶ ἀναιρήσαντας τὸν Ἰησοῦν. οὐκ ἐνταῦθα δὲ μόνον τοῦτο γίνεται, ἀλλὰ κ̣αὶ ἐν τῷ ἑκατοστῷ ὀγδόῳ ψαλμῷ λέγεται· "ἐλάλησαν κατ' ἐμοῦ γλώσσῃ δολίᾳ καὶ λόγοις μίσους ἐκύκλωσάν με. ἀντὶ τοῦ ἀγαπᾶν με ἐνδιέβαλλόν με, ἐγὼ δὲ προσηυχόμην· καὶ ἔθεντο κατ' ἐμοῦ κακὰ ἀντὶ ἀγαθῶν καὶ μῖσος ἀντὶ τῆς ἀγαπήσεώς μου. κατάστησον ἐπ' αὐτὸν ἁμαρτωλόν, καὶ διάβολος στήτω ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ"– τοῦτο ἑνικῶς περὶ Ἰούδα λέγει–· "ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαι αὐτὸν ἐξέλθοι καταδεδικασμένος, καὶ τὴν ἐπισκοπὴν αὐτοῦ λαβέτω ἕτερος". ὁτὲ μὲν οὖν περὶ τοῦ Ἰούδα, ὁτὲ δὲ περὶ τῶν ὁμοφρονησάντων αὐτῷ λε´̣γει, κ̣αὶ διὰ το̣ῦτο ἐν τοῖς αὐτοῖς στίχοις ὅπου μὲν ἑνικῶς, ὅπου δὲ πληθυντικῶς. καὶ ὧδε οὖν λέγει· "οἱ ἐχθροί μου εἶπον". τοῦτο εἴρηκαν· τ̣ὰ κακά, ἃ νομίζουσιν κακά, κατ' ἐμοῦ εἶπον· "πότε ἀποθανεῖται, καὶ ἀπολεῖται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ"; ἐνόμισαν γάρ, ὅτι ἀποθανόντος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ σβέννυται αὐτοῦ ἡ διδασκαλία καὶ ἡ περὶ αὐτοῦ φήμη, κα̣ὶ ἐ´̣λεγον· "πότε ἀποθανεῖται"; τοὐναντίον δὲ ἀπέβη ᾧ ἐνόμισαν. οὐχ οὕτως τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ διέλαμψεν ὅτε ἔζη καὶ ἐν βίῳ ἦν ὡς ὅτε ἐσταυρώθη καὶ ἀνελήμφθη. πρὸς δὲ ἀναγωγὴν περὶ ετερ τῶν ἑτεροδόξων τοῦτο λημπτέον· ὅσοι γὰρ οὐκ ὀρθῶς φρονοῦσιν, ἀλλὰ ἀπατώμενα καὶ ἀσεβῆ λέγουσιν περὶ τοῦ σωτῆρο̣ς, ἐκεῖνοι εἶπον κατ' αὐτοῦ κακά. καὶ ἐπειδὴ ἔστιν τις ἔξαρχος τῶν αἱρέσεων, ὁ ψευδοσλόγος ἢ καὶ ὁ ὑποβολε̣ὺς αὐτο̣ῦ διάβολος, διὰ
english: Having served the Savior by his birth. It must be said thus: the world came into being in six days, and sixty is a perfect number, as it has been often demonstrated; for in tens, sixty-six is [present]. Therefore, he who surpassed the world and having gone above is able, being a 'man trained for war' (Ps 45:3), having a sword 'upon his thigh' (Ps 45:3). Concerning the bed of Solomon, these sixty are able, concerning the Lord's body, circling it, observing, by what cause the Savior was incarnated. 'Sixty' therefore [are] 'able around it, all holding a sword'. They are swords. And the swords which the wise hold are swords. 'The righteous shall rejoice in glory and shall exult in their throat' (Ps 97:11), 'and a two-edged sword in their hands' (Ps 45:3). They have two-edged swords in their hands. And they also have [it] 'upon the thigh'.

And since the drama concerning the marriage of the bride and bridegroom is a bridal chamber, he says the temperate ones concerning the bridegroom, to show, and he says that they have a sword upon the thigh, cutting away shameful desires. 'You turned his whole bed in his sickness' (Job 33:25). This says: he did not give a brief healing to the one greatly sickened, but 'turned his whole bed' (Job 33:25) away from the sickness, so that he might no longer be sick, but might be healthy, as I said concerning the paralytic. And you also say concerning Lazarus, the one being drawn out having a body, that, when he was taken up from thence by the angels, his whole bed was turned, his whole sickness. He was no longer laid down in sickness. Instead, he was being carried into the bosom of Abraham.

'I said, Lord, have mercy on me' (Ps 51:3). Instead, he says that: what was upon us was achieved, to be rescued from the bed of sickness and to be helped from the bed of pain; for I did this, 'I said, Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, for I have sinned against you' (Ps 51:3). You see that, when he sinned, then he was in [trouble] and then he was laid upon a bed and a couch. When therefore anyone knows Him who is able to rescue, he will attain to the one who is striving, similarly to him: 'I want, be cleansed' (Mark 1:41), 'Rise, take up your bed and walk' (Mark 2:11). 'I' therefore 'said, Lord, have mercy' (Ps 51:3). By saying: 'Lord, have mercy on me', I showed that I was not able to be pitied by myself. I healed.

I have sinned against you, I have sinned against you. In this way, almost all of us sin toward God, knowing much about Him through ignorance and doing much contrary to His laws. 'I have sinned' is thus 'against you'; but having said, 'Lord, have mercy on me,' he possesses the petition.

My enemies said evil things to me: 'When will he die, and will his name be destroyed?' (Ps 54:1). I say that this psalm is to be spoken from the person of the Savior according to man. And since the Jews have become His enemies, like traitors to the truth, having not understood the one who came among them, and since Judas also became one of the disciples, regarding the enemies he speaks singularly of those having risen up against him—once in reference to Judas as the beginning of the betrayal, and once plurally because of those following him and having overthrown Jesus.

And it is not only here that this happens, but also in the 108th psalm it is said: 'They spoke against me with a deceitful tongue, and with words of hatred they surrounded me. Instead of loving me, they attacked me, but I was praying; and they set evil against me instead of good, and hatred instead of my love. Set the sinner upon him, and let the devil stand at his right hand' (Ps 108:2-5)—this he says singularly concerning Judas—'in the judging of him, let him go out condemned, and let another take his oversight' (Ps 108:8). Once therefore concerning Judas, and once concerning those who agreed with him, he speaks; and for this reason in the same verses where there is singular, there is plural.

And thus he says: 'My enemies said.' This they said: the evil things which they think are evil, they said against me: 'When will he die, and will his name be destroyed?' (Ps 54:1). For they thought that after the death of Jesus his teaching and his fame would be extinguished, and they said: 'When will he die?' On the contrary, it went the opposite of what they thought. His name did not shine forth less when he lived and was alive than when he was crucified and taken up. And for the correction of those of heterodox opinion, this is to be taken: for as many as do not think rightly, but are being deceived and say impious things concerning the Savior, they are the ones who spoke evil against him.
